Owners with an escrow account should pass the bill to the servicer, because a lender cannot pay a bill it never received. Missing the city date is the easy mistake here: the county bill's November 1 credit and the city's November 30 credit are different so check which date applies to which bill. City commissioners vote the city rate each year on the finance director's advice, and Frankfort Independent Schools sets the old city school rate.

Franklin County housing and the buyer pool

Franklin County is the seat of state government and is more urban than most of Kentucky. Two school systems share the area. Franklin County Public Schools covers nearly all of it, including most of Frankfort, while Frankfort Independent Schools covers downtown, South Frankfort around the Capitol, and Bellepoint. Population is 52,649. Sellers should expect buyers to ask about both bills, since the city charge is extra for any house inside the limits.

The typical house value is $216,600. Owners live in 64.5 percent of homes, which leaves a large rental share. There are 24,404 housing units, median gross rent is $967, and 96 permits for new homes were issued in 2025. With the state workforce nearby, sellers in Frankfort draw from a deeper buyer pool than most Kentucky counties offer, and tax bills run larger in dollars. A seller carrying a tax balance should collect payoff figures from both billing offices before picking a closing date.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Franklin County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How to appeal your assessment

Meet the PVA first, because the state will not take an appeal from an owner who skipped the conference. The roll is posted for 13 days beginning in the first week of May, and the PVA has to advertise that period in the county's largest newspaper.

Next, file at the county clerk's office by the end of the following business day. A local board of assessment appeals then hears cases roughly four or five weeks later. It listens only to evidence offered with you and the PVA both present, so bring comparable sales, a recent appraisal, repair estimates or insurance records. You may audio-record the hearing, and the board owes you a written explanation of any change. If bills have already printed when the board raises a value, a supplemental bill makes up the gap.

Steps to take before you list

A Frankfort sale involves two tax accounts, so a short checklist saves time.

  • Find out whether the house is inside the city limits. If it is, expect a county bill and a city bill, and ask whether the city bill also carries the school charge.
  • Call the sheriff at (502) 875-8740 and, for a city address, the Finance Office at (502) 875-8500. Ask what is owed and what has already been paid this year.
  • Keep the paid receipts. The buyer's title company will ask for both.
  • If you claim the homestead exemption, tell the PVA at (502) 875-8780 once the sale is final so the exemption does not stay attached to your old address.

Bring the deed or a recent bill to any of these offices. It carries the parcel details staff need to pull your account without delay.

Homestead exemption

Seniors and totally disabled owners qualify, as long as the house is their home. The state exemption is $49,100 in 2025 and 2026, deducted from assessed value before tax is calculated.

File with the Franklin County PVA. Ask that office how the January 1 ownership date applies if you buy or sell partway through a year, and tell it about any sale so the exemption comes off the old address.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Franklin County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling with unpaid Franklin County taxes

The tax follows the parcel to the closing table. KRS 134.015 treats the tax as the owner's personal debt from the assessment date, and a delinquency lien survives a change of ownership.

Open bills pass from the sheriff to the county clerk on April 15. From then on 1 percent interest accrues every month, the clerk takes a 10 percent commission, and a county attorney commission of 20 percent applies after the first notice goes out. The county attorney mails notices before any sale, which must fall between 90 and 135 days after the transfer.

  • Ask the sheriff for a payoff at (502) 875-8740, and the city Finance Office at (502) 875-8500 if the house is in Frankfort.
  • Have the title company pay both bills from your proceeds so the policy issues clean.
  • A buyer that purchases as-is and closes quickly can take over a house with arrears and repairs without a listing period.

Because the county and the city keep separate records, a change of address filed with one does not reach the other. After closing, tell the PVA the buyer's name and mailing address, and tell the city Finance Office too if the house is inside Frankfort. That way the next county and city bills reach the new owner instead of coming back to you.

Frequently asked questions

Do Frankfort homeowners pay the city and the county?

Yes. They receive a county bill collected by the sheriff and a city bill collected by the Finance Office, which also collects for Frankfort Independent Schools.

Where is the Franklin County sheriff's tax office?

It is at 974 River Bend Road, Frankfort, KY 40601, and the phone is (502) 875-8740. Bills can also be searched and paid on the sheriff's website.

Where is the Franklin County PVA?

It is at 313 West Main Street, 2nd Floor, Room 209, Frankfort, KY 40601. The phone is (502) 875-8780, and weekday hours are 8:00 to 4:30.

How big is the Franklin County homestead exemption?

It is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026. Seniors and totally disabled owners apply through the PVA, and the amount is subtracted from the assessed value.

How soon after April 15 can Franklin County hold a tax sale?

The sale must fall between 90 and 135 days after the sheriff transfers the bills to the clerk, and the county attorney mails notices beforehand.

Hardin County market context

Hardin County had 113,482 residents in the July 2025 estimate, up 2.5 percent from 2020. Elizabethtown is both the seat and the biggest city, and Fort Knox shapes the local economy. The county has 51,149 housing units, 432 building permits were issued in 2025, and 62.6 percent of homes are occupied by their owners. The market is deep enough that a conference with the assessor can lean on recent sales near your street.

Two school districts matter for a tax bill. Hardin County Schools covers most of the county, and Elizabethtown Independent Schools serves most of the city of Elizabethtown. Each district sets its own rate.

Offices that bill, assess and collect

Everything runs through the government building on North Provident Way in Elizabethtown.

  • Sheriff's Office, tax department: Suite 101, 150 North Provident Way, Elizabethtown, KY 42701. Phone 270-765-5133 and pick option 1.
  • PVA (the assessor): 270-765-2129. Its website has a parcel search, a tax estimator and an exemption page.

  • Planning and Development Commission: Suite 225, 270-769-5479, open weekdays from 8 in the morning to 4:30 in the afternoon for building permits outside city limits.

Two cities bill part of the tax themselves. A tax district code of 03 on your bill means the City of Radcliff (270-351-4714), and 06 means the City of Vine Grove (270-877-2422).

Fall 2026 due dates

The sheriff posted dates for bills due beginning November 1, 2026, which cover the assessment as of January 1, 2026. The discount period is longer than the date written into KRS 134.015.

  • Discount: November 1 through November 30, 2026.
  • Face amount: December 1 through December 31, 2026.
  • 5 percent penalty: January 1 through January 31, 2027.
  • 21 percent penalty: February 1 through April 15, 2027.

A current-year bill has to be paid whole. A single payment can cover several bills when copies are attached, and a stamped, self-addressed envelope brings back a receipt. Paying by card, online or at the counter, adds 2.49 percent. A taxpayer with no bill by early November can call and a duplicate goes out, or print one from the sheriff's tax bill search.

2026 real estate tax rates

Commercial and telecommunication property in the Industrial Taxing District (District 00) carries an extra ten cents under a 2023 ordinance. Timberland Fire Protection charges 2 cents per acre.

How to appeal your assessment

The PVA publishes the inspection dates in the News-Enterprise each year and prints them on assessment notices. The window opens the first Monday in May and stays open thirteen days. Hold your conference with the PVA before or during that time.

When the conference settles things, you are finished. When it does not, hand the appeal form to the County Clerk, who sets a hearing before the county board. A further appeal goes to the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals.

Collect sale prices from your own neighborhood first. In the Elizabethtown Independent district each dollar of assessed value carries a higher rate, so a successful appeal saves more there than in the county school district.

Homestead exemption

Owners aged 65 and up, and owners totally disabled, who live in the house can apply at the PVA. The PVA's rate page lists the homestead and disability amount at $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, after $46,350 for 2023 and 2024.

That figure comes off the assessed value, so the saving depends on your rate. Questions go to the PVA at 270-765-2129. A buyer has to apply separately after closing, because the exemption belongs to the owner.

Who pays the bill at closing?

The bill is for a calendar year and goes to the person who owned the property on January 1. A closing agent or attorney usually works out each side's share, then either pays the sheriff at the table or gives one party a credit on the settlement statement and leaves the payment to them.

The sheriff will not take a pro-rated payment, so one or both parties must send the full amount. After a transfer, bills normally go in care of the new owner, though a sale near the print date may miss the update. If a bill reaches your old address, forward it to the buyer.

Steps for a seller

Start with the tax district code on your bill, since it tells you whether the county school rate, the Elizabethtown Independent rate or a city bill applies. Next, confirm with the sheriff that the current year is paid, or agree with the buyer on who will pay it. Call the clerk if any earlier year shows up as delinquent.

If you hold the homestead exemption, tell the PVA about the sale. Make sure the deed lists a mailing address for the new owner's bill. Then ask the closing agent to show the tax split on the settlement statement, so nobody pays the full year twice. A seller who has tax and repair worries at once may find a quick cash sale simpler than a listing, though the payoff still comes out of the proceeds.

Permits before a listing

The Planning and Development Commission, created by the fiscal court in 1979, serves unincorporated Hardin County, including Glendale, Cecilia, Rineyville, Stephensburg and Colesburg. A building permit application needs an aerial photo of the property showing the structure and its distance from each property line. Sellers who built a deck, shed or addition without a permit can ask the commission's office whether it is on file before a buyer's inspector asks.

Houses inside Elizabethtown, Radcliff and the other cities are handled by those cities' offices.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

If a bill goes delinquent

When April 15 passes, unpaid bills move to the County Clerk. Call 270-765-2171 for the figure. Interest builds monthly, clerk and attorney commissions are added, and the clerk's website carries a delinquent tax calculator and tax sale information.

An owner with back taxes can still close, because the title company pays the certificate out of the proceeds. Owners who would rather skip repairs and a listing can ask a cash buyer for an offer and compare it with the payoff.

Frequently asked questions

What is the discount period on Hardin County bills for 2026?

The sheriff lists November 1 through November 30, 2026. Face amount runs December 1 through 31, and penalties begin in January 2027.

Can I pay a Hardin County bill in installments?

No. Current-year bills cannot be paid in part. One check may cover several bills if a copy of each is attached.

What does a card payment cost in Hardin County?

2.49 percent of the bill, online or at the sheriff's office. A mailed check to 150 North Provident Way, Suite 101, avoids the fee.

Whom do I call for a payoff on an old Hardin County bill?

The County Clerk at 270-765-2171. Delinquent prior-year bills are held there, and the clerk's website has a calculator.

Which Hardin County cities charge their own tax?

The 2026 schedule lists Elizabethtown, Radcliff, Sonora, Upton, Vine Grove and West Point. For districts 03 and 06 the sheriff points payers to Radcliff and Vine Grove for the separate city bill.

Who to call about a Madison County tax bill

Three Richmond offices split the work. The sheriff answers for the bill, the PVA answers for the value behind it, and the County Clerk answers for deeds and for overdue bills.

  • Sheriff: 135 W Irvine, Suite B01, Richmond, reached at 859-623-1511. Bills can be searched and paid through a secure portal, at the counter, or by post, and cash should never go in an envelope.
  • PVA: appraisals and exemption paperwork, at 859-623-5410.
  • Clerk: deeds are filed at the Richmond Branch, 321 N. Madison Ave. The Berea branch at 304 Chestnut Street serves vehicle and marriage license customers.

An heir or agent can settle a bill ahead of a sale too, because KRS 134.119 lets the sheriff accept money from a third party for the owner.

Housing and land in Madison County

Madison County is a college county that has been adding residents for decades. Eastern Kentucky University is in Richmond and Berea College is in Berea, the county's only two cities. Population was 82,916 in 2010 and 92,701 in 2020, and the July 2025 estimate is 101,696, a gain of 9.7 percent over April 2020.

The county has 42,389 housing units. Owners live in 62.0 percent of homes, the typical owner-occupied home is worth $232,000, and typical gross rent is $889. Roughly 36 percent of residents were rural at the 2020 census, so plenty of sellers own land around Kingston, Waco or Speedwell rather than inside a city.

Appraisal of a farm follows what its soil earns, and a subdivision developer's offer plays no part. That is the rule in Section 172A of the state constitution. Ask the PVA to show how each of your acres is classified before you price a farm.

Due dates and penalties

Trust the periods shown on your own bill or in the portal. The ordinary timetable sits in KRS 134.015.

Typical Kentucky payment stages

A late-printed bill gets a compressed schedule from the Department of Revenue, counted from the mailing date. Fees pile onto delinquent bills, and one percent interest per month starts after the transfer to the clerk.

The Clerk's website carries the delinquent county property tax list and a third-party purchaser page. Search for your parcel before you list. The County Attorney's office also runs delinquent collection, and an installment agreement signed before the Clerk's sale keeps a bill from being bought by an investor. Its number is 624-4777, extension 9.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Madison County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How to dispute your valuation

A sit-down with the PVA comes first. When it settles nothing, you file a petition at the Clerk's office and the county board takes the case, as laid out in KRS 133.120. Carry sales data, an appraisal or insurance records, and keep paying on your own number during the dispute.

Close to either campus, nearby recent sales of similar houses make the strongest comparables. On acreage, ask which agricultural class the PVA applied. KRS 133.030 has the board meet between 25 and 35 days following inspection.

Senior and disability homestead exemption

Madison County offers one. The deduction for 2025 and 2026 is $49,100 off the assessed value. It is open to owner-occupants who are 65 or older or classified as totally disabled, and the Madison County PVA takes the application. A buyer who qualifies files separately after closing.

Steps to take before you list

A short checklist keeps a tax question from surfacing at the closing table. Work through it in order and you will know your exact position before a buyer does.

  • Search your parcel on the sheriff's portal and note whether the current bill is paid.
  • Check the Clerk's delinquent list for earlier years, and call the Clerk's office if your parcel appears.
  • Ask the PVA how your property is classified and whether an exemption is on file in your name.
  • Request a written payoff from each office that holds a balance, and ask how long each figure stays good.
  • Give those letters to the title agent so the amounts come out of your proceeds at the closing.

If you inherited the house, confirm whose name the tax roll shows. If the roll still carries the prior owner, the bill goes to that name, so ask the PVA about a name and address change before you list. A buyer's title examiner will find an open lien no matter who is named on the roll, so settle it early rather than at the last minute.

Keep copies of every payment receipt and every letter you receive from the sheriff, PVA or Clerk. If a bill is missed during a closing, the sheriff's office carries no responsibility, so the paper trail protects you. Mortgage servicers are not sent a copy of the bill, so a homeowner with a loan should hand each bill to the lender on time.

Cash buyers often move faster than the offices do. Tax payoffs, a recorded deed and a notarized price certificate each take their own turn at a counter, so start gathering them as soon as you accept an offer.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Madison County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Before a Madison County closing

Get a payoff figure from the sheriff for this year's bill and scan the clerk's delinquent list for earlier years. Property taxes are commonly prorated between buyer and seller, with the current owner answerable for payment, so check how your settlement statement divides the bill.

A tax lien can ride with the land for as long as eleven years under KRS 134.015(5), which is why title agents ask for payoff at the table.

Deeds go to the Clerk's Richmond Branch at (859) 624-4703, extension 3. The office keeps papers from 1786 onward, searchable by a person's name only, and has scanned everything since 1986 for viewing in person or through the paid ECCLIX service. Electronic filings are handled each morning until roughly 10:00. Owners can also enroll in DocAlert, a free notification that fires whenever a document is recorded under their name or property details.

The state's transfer tax is fifty cents for each $500 of value under KRS 142.050, paid when the deed is filed. Ask the closing agent to show it on the settlement statement, and bring a photo ID to any counter where you sign or pay. Call ahead to the Clerk's recordings desk to confirm what the office will accept for payment that day. If you plan a cash sale, line up the payoff letters and the signed deed early so the closing is not delayed by a tax or recording question.

Frequently asked questions

Can Madison County property tax be paid online?

Yes, through the sheriff's secure portal, which also lets you search bills. The portal displays any processing fee before you confirm, and paying at the Richmond office or by mail still works.

How large is the 2026 exemption for Madison County seniors?

It is $49,100, the same as for 2025. Owners 65 or older, or totally disabled, apply through the PVA.

Which Madison County office records a deed?

The Clerk's Richmond Branch at 321 N. Madison Ave. Call (859) 624-4703, extension 3, for the recordings desk.

Is there help when a Madison County bill has gone delinquent?

The County Attorney's delinquent tax program, at 624-4777 extension 9, can arrange installment payments if you sign before the Clerk's sale.

Who pays the Madison County tax bill when a house changes owners mid-year?

The current owner must make sure it is paid, and bills are commonly prorated at closing. Confirm the split with your closing agent.

Who handles a Laurel County tax bill

Three offices in and around London split the job. Valuation sits with the PVA, payment with the sheriff, and leftovers with the clerk. Calling the wrong one costs a seller time, so here is who does what.

  • Property Valuation Administrator (PVA): Room 127 at 101 S. Main St. Call (606) 864-2889. The office closes at 4:30 Monday through Friday, and its website runs parcel searches by street address, owner name or parcel number.
  • Sheriff: 1380 East Hwy 192. Call 606-864-6600. Counter service ends at 4:00 on weekdays, and Saturday and Sunday are closed.
  • County Clerk: Room 203 at the same Main Street address, phone (606) 864-5158. The clerk receives delinquent bills and runs the sale of the liens.

The rate differs by taxing district, so get the figure for your own parcel from the sheriff or the PVA.

Laurel County housing at a glance

London is the seat, and Corbin lies mostly across the border in Whitley County. The county had an estimated 63,746 residents in July 2025, up from 62,613 in 2020. It has 27,063 housing units and 23,996 households, and 71.6 percent are owned by their occupants. The middle home value is $159,500. Owners with a mortgage have a median monthly cost of $1,239, and owners without one pay $382. About 19.1 percent of residents are 65 or older, which is the group the homestead exemption below serves.

Payment dates and penalties

The assessment date is New Year's Day, and the tax for that year is due at the sheriff's office before December 31 ends. KRS 134.015 turns the calendar into money.

  • Anyone who clears the full amount by November 1 pays 2 percent less.
  • November 2 through December 31 means paying the printed total.
  • January adds 5 percent on top.
  • From February, the add-on is 10 percent.

If bills are late getting out, the state can swap in a shifted timetable with a discount month followed by a face-value month. The sheriff accepts payment three ways: walk in, mail a check, or leave one in the box on the building's front. Cards work at the office only. Cash does not belong in either the mail or the box, and a mailed receipt needs an envelope you have addressed and stamped.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Laurel County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How to appeal your assessment

Start by talking to the PVA or a deputy, since the local board will not hear an owner who skipped that step. Each May the roll of real property is open for public viewing, starting on the first Monday and lasting thirteen days with Saturdays included. The clerk's office accepts the written appeal until closing time on the first workday after the viewing days end.

The board convenes about a month after viewing ends. Useful proof includes comparable sales, an insurance policy, construction costs, or a description of the lot. Appeals that arrive without documents get denied, and a no-show at the hearing forfeits any later claim to the Kentucky Claims Commission. A bill printed before the dispute ends uses the owner's number, and the board's higher value would trigger a supplemental bill.

Homestead exemption

For 2025 and 2026 the exemption is $49,100 of assessed value. Eligible owners are at least 65 years old or classified as totally disabled. With so many older residents, a share of Laurel County sellers may have it on file already.

Applications are filed at the PVA's Room 127 office, along with documents showing age or disability. A claim based on disability is renewed yearly, except for owners with a service connected disability and owners whom Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems has already ruled permanently and totally disabled. Ask the PVA how the exemption is treated after the house is sold.

What a delinquent bill turns into

On April 15 the sheriff's collection season ends. Open bills pass to the clerk, who files a lien and calls each a certificate of delinquency. A 1 percent monthly interest charge starts, and even a few days into a month counts as the whole month. The state's sample bill is $1,000. At the handoff it stands at $1,254 on an assumed 4 percent sheriff commission, and every later step adds interest plus commissions for the clerk and county attorney.

Once listed in the June newspaper$1,659.90$405.90
Taken over by a buyer at the sale$1,704.21$450.21

The county attorney mails a first notice within 30 days of the transfer and a second within 60 days, and the second names the sale date. The clerk sets the sale 90 to 135 days after the transfer, and an outside buyer of the certificate can add hefty fees of its own. Buyers register with the clerk ahead of the sale and post a deposit of 25 percent of their list value. KRS 134.015 lets that lien last eleven years, whoever holds title.

Tax steps to finish before listing

  • Get a statement from the sheriff showing this year's bill and any older year still open.
  • Ask the clerk's delinquent tax staff whether a certificate already exists against the parcel.
  • Check the PVA website to confirm owner name, parcel number and assessed value.
  • Use the bill search links on the sheriff's website to pull the parcel's tax history, and bring the printout to the listing appointment.
  • If you hold the homestead exemption, ask the PVA what happens to it at the sale.
  • Spell out in the contract how this year's bill is divided so each side's share is clear to the closing agent.

A seller who prefers to avoid repairs can request a direct cash offer. Any balance due is deducted from the proceeds.

Splitting the bill at closing

The tax year runs from January 1, and the bill is assessed to whoever owns the parcel on that date. If you sell in the spring, the bill that arrives in the fall may still carry your name. The closing agent normally prorates the year between you and the buyer on the settlement statement, then pays the sheriff from the proceeds.

Bring the agent the latest bill and your sheriff statement so the proration starts from real figures, not guesses. If the clerk shows a certificate against the parcel, the payoff comes out of your side of the closing before you get paid. A cash sale handles all of this the same way, but without waiting for a buyer's lender to order its own tax search.

Frequently asked questions

Where does a Laurel County owner pay the tax bill?

At the sheriff's office, 1380 East Hwy 192, London. Payment is accepted at the counter with a card, by mailed check and at the drop box outside.

How big is the early payment discount in Laurel County?

Two percent off the bill, if the sheriff has full payment by November 1. From the next day through December the printed amount stands.

Which office handles a disagreement over value?

Start with the PVA's office at (606) 864-2889, because a meeting there is required before any appeal.

How much does the Kentucky homestead exemption take off?

Qualifying owners lose $49,100 of assessed value, and applications go to the PVA.

Does a tax lien stay with the property after a sale?

Yes. The lien under KRS 134.015 can run eleven years regardless of ownership, so a buyer's title agent looks for it.

Barren County, KY Property Tax Guide: Offices, Appeals and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Kentucky

How Barren County property tax is set and collected

Barren County divides the job three ways. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) puts a value on each parcel, and rates come from the fiscal court and other taxing districts. The Barren County Sheriff mails the bills and takes payment from November through April. A disagreement about value goes to the PVA, and a payment question goes to the sheriff.

Glasgow is the seat and the largest city, joined by Cave City and Park City. Interstate 65 clips the northwest corner, and the Cave City interchange feeds traffic to Mammoth Cave National Park, so lodging and tourism shape part of the tax base there while farming and Glasgow's factories carry the rest.

When and how to pay the sheriff

The office takes payments from November until April each year. Bring your bill so the payment lands on the right account. Kentucky's standard calendar gives a 2 percent discount through November 1, and penalties begin after December 31.

Payment options are the sheriff's counter, the mail (send the top portion of the bill with it) and the online portal. The portal charges $1.50 per bank ACH payment and roughly 2.75 percent on cards. A stamped return envelope inside gets you a mailed receipt. Knowing which bills exist is the taxpayer's job, a point that matters for rentals, second parcels and mobile homes.

Calendars can shift in years when bills run late, so ask the office for the discount deadline that applies to your bill.

Disputing an assessment

No appeal can start until you have spoken with the PVA. When you and the PVA can't agree during the inspection window, the next step is a filing at the clerk's office on the business day after the window closes, which puts the dispute before the county board of assessment appeals.

The three-member board sits 25 to 35 days after inspection ends, and it must deny an appeal where the owner offers no facts. Gather recent sales of comparable houses close to yours, and at the conference ask to see which sales the PVA relied on. The result arrives by certified letter, with the steps for a further appeal.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Barren County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Barren County home values

Home prices here are modest, as are incomes. Half of owner-occupied homes are worth more than $178,000, and a lower price means a smaller tax bill in dollars but also a thinner margin when back taxes, repairs and a loan payoff all come out of one sale price.

Barren County housing and income
MeasureBarren County
Population, 2020 census44,485
Population estimate, July 202545,641
Housing units, July 202520,957
Owner-occupied rate, 2020 to 202465.2%
Median owner-occupied home value$178,000
Median gross rent$796
Median household income$50,628
Building permits, 2025204

Homestead exemption

The house must be your home, and you must be 65 or older or totally disabled. Use the state form, file it with the Barren County PVA, and the approved amount is subtracted from assessed value.

KRS 132.810 treats a mobile home or manufactured house as a residential unit, which matters in a county this rural. The dollar figure moves with the cost of living every two years, so ask the PVA what applies to your year. After a sale, the owner or an executor tells the PVA about the transfer, and whoever buys the house applies fresh.

If a Barren County tax bill goes unpaid

The sheriff's role stops after April 15, and the bill moves to the county clerk, who records a lien. Monthly interest of 1 percent starts, and the clerk and county attorney each add a commission. Letters follow, and the clerk lists delinquent parcels publicly before a summer sale to private buyers.

KRS 134.015 makes the tax the owner's personal debt, and the lien can survive a sale for as long as 11 years. Sellers need a written payoff, from the sheriff ahead of April 15 or the clerk after it, and the amount shifts monthly. Since the lien rides with the property, closing is where it gets paid, from the seller's proceeds.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Barren County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What shapes demand for Barren County houses?

The county is mostly rural, with farming the main industry. Glasgow adds manufacturing plants, a hospital and a Western Kentucky University campus, and it serves as the medical and retail center. A data center equipment plant announced for Glasgow in 2026 is expected to bring 400 manufacturing jobs.

  • Cave City and Park City draw visitors who come for Mammoth Cave, Diamond Caverns and the roadside caves along the corridor.
  • Barren River Lake and its state resort park, on the Allen County line, support lake-area homes and cabins.

Roads matter to buyers. Besides Interstate 65, the county has US 31E, US 31W and US 68. A house on a through route near the interstate interchange values differently from a farm tract on a back road, which is why the PVA's neighborhood sales data decides much of an assessment. Three school systems divide the county: Barren County Schools, Glasgow Independent and Caverna Independent. Ask the sheriff which district appears on your bill.

Preparing the house and the paperwork

Before you list, line up the pieces a buyer's lender will ask about. Get the sheriff's current balance, including any older parcel in your name. Ask the PVA whether the record shows your exemption and describes the house correctly, since an update that never got made can overstate or understate value. If the home sits near Barren River Lake or a creek, ask the floodplain administrator about the mapped zone before a buyer does.

Then think about timing. Because the sheriff takes payment from November through April, a house sold in those months can have its bill settled at the counter, while a sale after April 15 means the clerk holds the account and quotes the payoff. Either way, the figure should be in writing and dated close to the closing.

Offices to check before a sale

Beyond the PVA, the clerk and the sheriff, a few other offices touch a sale. A building and electrical inspector, at (270) 651-3921, answers permit questions for additions and rewiring. The county floodplain administrator can say whether a parcel near Barren River Lake or a creek sits in a mapped flood zone. A joint city and county planning commission, at (270) 659-0661, handles zoning.

  • Check who is the owner of record and whether an exemption sits on the parcel.
  • Ask the sheriff whether other parcels carry your name, such as a vacant lot or a mobile home.
  • If the house passed through an estate, check that the clerk shows a clean recorded deed.
  • Update your mailing address with the sheriff so later notices reach you.

An owner in a hurry, with taxes owed or a house needing work, can compare a cash offer with a listing in which the bill is cleared at closing.

Frequently asked questions

When is the Barren County tax season?

The sheriff collects from November until April. Kentucky's standard calendar gives a 2 percent discount through November 1, but ask the office for the dates on your bill.

Can Barren County tax be paid on the internet?

Yes, through the link on the sheriff's property tax page. The charge is $1.50 for bank ACH payments and about 2.75 percent for credit or debit cards.

Where does a Barren County valuation dispute begin?

With a conference with the Barren County PVA. State law requires it before an appeal, and it takes place during the roll inspection period that opens in early May.

Does a mobile home earn the Barren County exemption?

It can. KRS 132.810 treats a mobile home or manufactured house as a residential unit when the owner lives there and is 65 or older or totally disabled.

Can delinquent Barren County tax stop a sale?

It doesn't have to. The lien stays with the property, so the payoff is settled from the seller's proceeds at closing. Ask for the amount in writing before accepting an offer.

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Bullitt County for sellers

Bullitt County is the Louisville suburb that grew into a distribution hub, just south of Jefferson County. Shepherdsville is the county seat, and Mount Washington is the largest city. Interstate 65 runs through the middle of the county, and warehouse and business parks cluster along it. About a fifth of the county, in the west, is Fort Knox training land, so not every acre is on the market.

The 2025 population is 86,454, up 5.1 percent since April 2020. The typical owner-occupied home is valued at $247,200, owners hold 84.9 percent of homes, and typical rent is $987. Builders took out 654 permits in 2025 against 34,722 housing units, so new construction is a real competitor for any seller. Typical owner cost is $1,561 a month with a mortgage and $524 without one.

Where to pay and who to call

The Sheriff's Office takes the money and distributes it to the state, county, schools and special districts. It sits on the first floor of the courthouse at 300 South Buckman Street in Shepherdsville, phone 502-543-2514. Mail goes to PO Box 205, Shepherdsville, KY 40165. From October 1 through December 31 you can also pay by check at any Stock Yards Bank branch in the county.

Assessments belong to the PVA, whose county annex is at 149 North Walnut Street, phone 502-543-7480. The County Clerk, at 502-955-6369, gives payoff figures for delinquent bills from earlier years.

Due dates and penalties

The clerk delivers the bills to the sheriff at the end of September, and most owners see them in the first week of October. If yours has not come by mid-October, call for a duplicate. The 2026 bills carry four due dates, by receipt or postmark.

  • November 1: face value less a 2 percent discount.
  • December 31: face value.
  • January 31: face value plus a 5 percent penalty.
  • April 15: face value plus a 21 percent penalty.

After April 1, the sheriff no longer accepts personal or business checks. Pay with cash, a certified check, a money order or a card, and expect the processor to set the card fee. Partial payments are refused.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Bullitt County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

2026 tax rates by jurisdiction

The sheriff publishes a rate chart for each jurisdiction. These real estate rates are in the cents-per-$100 form Kentucky uses.

2026 Bullitt County real estate rates

The first six lines add up to 100.30. The Nichols, Southeast and Zoneton fire districts are each 10.0, and a Plum Creek water line of 1.0 applies to real estate in its area. Shepherdsville's own tax comes combined with the county bill. Other incorporated places, including Mount Washington, Hillview, Hunters Hollow, Pioneer Village, Fox Chase, Lebanon Junction and Hebron Estates, bill their own city tax, so call the city. The tax district code on your bill tells you which lines apply.

School district on your bill

Bullitt County Public Schools serves nearly the whole county and accounts for the largest line on the bill, 73.10. The schools on Fort Knox are run by the Department of Defense Education Activity instead, so a Fort Knox address is handled differently.

Homestead exemption

An owner who is 65 or older on January 1 and lives in the home can reduce the assessment by up to $49,100. Bring proof of age, such as a driver's license, to the PVA with the application, and do it before paying the bill. A totally disabled owner qualifies under the state rule as well. The application is due at the PVA by December 31 of the tax year.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Bullitt County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How an assessment appeal works

Request a conference at the PVA once your notice arrives. The tax roll is open for inspection for thirteen days starting the first Monday in May, and a filing at the County Clerk is due the workday after the inspection period ends. The board of assessment appeals sits for as many as five days, starting 25 to 35 days after inspection closes. Bring comparable sales and photos, because the board decides on evidence and a case with none is denied.

Reading your Bullitt County bill

A Bullitt bill is a stack of separate charges, and which ones you see depends on where the house sits. Everyone pays the state, county, health, library, school and extension lines. After that, the tax district code on the bill decides whether a city tax, a fire district or the Plum Creek water line applies to you.

If you live in Shepherdsville, the city's charge is folded into the sheriff's bill. If you live in Mount Washington or one of the other incorporated places, you will get a second bill from the city, and the city answers questions about it. A buyer's lender will want to see both paid, so a seller in a city should ask each office for a current balance.

Paying by check, at the bank or at the counter

The sheriff's office will take payment in person during its hours, and mail works if you use the Shepherdsville PO box. The bank option is handy for owners who live far from the courthouse: from October 1 through December 31, any Stock Yards Bank branch in the county takes check payments during business hours.

Plan around the April 1 cutoff. After that date, the sheriff accepts only cash, a certified check, a money order or a card, so a seller who waits for the last weeks of collection cannot write a personal check. Partial payments are turned away, which means the amount you send must cover the full bill.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Timing a sale around the tax calendar

Tax dates can help you pick a listing window. A house that closes before January 1 hands the next bill to the buyer, while one that closes in spring leaves the bill in your name, and the closing agent then splits the year. Neither route is a problem if the tax is current and the settlement statement spells out who pays.

If you have not paid yet, the November 1 date is the cheapest point of the whole year, and January 31 is where the penalty starts. A seller who knows a sale will close in the winter can pay in the discount window and keep the savings.

Handling the tax at closing

The bill goes to the January 1 owner, so a house that sells in the spring is still billed to the seller. The closing agent divides the year between the parties. The sheriff requires the full bill to be paid, so the settlement statement must show who pays.

  1. Call the sheriff at 502-543-2514 to confirm the current bill is paid.
  2. Ask the clerk at 502-955-6369 for a payoff on any earlier year.
  3. Check the PVA record and homestead status.
  4. Tell the closing agent who is paying the full bill.

Anything unpaid after April 15 moves to the clerk with a lien, and interest runs 1 percent a month, so ask for a payoff before the closing date. Sellers with inherited, tenant-occupied or heavily worn houses can often close with a cash buyer and have the tax paid from proceeds.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Bullitt County sheriff's phone number for taxes?

Call 502-543-2514. The office is on the first floor of the courthouse at 300 South Buckman Street in Shepherdsville.

When does the Bullitt County 2% discount end?

For the 2026 bills it ends November 1, by receipt or postmark. December 31 is face value, January 31 adds 5 percent, and April 15 adds 21 percent.

Can I pay Bullitt County taxes at a bank?

Yes. Any Stock Yards Bank branch in the county takes check payments from October 1 to December 31 during business hours.

Does Shepherdsville charge a separate city tax?

No separate bill. Shepherdsville's tax is combined with the county bill, while other cities such as Mount Washington and Hillview bill their own city tax.

How much is the Bullitt County homestead exemption?

Up to $49,100 off the assessed value for owners 65 or older who live in the home on January 1. Apply at the PVA before paying the bill.

Bourbon County, KY Property Tax Guide: Offices, Appeals and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Kentucky

Selling in Bourbon County? Get a Cash Offer

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Bourbon County?

Who handles property tax in Bourbon County

Your bill comes from a division of labor inside the Paris courthouse building. Room 15 houses the Property Valuation Administrator (PVA), who decides what the property is worth. Room 104 houses the Sheriff's Office, which prints the bills and receives payment.

The PVA's number is (859) 987-2152, extension 217, and the sheriff's number is (859) 987-2130. Both keep weekday hours from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The sheriff closes on holidays, including Good Friday, Memorial Day and Thanksgiving, so plan around those days if you are paying in person.

Bourbon County at a glance

Farmland rolls out around Paris, and Millersburg and North Middletown are the other small towns. About 20,243 people live here in 9,399 housing units. A typical home is worth $229,300, and owners occupy 63.7% of them. Few people move: 94.9% stayed in the same house over the past year, which keeps listings scarce. Builders took out 109 permits in 2025.

If you own acreage, ask the PVA in Room 15 for the parcel record and compare it with a recent local sale before you accept the assessed figure as right.

Due dates and penalties

The Sheriff's Office collects from November 1 through April 15. The earlier you pay, the less you owe. A U.S. postmark counts as the date of payment.

Bourbon County Sheriff's collection periods
Payment periodDiscount or penalty
November 1 to November 302% discount
December 1 to December 31Base amount due
January 1 to January 315% penalty
February 1 to April 1521% penalty period

Delinquent notices are mailed February 1. After April 15 each unpaid bill is handed to the County Clerk, and significant extra fees follow. Selling in spring? Ask where your bill is now.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Bourbon County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How to pay a Bourbon County tax bill

You can walk in at 301 Main Street, Suite 104, Paris, or mail a check to the same address. The bill is a postcard sent to the homeowner. When a lender pays from escrow, check with the lender about whether it also needs a copy.

  • Cash, cashier's checks, money orders, and personal or business checks from U.S. banks all work.
  • Credit and debit cards work at the counter only, and a 3.5% fee comes with them.
  • The office turns away third party checks and foreign funds.
  • If a check bounces you pay $50, and the bill stays unpaid.

What to bring to the Sheriff's Office

Carry the postcard or your parcel details, and a form of payment from the list above. Checks are payable to the Bourbon County Sheriff's Office. Payment by phone or online is not offered, so you will need either a visit or a stamp.

  • A mailed check is dated by its postmark, so drop it in the mail early in November if you want the discount.
  • Make sure the check comes from a U.S. bank and carries your own name, not someone else's.
  • Also expect closures on Martin Luther King Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Christmas and New Year's, in addition to the holidays listed above.

Can I dispute a Bourbon County assessment?

Yes. The value is set as of January 1, and the first step needs no paperwork: ask the PVA or a deputy to meet with you.

KRS 133.120 sets out the process. Book your conference in May, while the county's inspection window is open. It lasts two weeks, though the state may extend it. If the talk goes nowhere, mail the County Clerk a letter stating why you disagree and what you think the house is worth. That letter reaches the board of assessment appeals through the clerk, and it must arrive one workday after the window closes. Show up at the hearing with nearby sales, an appraisal or a repair estimate from a contractor.

Keep paying while you appeal. Base the payment on the value you claim, and expect to owe the difference plus interest if the board decides on more. Going straight past the county board also shuts you out of the state-level Board of Tax Appeals.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Bourbon County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Homestead exemption

The exemption here is the one set by the state, and you qualify by turning 65 or by being classed as totally disabled. For 2025 and 2026 the deduction is $49,100, and the state resets the figure every two years.

File the application at the PVA's desk. The deduction is subtracted from the assessed value first, and tax is figured on what is left. Disability claims must be renewed each year, with two exceptions: owners with a service-connected disability, and owners that Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems has ruled permanently disabled. Check with the PVA to learn which deduction your current bill reflects.

What a late bill costs

Timing changes the total a lot. November earns the 2% discount, December costs the plain amount, January adds 5%, and the 21% penalty period covers February 1 through April 15. Between the November rate and the last collection day, the gap is more than a quarter of the bill.

Once the clerk has the bill, the clerk's own fees get added, so the payoff is the figure quoted the day you pay. Sellers with an old unpaid year should phone the clerk for it before choosing a closing date.

The Bourbon County tax year in order

The same calendar repeats every year.

  • January 1: the assessment date. The PVA values the property as it stands that day.
  • May: the two-week inspection window, when you can sit down with the PVA or a deputy.
  • The workday after the window closes: your written appeal reaches the County Clerk.
  • November 1: the Sheriff's Office starts collecting, and the 2% discount runs through November 30.
  • February 1: delinquent notices are mailed.
  • April 15: collection ends at the sheriff's desk, and unpaid bills go to the clerk.

If you list in spring, find out where your bill sits in that sequence. Title companies ask the same thing, and a bill already at the clerk takes longer to clear.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What happens to the tax bill when you sell?

Tax left unpaid attaches to the house, though the debt itself is owed by the person who held title on January 1. Your closing agent checks that the bill is current. The buyer's lender or title company will also want the deed and any lien releases in hand, and all of that paper comes out of offices at 301 Main Street.

  • Call the sheriff to learn whether this year's bill is paid, and which period it falls in.
  • Write the buyer's mailing address on the deed's tax-bill line, so the next postcard reaches them.
  • Settle with the buyer how this year's tax will be divided.
  • An older unpaid year is a clerk matter, so the clerk gives that payoff.

Owners here spend about $1,424 a month with a mortgage and $466 without one, and the tax bill is a slice of that. A cash buyer skips the lender's escrow questions, but the tax check at title stays the same.

Frequently asked questions

What is the deadline to avoid a penalty on a Bourbon County bill?

Pay by December 31 and you owe only the face amount. The 2% discount stops after November 30, and the 5% penalty starts January 1.

Where can I hand over a Bourbon County tax payment?

Go to the Sheriff's Office at 301 Main Street, Suite 104, Paris, or send it by mail. Cards are taken in person only, and the fee is 3.5%.

What happens to a Bourbon County bill unpaid after April 15?

It moves from the sheriff to the County Clerk, with significant added fees. Ask the clerk what the payoff is.

How do I appeal my Bourbon County property assessment?

Ask the PVA for a conference in May. If you do not settle there, file a written petition with the County Clerk one workday after the inspection window ends.

Who is eligible for the Bourbon County homestead exemption?

Anyone 65 or older, and anyone classed as totally disabled, can apply through the PVA. The deduction is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026.

Which McCracken County offices touch a tax bill

Three do, each with its own lane. A parcel's dollar value is the work of the Property Valuation Administrator (PVA). The Sheriff's Office receives the payment. Only after the spring cutoff does the County Clerk get involved, and then only for bills still open. The PVA neither mails bills nor accepts payments, so a check carried to the assessment office will be turned around.

You will find the PVA at 621 Washington Street in Paducah. Weekday hours run eight to four-thirty, and callers can dial (270) 444-4712. Public service companies and a few similar accounts are valued in Frankfort by the state Revenue Cabinet instead. For payments, see the Sheriff's tax page, which lists walk-in service Monday to Friday between 8:30 and 4:30 during collection season. County offices share the 300 Clarence Gaines Street address.

Due dates and penalties

Collection by the Sheriff opens November 1 and closes April 15, and notices go out in late September or early October. KRS 134.015 then prices each stage:

  • By November 1: bill minus 2 percent.
  • November 2 to year end: the printed figure.
  • January: add 5 percent.
  • February through April 15: add 10 percent.
  • After April 15: the Sheriff hands over what is still open.

Mail, phone, counter and a website button (live November through April) all work. Anyone paying by card or e-check owes a processing charge to an outside vendor, which is shown before you confirm. If a lender escrows your tax, call it first, because the Sheriff sends a bill to the owner only, and the lender may already have requested its own copy.

What goes into a McCracken County bill

The state's 2025 real property rate is 10.6 cents on each $100 of assessed value, down from 10.9 cents the year before. The city, schools, library, fire districts and county each add a levy, and the PVA lists those same bodies as users of its assessments.

One line is newer than the rest: a county 911 fee that first appeared on the 2024 bills. Most parcels pay $46.26. The early-payment reduction skips that line, which matters when you estimate a credit at closing.

A house far from that middle point deserves a question to the PVA about how its value was built. Ask to see the property record, check the square footage and room count against what you own, and point out anything that is wrong, such as a finished space that does not exist or a feature that was torn out.

How to contest a value

Begin with a sit-down at the PVA office, since nothing can be filed before it. The dates after that are fixed by statute.

  • The roll lies open for 13 days beginning the first Monday in May.
  • Expect the PVA or a deputy to explain the valuation and write up what each side said.
  • File the appeal with the County Clerk one business day after the viewing window shuts.
  • Gather proof for the hearing: insurance papers, building costs, land and structure descriptions, and sale listings. A claim with nothing attached is rejected.
  • A panel of local owners hears the case about a month later.

A hired representative has to be on the Revenue Department's list of eligible professionals, such as an attorney, CPA or certified appraiser, with your signed authorization. If bills are already out and the board lands above your claimed figure, a supplemental bill follows. The Sheriff adds a caution of its own: leaving new additions off the record can bring a 20 percent penalty on the bill.

Homestead exemption

Owners 65 and over, and those found totally disabled, can take $49,100 off assessed value for both 2025 and 2026. The rate then applies only to what remains.

Apply at the McCracken County PVA, not the Sheriff. Age can be shown with a birth certificate, driver's license or passport. Claimants who rely on disability must have a federal or retirement-system finding, and most renew yearly. A service-connected disability, or a ruling of permanent and total disability by Social Security or the state retirement systems, removes the yearly renewal. Nothing is granted until a formal application is on file.

Selling with taxes owed

An unpaid bill stays with the parcel. After April 15 the County Clerk holds it as a certificate of delinquency, records a lien, and charges 1 percent a month. KRS 134.420 lets the lien run 11 years through any change of owner, which means a buyer's title search will turn it up.

Delinquent bills go to the County Attorney, who works under a state agreement. Its letters warn that ignoring the bill can end in foreclosure, while an owner who keeps up an installment agreement has the bill marked unavailable for sale to investors. The Clerk's yearly sale of such bills is normally held in October. An investor who buys one must notify the owner within 50 days, may add its own charges, and can ask a court to foreclose after a year.

Before listing, get a payoff figure from the Sheriff, and clear it before April 15 if you can. Ask for the amount in writing with the date it stays good, then pass it to the closing agent so it is paid from your proceeds at the table. Bring the deed and a photo ID when you visit, and keep every receipt, since the title agent will want proof that each year is clear. If you have an installment agreement with the County Attorney, tell the closing agent so the remaining balance is included in the payoff. If the house has repairs you would rather skip, an investor paying cash for the house in its current condition can fold the tax payoff into one closing.

About McCracken County

The county spreads over 268 square miles at Kentucky's far western tip, part of the Jackson Purchase, with the Ohio River along its north and the Tennessee River along its northeast. It anchors the Paducah, KY-IL metropolitan area. Paducah, the seat, is the lone incorporated city. Lone Oak, Heath, Reidland and West Paducah are among the communities outside it.

Two districts teach the children: McCracken County Public Schools for nearly everywhere outside the city, and Paducah Public Schools for most of Paducah. Buyers often ask which one a house falls in, so know the answer before you list, and check it against the address on your tax bill. Owners live in about 69 percent of homes, and 170 permits in 2025 mean most sales involve an existing house.

Frequently asked questions

Is the McCracken County PVA where I pay my tax?

No. The PVA handles values and exemptions only. Take payment to the Sheriff's Office.

What changes on April 15 for unpaid McCracken County taxes?

Sheriff collection of the prior bill ends that evening. Any balance heads to the County Clerk's office, and interest and fees begin to build.

Is the 911 fee on McCracken County bills eligible for the early-payment cut?

No. The 911 fee that arrived with the 2024 bills sits outside the discount, and most parcels owe $46.26 for it.

How much is the homestead deduction for a McCracken County owner in 2026?

For 2026 the deduction is $49,100, as in 2025. Anyone 65 or older, or totally disabled, applies through the PVA.

Can I close on a McCracken County house that has back taxes?

Yes. The usual route is for the closing agent to pay the balance from the seller's proceeds, after you have asked the Sheriff or Clerk for a payoff.

Who sends the Oldham County tax bill

Oldham County's sheriff mails and collects the bill, while the Property Valuation Administration (PVA) sets the value behind it. One bill rolls together what is owed to the state, the county, the school districts, Crestwood and 18 special districts. Envelopes are in the mail by the end of September, and the sheriff's number is 502-222-9501.

The sheriff's site also has a Property Tax FAQ that goes into payment options. Anything about a value that looks wrong goes to the PVA at 502-222-9320, because the sheriff never assigns value to a parcel. The bill itself shows the due dates, how to avoid penalties and what a mortgage servicer's payment looks like.

Oldham County at a glance

Oldham County sits in north central Kentucky and is part of the Louisville metro area, with the Ohio River forming its northern edge against Indiana. La Grange is the seat and the biggest city. Crestwood, Goshen, Pewee Valley, Prospect, Orchard Grass Hills and River Bluff are cities too, and Buckner and Westport are census-designated places. Prospect lies mostly in Jefferson County, so confirm which county bills a Prospect parcel.

Prices run well above the state norm, and the county keeps growing: it gained roughly 3,400 residents between April 2020 and July 2025.

  • Population is 70,986 for 2025, up 5.0 percent since April 2020.
  • A typical owned home is worth $393,100, and owners live in 87.1 percent of occupied homes.
  • Owners with a mortgage pay a median of $2,193 a month. Those without one pay $712.
  • Rent runs $1,219 a month at the median, and household income is $122,497.
  • The county has 24,896 housing units, and builders pulled 276 permits in 2025.

School zones drive many buyer questions. The county is served by North Oldham, Oldham County and South Oldham high schools, so know which one serves your address.

Oldham County payment calendar

What to do about a high valuation

The first step is a conference with the PVA. Bring your own number and backing for it, such as nearby sales, a recent appraisal, contractor quotes or rent records. A statewide PVA appeal guide lays out the whole path.

If talks fail, the route runs through the Oldham County Clerk to a three-resident local board and finally to the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals, where the deadline is 30 days from the mailed ruling. In a county with prices this high, sales from the same subdivision make the strongest evidence.

Getting ready for a PVA conference

A conference goes better when you walk in with paper. Collect a few items before you call 502-222-9320: your latest bill, any recent appraisal, photos of defects such as a worn roof or foundation cracks, quotes from contractors, and sale prices for three or four houses near yours. For a rental, add rent and expense records.

Write down the value you think is right and why. A figure with backing behind it is far harder to wave off than a complaint that the number feels high. If the PVA does not budge, you will still have a record to carry to the local board.

Keep paying the bill while the appeal runs, because a higher final value later produces a supplemental charge.

Where unpaid Oldham County bills end up

Anything the sheriff has not collected by closing time on April 15 goes to the County Clerk. The clerk's delinquent tax page sends value disputes to the PVA and sale questions to the Department of Revenue.

From there the parcel is liened, interest runs at 1 percent monthly, the county attorney mails warnings, and a sale waits at least 90 days after the transfer. If an investor buys the certificate, the owner then owes the investor.

If you are selling, get the clerk's written quote and settle it from your proceeds at closing. The title company will ask for it anyway.

Charges at closing for an Oldham County seller

Kentucky's transfer tax is the seller's: fifty cents for each $500 of value, counting any remainder as a full $500, taken by the clerk with the deed (KRS 142.050). Deeds between spouses, corrective deeds and foreclosure deeds are exempt.

  • Every deed lists the full price, mailing addresses for both sides and a forwarding address for the next tax bill.
  • A gift or token-price sale needs a sworn market-value estimate.
  • Heirs file the personal representative's affidavit wherever the estate holds land.

Why bills differ from street to street

The sheriff bills 18 special districts and one city, so neighbors a few miles apart can owe different totals. Before you compare listings, check which districts appear on each bill.

When you set an asking price, use a recent bill for your own address and expect a buyer to do the same. Ask the sheriff or the PVA if anything on it looks unfamiliar.

Steps for selling with a tax problem

A house with a lien on it can still be sold. The County Clerk quotes a payoff valid through a stated date, and the title company pays it from the sale proceeds. If you want a quicker route than a traditional listing, a cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and the buyer's financing wait, and the lien still gets paid at closing.

  1. Call the clerk for a written payoff and ask how long it stays good.
  2. Confirm that the current year's bill is paid or prorated.
  3. Ask the sheriff to confirm nothing is open from earlier years.
  4. Bring the payoff and receipts to the title company before the closing date.
You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Escrow, servicers and the January 1 rule

Many owners never write a check, because a mortgage servicer pays from escrow. That is fine until a sale or a refinance, when the paid-through date matters. Ask the servicer for a statement showing what it paid and when, and make sure the discount deadline was met if you want the 2 percent saving.

Ownership on January 1 decides who is billed for the year. A seller who closes after that date will still see the sheriff's envelope with their name on it, and the title agent will prorate the total between the two sides. Put the split in writing, hand the agent your copy of the bill and keep the receipt for your own tax records.

Frequently asked questions

Who handles questions about an Oldham County valuation?

The PVA, 502-222-9320. Values come from that office, and the sheriff only collects what they produce.

When do Oldham County property tax bills arrive?

Mailing wraps up by the end of September. Call the sheriff at 502-222-9501 if yours is missing in early October.

Is Crestwood's city tax billed separately?

No. The Crestwood levy rides on the same sheriff bill as the county and district charges, so a single payment covers all of them.

Who pays the transfer tax on an Oldham County sale?

The seller, at fifty cents per $500 of value, paid to the clerk before the deed is recorded.

Can a house with a tax lien on it still be sold in Oldham County?

Yes. The County Clerk quotes a payoff valid through a stated date, and the title company pays it from the sale proceeds.

Who values your house and who bills you

Think of the system as a relay. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) sets each parcel's assessed value. Around October 1 the sheriff sends out and collects the bill. When April 15 passes with money still owed, the county clerk is handed the baton.

The sheriff doesn't decide what your house is worth. Your bill multiplies the PVA's figure by the rate of every taxing body over the parcel: the state, the county, a school district and any special district. If your house is inside Winchester, which is both the seat and the only city, ask the city whether it bills a separate city tax and when.

Where to pay a Clark County bill

The sheriff's office is in the basement of the Governor James Clark Judicial Building in Winchester, and the number for questions is (859) 744-4390. Payment is accepted several ways.

Ways to pay the Clark County sheriff
MethodWhat to know
By mailCheck or money order to 17 Cleveland Avenue, Winchester, KY 40391; the USPS postmark counts, private meters do not
Drop boxCheck or money order in the box off West Broadway, with the bill number, map number or address written on it
OnlineDebit, credit or Google Pay through the sheriff's website, with merchant fees
In personCheck, money order or cash; cards with fees; weekday hours of 8:00 am to 4:00 pm
Bank counterA downtown bank branch on West Broadway takes checks and money orders for the exact amount, with the bill, and no cash

No bill by October 15? Call the sheriff. If a buyer or a mortgage company is supposed to pay, forward the bill to them right away.

Due dates and penalties

KRS 134.015 fixes these dates, and they repeat annually.

  • Through November 1: pay in full and take a 2 percent discount.
  • November 2 to December 31: the bill as printed.
  • Every day in January: 5 percent is added.
  • February 1 to April 15: a 10 percent penalty plus a 10 percent add-on.

At the close of business on April 15 the county clerk takes whatever is still unpaid. Payments made at the clerk's office carry a 20 percent county attorney fee, a 10 percent clerk fee and monthly interest of 1 percent, and delinquent bills can be sold to a third party. Bills go out October 1, the face amount holds until December 31, and collection passes to the clerk after April 15.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Clark County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What to know about Clark County property

Clark County sits next to Lexington and belongs to its metropolitan area. It covers 255 square miles. In 2020 it had 36,972 residents, 14,917 households and 16,116 housing units. About 65.6 percent of occupied homes were owned and 34.4 percent rented, with 7.4 percent of units vacant. Around 71 percent of residents live in urban parts of the county, and the rest live where acreage and farm parcels change hands.

The Kentucky River, Red River, Lulbegrud Creek and Boone's Creek cross the county, so a parcel near the water deserves a look at flood risk before you list. Manufacturing around Winchester, helped by I-64 and the Mountain Parkway, supports the in-town market.

How to challenge an assessed value

Call the Clark County PVA at (859) 745-0250 and request a conference before the roll's public review closes. The review runs thirteen days from the first Monday of May, and no appeal can start without the conference. A phone call counts.

Not satisfied? File a written petition with the clerk by the first workday after review ends. Name the parcel, give your reasons and state what you believe is fair cash value. The hearing follows about a month later, and the board wants facts: sale listings, construction costs, loan papers.

Officials can start a review too. The county judge/executive, a mayor or a school superintendent may ask the board in writing to look at specific parcels, which is how some values rise without the owner filing anything. The plan: confer, file, bring comparable sales and pay on the figure you claim.

Homestead exemption

An owner who has reached 65, or who is totally disabled, can have a set sum removed from the home's assessed value. The state figure is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, and a fresh amount is published every second year.

File with the Clark County PVA. A birth certificate, driver's license or passport shows age. Disability claims require a federal or retirement system classification, and most renew yearly.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Clark County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling with unpaid tax

Title companies pay the balance at the closing table out of your price. Ask the sheriff what the current bill stands at, and ask the clerk whether an earlier bill turned into a certificate of delinquency. Under KRS 134.015 the lien from an unpaid year stays with the land for eleven years whoever owns it, so a buyer's title search will turn it up.

The cheapest time to clear a balance is before April 15, while the sheriff still has the bill and the extra cost is limited to the penalty and add-on. Afterward the clerk's percentages stack up, and an outside investor can buy the claim. An empty, inherited or run-down house can still sell to an investor who accepts it unrepaired and pays the tax out of the price. Ask for that payoff to be shown as its own line on the settlement statement.

At closing, ask the agent to divide the current year by the date the deed transfers, so each side covers its own months.

A person who buys after the bill is issued may still receive it in the old owner's name, because value is set each year at an earlier date. Forward any mail you get after closing to the new owner or their lender.

Preparing to list

Start with the PVA record. Ask whether the acreage, building details and any outbuildings match what stands on the land, since errors flow straight into the bill. Then confirm the exemption on file still fits the owner. If the PVA has your property as the wrong size, a buyer will see the problem in the assessment history.

Next, collect your payment proof for the year. The sheriff can confirm what has been paid, and a bank or servicer that pays from escrow should show the same. Keep receipts together with your deed so the closing agent has everything in one place.

Last, think about timing. A sale in the autumn means the bill may just have gone out, while a sale after February 1 means penalties may already be running. If you're up against a deadline, an as-is cash purchase that pays the tax from the proceeds can close faster than a financed one, and it needs no repairs or showings. Whichever way you go, get the payoff in writing before you agree to a price.

Frequently asked questions

Which Clark County phone numbers cover tax bills and values?

Call the sheriff's office at (859) 744-4390 for bill and payment questions. For value questions call the Clark County PVA at (859) 745-0250.

When do Clark County bills get mailed?

Around October 1 each year, and they also appear online. Owners without a printed bill by October 15 should call the sheriff.

Does the Clark County sheriff accept cash?

Yes, at the sheriff's office counter in Winchester. The downtown bank location does not accept cash.

Who sets the value of my Clark County home for tax?

The Clark County PVA, not the sheriff. The sheriff only collects the bill that results from the PVA's assessment and the local tax rates.

What if I miss the April 15 date in Clark County?

The unpaid bill transfers to the county clerk. There a 20 percent county attorney fee, a 10 percent clerk fee and 1 percent interest per month apply, and the bill can be sold to a third party.

Nelson County became the fourth Kentucky county in 1784, carved from Jefferson County, and spans about 418 square miles of land. My Old Kentucky Home State Park hosts The Stephen Foster Story each summer, and the Basilica of St. Joseph Proto-Cathedral recalls the 1808 founding of the Diocese of Bardstown. Anything unpaid at the sheriff by April 15 passes to the County Clerk.

The sheriff returns any check that differs from the bill by even a dollar, as well as late or partial ones, because audit rules demand exact accounting. If a lender escrows your tax, send the bill to the lender. The first proper payment received gets processed, and no refund goes to an owner who pays ahead of the lender.

How to challenge your assessment

Begin at the PVA, which holds a conference with the owner or a representative. KRS 133.120 requires it before any formal appeal, and a phone call can count. The tax roll is displayed for 13 days beginning the opening Monday in May under KRS 133.045, and the conference must fall before or during that stretch.

A disagreement that survives the conference becomes a written petition at the County Clerk. It lists the parcel, the reasons and the owner's estimate, and it is due the workday after inspection closes. Hearings are public, and the owner supplies the facts: sales listings, insurance policies, construction costs or loan papers. The bill itself isn't delayed, and an increase is billed with interest from the original due date.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Nelson County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Homestead exemption

Owners aged 65 and up, and owners classified as totally disabled, are eligible. The state figure of $49,100 applies to 2025 and 2026 and comes off assessed value before rates. The Nelson County PVA takes the filing, and a passport, birth certificate or license shows age. Disability claims renew each year, except for owners with a service-connected disability and for owners ruled permanently and totally disabled by federal Social Security or the state retirement system.

Tax tasks before closing

The tax is a personal debt of the January 1 owner, and delinquent property carries a lien for eleven years under KRS 134.420. A buyer's title company searches for it.

  • Collect every bill for the parcel, including city and independent school lines for a Bardstown address.
  • Ask the sheriff for the exact payoff on the planned closing date.
  • Write the buyer's mailing address for tax bills into the deed, per KRS 382.135.
  • For an inherited house, the executor files an affidavit with the County Clerk naming recipients and values.

A New Haven or Bardstown city bill is separate from the county bill, so a payoff quoting only the county number leaves a gap. Confirm the payoff in writing and keep the receipt with the closing file.

If the house needs work or taxes are behind

Selling with taxes owed is common. The closing agent pays the payoff from your proceeds, so the number you need is the full amount across every bill, not just the county line. After April 15 the clerk quotes it instead of the sheriff. A cash buyer who accepts the house as-is lets you skip repairs and showings, and you can set the closing around the payoff date.

For an heir, the executor's affidavit comes first, then the deed. Bring your photo ID, the latest bills for every district line on the parcel, and any exemption approval. After closing, tell the PVA about the new owner so the next set of bills goes to the right address.

If the house sits in a city district, check which bills the buyer will inherit. A Bardstown address may carry city and independent school lines that a county-only quote misses, and a New Haven or Fairfield address has its own city line. Ask the sheriff which districts apply to your parcel number before you sign a contract, so the payoff you quote the buyer is complete.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Which office handles a Nelson County valuation complaint?

The PVA, at (502) 348-1810. The sheriff doesn't assess property.

Does the Nelson County Sheriff take inexact payments?

No. A check that doesn't match the bill exactly, along with any late or partial payment, is returned.

What becomes of a Nelson County bill still open after April 15?

It moves from the sheriff to the Nelson County Clerk.

Do bills differ across Nelson County?

Yes. Districts 1, 7, 8, 11, 12 and 13 get one county bill, while districts 2, 3, 4, 5 and 9 also receive New Haven, Bardstown, Bardstown Independent School or Fairfield bills.

What deduction does a senior get on a Nelson County home?

The state subtracts $49,100 from assessed value for 2025 and 2026, after an owner who is 65 or over, or totally disabled, applies at the PVA.
