Who to call about a Woodford County tax matter

Questions about what a property is worth go to the Property Valuation Administrator. Questions about what you owe go to the sheriff. The valuation office is in the courthouse at 103 S. Main Street, Room 108, Versailles, and it opens at 8 each morning, closing at 4 Monday to Thursday and 5:30 on Friday. For the sheriff, call 859-873-3119 or 859-873-3126; the website has bill search with online payment.

A notice stating each property's value reaches owners in spring. The sheriff sends bills out during the final week of September, with overdue notices going out in February. The sheriff never mails threatening demands for property tax, so a letter from an unfamiliar "unit" with an 800 number should be reported, and the demand ignored.

What a seller of a Woodford County house should know

Woodford sits in the Bluegrass inside the Lexington metro area. Versailles is the seat and the biggest town; Midway is the only other city. The county had 27,883 residents in 2025, a 3.8 percent gain over 2020, and 11,917 housing units. Builders pulled 95 permits in 2025.

  • The middle owned home is worth $299,700.
  • A typical household earns $83,788, and 71.7 percent of households are owners.
  • Rent runs $1,138. Owners pay $1,571 with a mortgage and $577 without.

With prices like these, even a modest assessment gap shows up in the bill, so the steps below are worth the effort. Before you list, find out whether the PVA's value looks close to what comparable houses have sold for, and whether any exemption is on your parcel. A buyer's agent will look at the tax bill when estimating monthly costs, and a figure that is out of line can make a house harder to sell. If the roll is not open yet, plan around the first Monday in May, when the display begins.

If you want to ask about a value or an exemption in person, the courthouse counter in Room 108 is the place. Bring your parcel number or address, and write down the name of whoever helps you and the date.

Your tax year in Woodford County

The calendar is statewide and set out in KRS 134.015.

Yearly property tax steps for a Woodford County owner
WhenStep
January 1Assessment date; whoever is the owner of record that day is the taxpayer
Opening Monday of May, 13 daysRoll on public display
25 to 35 days laterLocal appeals board sits
Up to November 1Discount of 2 percent
November 2 to December 31Face amount of the bill
JanuaryAdd 5 percent
February onwardAdd 10 percent
April 15Unpaid bills go from the sheriff to the clerk, which records a lien

If you list in spring, last year's bill is still yours when your name was on the January 1 roll. Get a balance in writing from the sheriff for your title company.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Woodford County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How does a Woodford County owner challenge a value?

First, sit down with the PVA office. The state demands that conference, and the office has to walk you through how it reached your number and write down what each side claims. After that, the appeal goes to the County Clerk, and it must arrive by closing time the next workday once the display ends.

  • Bring evidence: details of the building and lot, insurance records, construction costs, and sales listings. Without evidence the appeal is denied.
  • Anyone you pay to represent you must be a recognized professional, such as an attorney, accountant, broker or appraiser, and needs your written permission.
  • You may record the hearing, and the board has to put any change in writing.

If you skip the local board, the Kentucky Claims Commission is closed to you. If bills print before your case ends and the final value comes out above your claim, a supplemental bill covers the difference.

How parcels are valued

The method depends on the property. Houses are compared to nearby sales, with adjustments for things like a basement. Barns and other farm structures are priced as replacement cost minus depreciation, and income property is valued from its earnings. Farmland is assessed on its agricultural worth under Section 172A of the state constitution, which can sharply lower the tax on open pasture. Anyone planning to divide a farm should ask both the PVA and the clerk what changes when the use changes.

Any parcel can be revalued yearly, and each must be inspected at least every fourth year. If your figure looks too high, ask the PVA which sales it relied on and when staff last inspected the house.

Homestead exemption

A homeowner who turns 65, or who is totally disabled, gets a fixed amount deducted from the assessed value of their residence, one deduction per household. The claim goes on Form 62A350 at the PVA office. The exemption carries on while the same applicant stays. An owner with a service connected disability rating, or anyone with a permanent Social Security disability finding, files once. A buyer applies fresh, and the PVA can quote the current sum, which the state revisits every two years.

After a sale, notify the PVA so your old address loses the deduction and the next owner can start a claim.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Woodford County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Unpaid after April 15

Right after the clerk records the lien, interest begins at 1 percent a month. Next comes a 10 percent clerk commission, then a 20 percent attorney commission. The attorney sends two notices, one at 30 days and one later, before a sale, which falls 90 to 135 days after the transfer. KRS 134.420 lets the lien run for 11 years, and it stays with the parcel. If you sell, it comes out of your proceeds. A private buyer who purchases the certificate may add fees.

Selling with a bill still open

Call the sheriff about the current year and the clerk about anything that crossed over on April 15. Ask for both numbers in writing, since the title company subtracts them from your payout. When a private buyer already holds a certificate, you pay that buyer, fees included, so find out who holds it.

Some cash buyers take the house with the bill still open and settle the balance from the proceeds, so you do not have to pay ahead of a sale you are still arranging. In any sale, the contract should name who covers the current year, because the January 1 owner is the one named on the bill. A written split also prevents a dispute after the keys change hands.

Frequently asked questions

Who sends out Woodford County tax bills each year?

The sheriff mails them during the last week of September. Call 859-873-3119 or 859-873-3126, or use the website for bill search plus online payment.

How can a Woodford County owner push back on a valuation?

Schedule the PVA conference, then lodge the appeal with the County Clerk the next workday after public display ends. The PVA is at 103 S. Main Street, Room 108, in Versailles.

When does the 2 percent Woodford County discount stop?

It ends November 1. The printed amount is due until December 31, then 5 percent is added for January and 10 percent after that.

If a Woodford County house sells in spring, who owes that year's tax?

The January 1 owner is taxed and appears on the bill. The sale contract and title company decide who pays at closing, so get a written sheriff balance first.

What are good questions for the Woodford County PVA?

Ask which recent sales back your value and when staff last inspected the house. The answers tell you if an appeal is worth the effort before May.

Allen County tax offices and what each one does

Property tax in Allen County runs through two desks in Scottsville. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) decides what each parcel is worth. The Sheriff takes the payment. Nothing the PVA does sets the tax rate. Your bill comes from that assessed value times levies from the county, the school board and taxing districts like the library and the health department.

Where to call in Scottsville
OfficeAddressPhone
Property Valuation Administrator201 W Main St #1, Scottsville, KY 42164(270) 237-3711
Sheriff, tax collector194 W Wood St, Scottsville, KY 42164(270) 237-3210
Sheriff, owners who never received a billScottsville(270) 237-3388

The PVA keeps weekday hours until 4:30 p.m. Online, the sheriff's page offers a tax bill search by owner or parcel, and the PVA's page carries the certified roll with ownership details.

Kentucky freezes both value and ownership on January 1. Buy in June and the bill for that year is still addressed to whoever owned on January 1. The PVA tries to send the new owner a copy using the deed on record. If no copy shows up, phone the sheriff instead of waiting.

Due dates and penalties

Four price points govern an Allen County bill under KRS 134.015: a 2 percent reduction for paying in full through November 1, the face amount during the rest of the year's last two months, a 5 percent surcharge in January, and a 10 percent surcharge from February onward.

The sheriff's work ends on April 15. At close of business, whatever is still unpaid transfers to the clerk, and each account becomes a recorded lien called a certificate of delinquency. Any sale has to wait at least 90 days and must happen within 135. Notices come from the county attorney during that stretch, and the clerk publishes the delinquent list a month or longer beforehand.

After the handoff the balance climbs by 1 percent each month, and the clerk and county attorney collect commissions. Kentucky's sample account begins with a $1,000 bill. Paid within five business days of the transfer it costs $1,387.79. After the county attorney's first notice it is $1,611.30, and it reaches $1,704.21 if an investor pays it at the tax sale. The sample uses assumed rates, so your own payoff will vary somewhat.

How to appeal your assessment

You can't skip the PVA. A sit-down with the PVA or a deputy has to happen before an appeal is taken, and the roll can be inspected for 13 days counting from the first Monday of May. The PVA publishes those dates in the newspaper with the widest circulation.

When the meeting is over, take the appeal to the county clerk by the next workday after inspection closes. Local property owners sit as the review board, and they meet between 25 and 35 days after inspection ends. Bring photos showing condition, repair bids, insurance paperwork and recent nearby sales. The board looks only at evidence presented while you and the PVA's representative are both present, and a changed value must be explained in writing.

You're free to make an audio recording of the hearing. Bills printed before a decision use the figure from your form, and a higher final value brings a second bill for the difference, which is why a realistic number matters.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Allen County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

The state rate and a typical Allen County home

The statewide real property rate for 2025 is 10.6 cents per $100 of assessed value. It was 10.9 cents in 2024. Levies from the county and local districts go on top, and the sheriff's bill search lists the complete amount for a given parcel. The midpoint value for an owner-occupied home is $192,300, a fair marker for where most Allen County owners sit.

The early-payment discount of 2 percent reduces the entire bill, local levies included.

Homestead exemption

Kentucky lets homeowners aged 65 or over, and those classed as totally disabled, shave $49,100 off assessed value for 2025 and 2026. The reduction happens before any tax rate is applied.

Reaching 65 doesn't switch it on. The application goes to the Allen County PVA at (270) 237-3711. A claim based on disability must be renewed each year, with two exceptions: owners whose disability came from military service, and owners ruled permanently and totally disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

Checking your own account before you sell

Before listing the house, spend ten minutes confirming three things. First, search the sheriff's page for your parcel and see whether the current bill shows as paid. Second, look at the PVA's roll to make sure the owner names and the description match your deed. Third, if you've held the house since before 2025, ask the PVA whether a homestead claim is on file and whether it needs renewing.

An error caught early costs one phone call. Mistakes found by a title examiner a week before closing cost time, and sometimes a buyer's patience. A mismatch in a name, such as a late spouse still listed, is the usual culprit, and the PVA is the office that corrects it.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Allen County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling with taxes owed

A tax lien attaches to the land, not to you personally. The statute lets it live until someone pays it or eleven years go by, and a sale doesn't end it. Expect the buyer's title company to find it and insist on a payoff, either before closing or out of what you'd receive.

  1. Ask the Allen County Sheriff to write down the balance shortly before the closing date.
  2. When the account has already moved to the clerk, the clerk gives that number instead, with interest and commissions included.
  3. Your closing agent subtracts the payoff from your share and files the release.
  4. Put the buyer's mailing address in the file so next year's bill finds them.

Selling for cash removes lender appraisals and repair demands. It does not remove the lien, which gets paid at the closing table in the same way.

Allen County at a glance

The county borders Tennessee. Scottsville is the seat and the only city. The 2020 census counted 20,588 people, and the July 2025 federal estimate is 22,536, up 9.5 percent. Housing units numbered 9,390 in 2025, and 74.5 percent of occupied homes are owned. Just 17 building permits were issued in 2025, which means buyers mostly choose among existing houses. US 231 is a four-lane parkway connecting Scottsville to Interstate 65, roughly 30 miles off.

Some county records burned in a 1902 courthouse fire, which can slow a title search on a very old parcel. For most sellers the smoothest closings come from a recorded deed that reads cleanly and a tax account showing nothing owed.

Frequently asked questions

Which Allen County office takes tax payments?

The sheriff takes them, as KRS 134.140 and 160.500 provide. Go to 194 W Wood St in Scottsville or call (270) 237-3210. The PVA only values property.

What is the penalty for paying Allen County taxes late?

January adds 5 percent and later months add 10 percent. After April 15 the clerk takes over the account, and interest of 1 percent monthly plus extra fees start accruing.

Is the Allen County homestead exemption automatic at age 65?

No. You must apply at the Allen County PVA. For 2025 and 2026 the amount is $49,100, and you need to be 65 or older or totally disabled.

I bought a house in Allen County after January 1. Who gets the tax bill?

The previous owner. Kentucky locks in ownership on January 1, so the bill carries that name. The PVA attempts to mail you a duplicate from the deed, and the sheriff can help if none arrives.

Can an Allen County tax lien block a sale?

Yes, it can stall a closing. KRS 134.420 keeps the lien on the parcel until payment or eleven years, and a buyer would inherit it. Get the sheriff's payoff figure and settle it at the table.

Selling in Anderson County?
We buy Anderson County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

Sheriff and PVA in Lawrenceburg

The Sheriff's counter at 208 S Main St takes the money, and its phone line, (502) 839-4021, answers weekdays from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. The Property Valuation Administrator, reachable at (502) 839-4061, sets the assessment that every bill is built on. Lawrenceburg is the only city, and the small places around it, Alton and McBrayer among them, use the same two offices.

The Sheriff mails bills in the final days of September and starts taking money on October 1. Mortgage companies no longer get mailed copies. A borrower who pays through escrow should ask the servicer in October whether it has the bill.

Owners near the Franklin County line can ask the PVA to confirm which county bills the parcel, since the boundary between the two was changed by a legislative act in 1854.

Discount, penalties and the April 15 cutoff

The Sheriff posts Kentucky's statewide schedule from KRS 134.015 on its tax page. The office accepts cash, checks and money orders only. It won't take installments, and a postmark earns nothing because the money must be in hand on the due date.

Bill stages at the Anderson County Sheriff
StageDatesEffect on the amount
EarlyOctober 1 to November 12 percent discount
Face amountNovember 2 to December 31The printed amount
First penaltyJanuary 1 to 31Five percent on top
Second penaltyFebruary 1 until the office closes April 15Ten percent, plus ten percent more as the Sheriff's fee

From February the Sheriff's add-on is figured on the tax plus the penalty, so the cost of waiting is steeper than the headline 10 percent suggests.

Once April 15 passes, collection moves to the County Clerk and the bill becomes a certificate of delinquency. Added costs are 20 percent for the County Attorney and 10 percent for the Clerk, plus interest of 1 percent monthly. Summer may bring a sale to an outside buyer.

What happens at the clerk's counter

The state revenue agency's model account starts from a $1,000 bill. Once the 10 percent penalty, the Sheriff's add-on and an assumed 4 percent commission are included, it reaches the clerk at $1,254. Paid within five business days it comes to $1,387.79, and after the county attorney's first notice, $1,611.30. Commission rates differ by county, so get a real payoff figure from the clerk.

The first letter goes out within a month of the handoff. KRS 134.128 puts the tax sale between 90 and 135 days after the transfer, with advertising in print and online.

The clerk's website has a delinquent tax lookup named DTax for accounts past April 15. What it shows is informational. The clerk sets the true figure at the moment of any sale, so an owner with an old balance needs a written payoff instead of a screen.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Anderson County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

A year in the life of an Anderson County bill

Everything starts on January 1, when value and ownership are locked in. Bills come out in late September, payment opens October 1, and the discount lasts to November 1. After that the printed amount holds through December, penalties step up in January and February, and the Sheriff's part ends April 15.

A spring sale doesn't change the name on that year's bill, which is whoever held title on January 1. How the year gets split between buyer and seller is a closing matter, so ask the agent. Owners who keep the house through the discount window pay least by settling in full before November 1.

Since installments are refused, plan one lump-sum payment. Mailing it close to a deadline is a gamble because a postmark doesn't count. Bring it to the counter on S Main Street, or ask the office how a mailed check is handled.

Contesting a valuation

Appeals follow a set sequence. Every assessment reflects the situation on January 1. The roll is open for 13 days beginning the first Monday of May. A conference with the PVA or a deputy comes first, and the County Clerk takes filings until the next day after inspection closes.

Roughly a month after inspection ends (25 to 35 days), the local appeals board sits for up to five days. Come with documents: descriptions of the land and buildings, insurance coverage, construction costs and comparable listings. A filing with nothing behind it loses. Skipping the hearing ends the appeal, and if the board sets a number higher than yours, a supplemental bill follows.

Homestead exemption

The PVA takes homestead applications from owners who have turned 65 and from owners classified as totally disabled. For 2025 and 2026 the state subtracts $49,100 from assessed value, a figure that is reset every other year.

Age is shown with a birth certificate, license or passport. A disability claim is renewed yearly unless the owner is a service-connected disabled veteran or has been found permanently and totally disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Anderson County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Is it worth appealing in a growing county?

An appeal makes sense when the roll shows a number well above what comparable houses nearby have sold for, or when the record describes features your house lacks. It makes less sense when the figure is close and you can't document a difference. Gather evidence first, then decide.

Anderson County had 23,852 residents in 2020, and the estimate for mid-2025 is 25,225. Houses follow people: the county held 10,652 housing units in July 2025, and builders took out 147 permits in 2025. Owners can compare their assessments with recent neighborhood sales before the roll opens.

  • Half of owner-occupied homes were valued above $225,100.
  • Households that own: 77.6 percent of 9,653.
  • Midpoint gross rent: $927.
  • Owners paid a median $1,391 a month with a mortgage and $411 without one.

Before the roll opens in May, pull together two or three recent sales of similar houses on your street and a few photos of anything in poor condition. Showing up with those turns an opinion into evidence, and the PVA can often fix a plain error at the conference without any hearing at all.

Someone who bought last year can list the deed price as next January's value if the home is unchanged.

Clearing back taxes before you sell

  1. The Sheriff can quote the live balance, with earlier years included. Past April 15, the Clerk holds that number.
  2. Your closing agent pays arrears from your share and files the release.
  3. The deed needs the buyer's tax bill address (KRS 382.135).
  4. A homestead exemption holder should let the PVA know about the sale.

Behind on taxes and not up for repairs? A written cash offer is one way out. Taxes and clerk charges come out of the price at closing, so the buyer gets a clean title and you keep what remains.

Frequently asked questions

Until what date does the discount last?

It ends on November 1. Anyone who pays the full bill by that day takes 2 percent off under KRS 134.015. From November 2 to December 31 you pay what is printed.

What happens if I wait until February?

From February 1 through April 15 the penalty is 10 percent, and the Sheriff adds a further 10 percent as a fee.

Can I pay in two halves?

No. Partial payments are not taken, and a check that arrives after the cutoff counts as late whatever its postmark.

Where does an objection to my value begin?

Call the PVA and request a conference. The clerk won't take an appeal without it, and the filing window shuts the workday after inspection ends.

How big is the homestead break?

It takes $49,100 off the assessed value for 2025 and 2026, and the PVA handles the paperwork.

Who does what with a Boyle County tax bill

Three desks touch your bill. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA), at 859-238-1104, decides what the property is worth for tax purposes and handles exemptions. The Sheriff's Office, at 321 W. Main Street, Room 103 in Danville (859-238-1123), mails the bills and takes payment. The County Clerk inherits any bill still open after the spring cutoff.

Valuing is never the sheriff's job. If the bill looks too large, talk to the PVA, and do it before you mail a check.

  • Value, exemptions, name or mailing address on the bill: PVA.
  • Paying this year's bill or looking it up: Sheriff's Office.
  • Bills from prior years: County Clerk.

Boyle County market snapshot

Danville is the county seat, and Boyle County wraps around it in central Kentucky, with Junction City and Perryville as the other cities. The July 2025 population estimate is 31,632, up from 30,614 at the 2020 count. Owner-occupied houses are valued around $209,900 at the midpoint, and 68.0 percent of homes are owner-occupied. Typical rent is $778, and the county logged 94 building permits in 2025. That mix of steady demand and modest new construction is the market a seller faces.

Due dates and penalties

Five cutoffs apply to each tax year. Below is the sheriff's schedule for the 2026 bills, where a postmark on or before the listed date counts.

Boyle County Sheriff's schedule for the 2026 bills
Paid or postmarked byAmount owed

Every year repeats this pattern with the dates moved forward. The sheriff's Tax Bill Web Portal looks up bills by bill number, map number, owner or address. Searches by owner sometimes fail on reversed names, so try the last name first as well as the first name first.

Which school district bills Danville properties?

The answer changes from street to street. Danville Schools serve the city and Boyle County Schools serve the rest, yet some parcels within city limits belong to the county district. A Danville mailing address alone tells you nothing.

A parcel in the Danville Independent district gets its school bill straight from the school system at 859-936-8507. A parcel in the county district has school tax folded into the sheriff's bill. Library, health, fire and similar special districts show up as extra lines where they apply.

Danville city tax rate

Danville's 2025 real property rate is 11.9 cents on each $100 of assessed value, down from 14.4 cents in 2017. The city says it has taken the compensating rate every year since 2017, so the rate slid while assessments grew.

  • Real property: 0.1190 in 2025, 0.1220 in 2024, 0.1440 in 2017.
  • Tangible personal property: 0.1595 in 2025.
  • Cars, trucks and boats: 0.2000 in 2025.

House Bill 44 lets a city hold revenue level with the compensating rate or raise it by up to 4 percent after a hearing. Past 4 percent, voters can petition to recall the increase. Your dollar total can still climb if the PVA raises the assessed value under a lower rate.

Can I contest my Boyle County assessment?

You can, though the PVA conference has to happen first and the state gives no shortcut. Property is valued as of January 1, and the public may inspect the roll for thirteen days in early May. Once the conference is over, take your appeal to the County Clerk before the workday ends on the day after inspection closes.

The county's board of assessment appeals meets roughly a month afterward and can sit up to five days. Arrive with proof, such as comparable sales, an appraisal, repair bids, insurance values or listings, because an appeal without it fails. Skip the local filing and the Kentucky Claims Commission is off the table.

When the bills are printed before your dispute is settled, they use the value you claimed. A supplemental bill follows if the board sets it higher.

Kentucky homestead exemption

Homeowners who are 65 or older, or whom a public or private retirement system has classed as totally disabled, get a fixed deduction from the assessment on their residence. It tops out at $49,100 through the 2026 tax year. Both ownership and residence must be true on January 1.

Send the application to the Boyle County PVA, the same office Danville points seniors toward. Get it in before December 31. Qualified but no exemption on the bill? Phone the PVA first, then pay.

Reading the lines on your bill

A Boyle County bill can hold more than one charge, and each has a different office behind it. County school tax is included on the sheriff's bill for parcels in the county district. Danville parcels in the independent district see their school charge come separately. Fire, library, health and other special districts appear as extra lines where they apply, and Danville city tax is figured at its own rate.

If a line looks wrong, ask which office set it. Value and exemption questions go to the PVA at 859-238-1104. Questions about the amount owed or the payment period go to the sheriff at 859-238-1123. Sorting that out early keeps a mistake from following you to the closing table, where the title company needs the numbers to be right.

When a Boyle County bill goes unpaid

Past April 15 the sheriff lets go of the bill. It turns into a certificate of delinquency held by the clerk, with a lien on the property. One percent interest is added each month, and commissions for the clerk and county attorney, postage and advertising stack on top. Within a week at the clerk's desk, the balance is well above what the sheriff would have taken.

Letters from the county attorney arrive at about 30 and 60 days. Unpaid certificates may be sold to outside buyers anywhere from 90 to 135 days after the handoff. If you are selling with old tax owing, request a payoff from the clerk and let the closing agent pay it out of your proceeds.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What happens to the tax bill when you sell?

Kentucky bills whoever holds title on January 1. If your house changes hands in March, that year's bill still comes in your name. Closing agents normally split the year between buyer and seller on the settlement statement, then either pay the sheriff or credit whoever will. A lender with an escrow account does not get the bill automatically, so owners should forward it.

  1. Get the current figure from the sheriff.
  2. Get any older figure from the clerk.
  3. Give both to the closing agent before the closing date.
  4. Confirm on the settlement statement who pays and who gets a credit.

Houses that arrive through an estate, carry back taxes, or need repairs a retail buyer would balk at can sell directly to a cash buyer, who clears the tax at the same table.

Frequently asked questions

Whom should I phone if my Boyle County assessment looks too high?

The PVA at 859-238-1104. The sheriff only collects, and the clerk handles appeal filings.

Is the Boyle County 2% discount still available after November?

No. On the 2026 bills the discount runs through November 30, 2026. December brings the face amount and January adds a 5 percent penalty.

Do Danville homeowners get one tax bill or two?

It varies. Parcels in the Danville Independent district get a separate school bill, while everything else, including Boyle County school tax, comes on the sheriff's bill.

What is the Kentucky homestead exemption worth?

Up to $49,100 off the assessment through the 2026 tax year, for owner-occupants who are 65 or older or totally disabled.

Can I sell a Boyle County house that has unpaid property tax?

Yes. Get a payoff from the clerk for past-due years and a current figure from the sheriff, and the closing agent can pay both at closing.

Which offices handle Grant County property tax

A Grant County tax bill passes through three counters. The PVA decides what each parcel is worth. The sheriff takes payment on the current year. The county clerk takes over whatever bills remain after mid-April. Rates come from the levying bodies themselves: the fiscal court, the school system, and any city or special district that taxes the parcel.

The PVA keeps an office in the Williamstown courthouse, 101 North Main Street, and the phone is (859) 824-6511. The sheriff works from 212 Barnes Road, Suite A, weekdays from 8 to 4, and answers at (859) 824-3333. Checks can be mailed to PO Box 235, Dry Ridge, KY 41035. For delinquent bills, call the clerk at (859) 824-3321.

City tax bills never go through the sheriff. Williamstown, Dry Ridge, Corinth and Crittenden each bill their own, so a municipal charge on a closing statement is a question for that city hall.

Payment calendar and penalties

The sheriff mails bills and posts them online on October 1, then takes payment until April 15. Splitting a bill into two installments is not allowed. Cards work, with a processing charge from the card company, and a mail-in payer who wants a receipt encloses a stamped return envelope.

Why the bill arrives in the seller's name

The sheriff bills whoever was listed as owner on January 1. Buy in spring and the year's first bill still carries the previous owner's name. Deed transfers never reach the sheriff, which leaves the seller to pass the bill on.

How to appeal your assessment

Nobody can file an appeal without first sitting down with the PVA or a deputy, which makes that office your first stop. Then comes a 13-day public viewing of the roll, starting the first Monday of May.

  • At the conference, the PVA walks through the method behind your value and keeps a written record.
  • Hand the written appeal to the Clerk before the office closes on the workday after the viewing period ends.
  • Collect proof: nearby sales, contractor bids, photos of damage, insurance papers, cost of construction.
  • Attend the board hearing, which falls within five weeks of the window closing. A no-show forfeits further review by the state Claims Commission.

An appeal without documents is denied by the board. Should bills go out before the board decides, your own figure is billed for now. A higher final value brings a second bill for the difference.

Steps for a seller before closing

Treat the tax bill as a closing item, not an afterthought. A short order of operations keeps the sale on schedule.

  1. Check which bills attach to the address: the county bill from the sheriff and, inside Williamstown, Dry Ridge, Corinth or Crittenden, a separate city bill.

For 2025-2026, owners who have reached 65 or are totally disabled may deduct $49,100 from the assessment.

Applications are made at the PVA, and the sheriff's office refers anyone asking about it there. A birth certificate, driver's license or passport proves age. Disability filers renew yearly, with two groups spared that chore: owners rated with a service-connected military disability, and anyone holding a permanent-disability finding from Social Security or the state retirement system.

Notify the PVA at sale so the deduction leaves your old address, and a qualifying buyer can apply separately.

Selling with unpaid taxes

Back taxes ride with the parcel. The sheriff deals only with the current year, so a bill that crosses April 15 lands with the Clerk, and a lien is recorded against the property. A buyer inherits the lien, which can last 11 years (KRS 134.420).

Costs climb in steps. The bill arrives at the Clerk as a certificate carrying the penalty and sheriff's add-on. Monthly interest, two commissions, postage and a $10 lien fee pile on after that, and the county attorney's first notice raises the payoff again.

An auction of the certificate can happen from day 90 to day 135 after transfer, and the winning bidder may tack on charges. Get a Clerk's quote on the payoff before the sign goes up. With a cash buyer, the lien is paid at closing out of the price.

A short order of steps helps. Ask the Clerk at (859) 824-3321 for the payoff, give it to your title agent, and keep the receipt once the balance is cleared. A buyer's title company will not insure over an open lien.

Grant County housing and the market

Grant County lies in northern Kentucky inside the Cincinnati metropolitan area. Williamstown holds the courthouse, while Dry Ridge, Corinth and Crittenden complete the list of cities. Growth is the main story here. Population is 26,181, which is 5.0 percent above the 2020 base. Homeowners make up 75.1 percent of households, and the median home value is $209,500. Median gross rent is $862, and 110 building permits were issued in 2025.

A cash purchase closes as-is, which can suit an owner with repairs waiting or a balance outstanding. It also avoids a lender's appraisal, so the closing date depends mostly on the title search and the payoff figure from the Clerk or sheriff.

Frequently asked questions

Who takes property tax payments in Grant County, KY?

The sheriff's office handles it, either at 212 Barnes Road, Suite A in Williamstown or through the mail to PO Box 235, Dry Ridge. After April 15, the County Clerk collects.

When does the Grant County early-payment discount end?

On November 1. Paying the whole bill from October 1 through that day takes two percent off, and face value applies from November 2.

Can a Grant County tax bill be paid in two installments?

No. The sheriff requires full payment of each bill, so pick a payment window you can cover in one go.

What does the homestead deduction take off a Grant County house?

It removes $49,100 from the assessment for 2025-2026. Filing is with the PVA at (859) 824-6511, and the owner must be 65 or older or totally disabled.

Must back taxes be settled before I list a Grant County house?

They can wait. The lien follows the parcel and is settled from the sale proceeds. Call the Clerk at (859) 824-3321 for the amount so your title agent can plan.

Leitchfield is both the seat and the largest city of this rural west central Kentucky county. Residents numbered 27,406 in July 2025, a 3.7 percent gain over April 2020. On November 30, 2026. The sheriff's schedule starts the discount on November 1, then shows the face amount for December and a 5 percent penalty in January 2027.

No. The office wants the whole bill at once and refuses partial payments. If a lender escrows your taxes, it can send the full amount for you.

With the County Clerk at (270) 259-5295. Real property bills still open on that date move to the clerk, who quotes the payoff including interest and commissions.

Transfer tax on a sale

The seller pays a Kentucky levy of $0.50 on each $500 of price, or part of $500. The clerk takes the money first and records afterward (KRS 142.050). The clerk's office on Main Street in Munfordville holds the county's land records, so call (270) 524-2751 for the current recording charge.

Paying the sheriff

The sheriff is the collector, and the online payment page at hartcountysheriffky.com is the quickest route. You can also go to the office at 100 Main Street, or call (270) 524-2341 to ask how the office handles mailed checks. Because the sheriff may take part payments, an owner who is short of cash can chip away at a bill, but the 2 percent discount applies only when the bill is paid whole on or before November 1.

Anyone can pay on the owner's behalf. A relative, a tenant or a lender can send the money, which helps if you are selling from out of town or an heir is settling an estate. Keep the receipt, because the title company may ask for proof that the year is paid.

What the PVA does before and after a sale

The PVA's job ends at valuation, but its records drive everything else. It keeps the name of the January 1 owner, the assessed value and the exemption file. After you sell, the office needs to learn about the transfer so the old homestead deduction stops and the new owner's bill goes to the right address. The clerk records the deed, and the PVA picks up the change from that record, so the sooner the deed is recorded, the sooner the files match.

If you disagree with a value while a sale is pending, remember the appeal route is slow. The board meets between 25 and 35 days after inspection ends, so an appeal will rarely finish before a quick closing. Plan to settle the bill as it stands and sort out any difference with the buyer in the contract.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Before you list

A quick sequence keeps tax questions from slowing the sale. Check the bill with the sheriff and confirm whether this year is paid. Ask the PVA who is listed as owner and whether your homestead deduction is on file. Ask the clerk what recorded papers exist for the parcel, especially on an older farm. Decide with the buyer who will pay the current bill, and put that on the settlement statement.

If you are paying near the November 1 cutoff, a closing that finishes before then lets the full-payment discount still apply to the bill. A closing after January means the 5 percent or 10 percent add-on may already be on it.

Frequently asked questions

Which office mails the Hart County tax bill?

The sheriff, at (270) 524-2341. The PVA supplies the value, and the clerk picks up claims the sheriff could not collect.

How large is the homestead deduction for Hart County owners?

$49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years. It goes to owners over 65 or totally disabled who apply with the PVA at (270) 524-2321.

Does Hart County reward early payment?

Yes. Paying the whole bill by November 1 cuts it 2 percent. Missing December 31 adds 5 percent through January and 10 percent after that.

Do I stop paying while my Hart County appeal is pending?

No. Meanwhile you owe tax on the figure you claimed, and a higher ruling brings a second bill with interest.

Can a Hart County house with back taxes be sold?

Yes, with the debt settled at closing. Obtain a payoff from the sheriff and have the title company send it from your proceeds.

Paying your Ohio County tax bill

Walk-in payments are accepted at the sheriff's tax office, 301 South Main Street, Hartford. If you would rather mail a check, address it to PO Box 186, Hartford, KY 42347. The phone line is 270-298-4444.

The counter opens at 8 a.m. and closes at 4 p.m. Monday through Friday. On the first and last Saturday of every month it is open until noon. A drop box hangs on the door for evenings and weekends. Mailed checks are honored by postmark, but never mail cash. A card works at the counter, and the sheriff's website has an online payment link. Refunds, for instance after an assessment is corrected, are mailed once a month near the end of the month, and refund questions go to the same phone line.

Values are not the sheriff's job. Questions about an assessment, the address on a bill or an exemption belong with the Property Valuation Administrator (PVA), 270-298-4433.

What Ohio County looks like for a seller

Land stretches a long way in Ohio County and people are spread thin. Hartford is the seat, Beaver Dam is the biggest town, prices are modest and almost nothing new gets built, so listings are nearly all resales. Population is 23,934 for July 2025, up 0.7 percent from April 2020.

  • A typical owned house is worth $121,400, and owners with a mortgage spend $1,105 a month on housing.
  • Of the 9,107 households, 77.2 percent own.
  • Household income is $57,798 at the midpoint.
  • The county has 10,377 housing units and issued just 3 building permits in 2025.
  • Rent at the midpoint is $739 monthly.

With so little turnover, pricing can be hard. A house in Fordsville, Rockport or McHenry often has fewer nearby sales to compare against than one in Beaver Dam, so lean on recent closed sales and a good photo record of repairs.

Payment periods and penalties

Bills become payable on October 1, and the assessment date behind every bill is January 1. This is the calendar the sheriff follows.

Ohio County collection calendar
DatesAmount due
October 1 to November 1Bill less 2 percent
November 2 to December 31Face amount
January 1 to 31Face amount plus 5 percent
February 1 to April 15Face amount plus 21 percent
After April 15Bill transfers to the County Clerk

State law, in KRS 134.015, names a 10 percent charge for the late period, so ask the tax office to price your parcel exactly before you send a check.

Still no bill around October 10? Phone the tax office and ask for a duplicate, which can come by mail, fax or email. Sending one to a different address is a favor, not a change of record. Only the PVA updates the mailing address on file.

What happens to bills left unpaid on April 15?

Prior-year payments leave the sheriff on April 15 and go to the Ohio County Clerk at 301 S Main St, Suite 201 in Hartford (weekdays 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.; recording desk 270-298-4423). The clerk's delinquent tax page lists the sale date, so call for the next one.

  • The bill becomes a recorded lien, and 1 percent interest is added each month.
  • Large-scale bidders (over three certificates here, five statewide or $10,000 in total) register with the state first.
  • A listed house with a certificate needs a written payoff from the clerk, since the balance grows each month.

Clearing the balance early is cheaper. After an investor buys the certificate, the debt is owed to that investor with extra fees on top.

How to contest your value

Your first call goes to the PVA, 270-298-4433, and the required conference must take place while spring inspection is still open. Bring comparable sales, repair estimates and photos. If the conference fails, the next stops are a form at the County Clerk, then a local three-person board, then the state Board of Tax Appeals. The PVA appeal guide spells out each deadline, including 30 days to reach the state board.

Do not hold back payment during an appeal. If the value drops, the difference comes back as a refund.

A year in the life of an Ohio County bill

Here is the full cycle. Value and ownership are fixed as of January 1. Bills become payable October 1, and the discount window shuts November 1. The face amount holds until the end of December, then penalties begin in January and step up in February. By April 15 anything still owed has left the sheriff's hands.

For a seller, that rhythm decides who pays what. A spring seller still owes the year's bill, since the house was theirs on January 1, and normally gets repaid by the buyer for the later months. A fall seller should check whether the 2 percent discount applies before the bill goes out the door. Whichever season you sell in, bring the most recent receipt to the closing agent along with the sheriff's phone number.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Ohio County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Exemptions and farm land

Residents who are 65 or older, or totally disabled, can claim the homestead exemption. A 70 percent VA rating or a 100 percent Social Security disability finding can also qualify, and the PVA decides each claim. It takes a set dollar amount off the assessed value, revised on a two-year cycle, and the next owner starts a new application.

Working farmland is taxed on what the land earns from farming, not on market price. In a county where 76 percent of residents live in rural areas, that can matter a great deal, so ask the PVA about any tract you plan to sell or split.

What a seller owes besides the tax bill

Kentucky's transfer tax lands on the seller. KRS 142.050 sets it at 50 cents for each $500 of declared value, rounding up, and the clerk wants it paid before the deed is accepted.

  • Ask the sheriff whether this year's bill is paid and by whom.
  • Check with the clerk for liens or certificates on record.
  • List a mailing address for future tax bills in the deed, which KRS 382.135 requires.

Any closing after January 1 leaves that year's bill in your name, so divide it in the contract and save the receipt.

Selling a house that has tax problems

You can sell with taxes unpaid. The title company subtracts what is owed from your proceeds. Before April 15 the sheriff gives you the figure, and after it the County Clerk does. Work through it in this order.

  1. Ask the right office for a written payoff that stays valid through closing.
  2. Pass the number to the title company.
  3. Make sure the clerk shows any lien as released.
  4. File the receipts.

Selling for cash avoids a lender's appraisal and repair demands, which suits an older house. The tax payoff still gets made at closing. Self-employed owners and heirs with a vacant property should also check that nothing is recorded against the parcel before choosing a closing date.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Where do I pay Ohio County property tax?

At the sheriff's tax office, 301 South Main Street in Hartford, or by check to PO Box 186, Hartford, KY 42347.

When does a penalty begin on an Ohio County property tax bill?

January 1 starts it, with 5 percent added through the end of that month. Payments from November 2 to December 31 cost only the face amount.

Can a house with an unpaid tax bill still be sold?

Yes. The balance is paid from your sale proceeds, based on a quote from the sheriff before April 15 or the County Clerk once that date is past.

Whom do I call to question my Ohio County valuation?

The PVA, 270-298-4433. Values are outside the sheriff's authority.

Who pays the transfer tax on an Ohio County sale?

The seller does, at 50 cents per $500 of the price on the deed, rounded up. The clerk collects it first.

Which offices handle Boyd County property tax

Three offices share the job. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) sets values. The Sheriff's Office bills and collects the current year. The County Clerk picks up older delinquent bills.

The PVA values all real and personal property in the county, except items the Kentucky Department of Revenue assigns itself, such as public service companies, bank shares and vehicles. Mail for the PVA goes to PO Box 434, Catlettsburg, KY 41129. For a house, the PVA's number is where everything else on your bill begins.

Boyd County housing and tax base

Boyd County covers about 160 square miles with roughly 300 residents per square mile. The 2025 population estimate is 47,751 in about 21,818 housing units. The typical owner-occupied home is valued at $130,700, the typical household earns $61,118, and owners live in 70.2% of homes. Owner costs run $1,217 a month with a mortgage and $463 without one.

A house near that value carries a smaller assessment than most Bluegrass homes, but the 911 fee and city levies still show up on the bill.

  • Ashland and Catlettsburg bill their own city property tax, so call the city, not the county, with questions about it.
  • The county bill carries a 911 service fee, and Boyd County 911 at 606-329-2191 answers questions about it.

Due dates and penalties

The Sheriff's Office follows the calendar in KRS 134.015. Paying early earns a discount, the middle stretch is flat, and two penalty steps come after.

Payment schedule applied by the Boyd County Sheriff
When you payDiscount or penalty
By November 12% discount
November 2 to December 31Face amount, no penalty
January 1 to January 315% penalty
After January 3110% penalty

You can view and pay your bill online through the Sheriff's Office. The dates printed on a bill can run later than the statute's calendar when the state allows an alternative collection schedule, so read your bill and ask the sheriff's office which dates apply to your parcel. When the sheriff's collection period ends, unpaid prior year taxes move to the County Clerk at 606-739-5116, option 4.

How to contest a Boyd County assessment

Start with the PVA. Value is fixed as of January 1, and whenever a property's value goes up from the year before, the PVA mails the owner a notice of change. That notice is your cue to look at the number closely, since the conference window is short.

Your first step is a conference with the PVA or a deputy. The window is six days a week for two weeks, starting the first Monday in May, though dates can shift. If you leave without agreement, a written petition to the County Clerk earns you a hearing before the board of assessment appeals, as KRS 133.120 provides.

  • Bring comparable sales, an appraisal, photos of damage or a contractor's repair estimate.
  • Ask to hold the conference by phone if a visit is hard.
  • The petition must state your reasons and your opinion of the property's fair cash value.
  • Keep paying while you appeal, since an appeal does not hold up the tax.

Does Boyd County have a homestead exemption?

Yes, the statewide one, for owners who reach 65 or are classed as totally disabled. For the two years covering 2025 and 2026 the deduction is $49,100.

File with the Boyd County PVA. A birth certificate, driver's license or passport proves your age. A disability claim needs proof of a total-disability classification from a federal or retirement program, and it is refiled yearly unless the owner has a service-connected disability or has been found permanently disabled.

For an owner on a fixed income, the exemption and an on-time payment in the discount window can matter more than a small change in value. Before listing, ask the PVA whether an exemption application is on file.

Key dates in the assessment year

  • January 1: the assessment date for every property.
  • First Monday in May: the roll inspection period normally opens and PVA conferences begin.
  • Third Monday in May: the inspection period normally ends, and the written petition follows within a workday.
  • November 1: the last day for the 2% discount.
  • December 31: the last day to pay the plain face amount.
  • January 31: the last day before the 10% penalty.

A notice on the county's tax page announces when each year's collection begins. The dates printed on your own bill win, since the state can set an alternative schedule.

Who can speak for me in an appeal?

You can appear yourself or send an agent. Kentucky law limits who may be paid to represent an owner at a PVA conference or a board hearing.

  • An attorney or a certified public accountant.
  • A tax consultant, or a real estate broker or sales associate who holds a Kentucky license.
  • An employee of the property owner.
  • A real property appraiser who holds a Kentucky license or certification.

An agent needs your written authorization and must disclose any personal stake, such as a contingency fee. Losing at the county board leaves one more stop, the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals, and only owners who went to the county board first may use it.

What a late payment costs

The statute's calendar makes the cost easy to see in percentages. Pay by November 1 and you get 2% off. Pay from November 2 through December 31 and you owe the face amount. January adds a 5% penalty, and after January 31 the statutory penalty is 10%. Extra charges can attach once a bill moves to the clerk, so get a payoff figure from that office before closing.

Your own bill carries county, school and district amounts plus the 911 fee, and the Sheriff's Office can give you the exact total for your parcel.

Steps for a seller before listing

A short checklist keeps the tax side of a sale from surprising you.

  1. Find your latest bill and check which dates apply to your parcel.
  2. Ask the Sheriff's Office whether this year is paid in full.
  3. Call the County Clerk at 606-739-5116, option 4, if any earlier year is still open.
  4. Phone the city if you live in Ashland or Catlettsburg and ask whether a city bill is outstanding.
  5. Ask the PVA whether your value changed and whether a homestead exemption is on file.
  6. Hand your closing agent the payoff figures so nothing is found late.

Doing this before the first showing means no tax question is left to hold up the contract.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Selling a Boyd County house with taxes owed

Delinquent tax attaches to the house as a lien, and the debt itself belongs to the owner as of the assessment date. A title company will want any unpaid bill cleared at closing.

  • This year's bill unpaid: the Sheriff's Office gives the exact amount.
  • An older year unpaid: the County Clerk's office quotes it.
  • City tax questions: City of Ashland, 606-385-3275, or City of Catlettsburg, 606-739-5223.
  • Escrow: ask the lender whether it has already paid.

If you cannot pay beforehand, ask the closing agent to deduct it from your sale proceeds. A cash buyer or an ordinary buyer both expect the same thing: a bill that is paid or a payoff figure the title company can read.

Frequently asked questions

Who collects property tax in Boyd County?

The Boyd County Sheriff's Office collects the current year's tax. The County Clerk collects delinquent taxes from prior years.

What is the Boyd County property tax discount?

KRS 134.015 allows 2% off for payment in full by November 1, then the plain amount until December 31. The dates printed on your bill control.

How do I pay delinquent Boyd County property taxes?

Call the Boyd County Clerk's office at 606-739-5116 and press option 4, or use the clerk's website.

When can I meet with the Boyd County PVA about my assessment?

Before the roll inspection window ends. It normally opens the first Monday in May and closes the third Monday.

Do Ashland and Catlettsburg charge their own property tax?

Yes. Questions about city property tax go to the City of Ashland at 606-385-3275 or the City of Catlettsburg at 606-739-5223.

Breckinridge County for homeowners

Western Kentucky's Breckinridge County follows the Ohio River across 586 square miles, which makes it large and sparsely settled at 35.9 people per square mile. Hardinsburg is the largest city and the seat, joined by Cloverport and Irvington. About 21,503 people lived here in 2025, a 5.2 percent gain on the 2020 count.

Owners hold 81.4 percent of the housing units, and the middle value of an owner's home is $156,700. Rent in the middle is $733 a month. Monthly owner costs in the middle come to $1,210 with a mortgage and $377 without. Builders pulled only 14 permits for 2025, which leaves resale houses with little new competition.

Breckinridge keeps Central time, but Meade and Hardin counties to the east keep Eastern time. When a closing involves offices on both sides, confirm which clock each office uses.

Which office does what

The sheriff bills and collects, the PVA values property, and the county clerk takes over unpaid bills.

Breckinridge County tax offices
OfficeContactUse it for
Sheriff's Office, 208 South Main Street, Suite 210, Hardinsburg270-756-2361, PO Box 127, weekdays eight to four CentralPaying and looking up the current bill

Payment dates and penalties

Bills are mailed in late October. If yours has not come by early November, ask the sheriff for a duplicate. Online lookup and payment run from November 1 through 4 p.m. Central on April 15, and postmarks count.

The sheriff's stages on the 2026 bills run like this:

  • November 1 to 30: face amount less 2%.
  • December 1 to 31: face amount.
  • January 1 to 31: face amount plus 5%.
  • February 1 to April 15: face amount plus 21%.
  • After April 15: pay at the County Clerk's office.

The sheriff cannot bend any of this, because statute and the Revenue Cabinet set the dates and percentages.

How paying a Breckinridge County bill works

Send the exact amount printed on the bill and nothing less. A short payment comes back in the mail, and the sheriff offers no installment plan. One payment can cover several bills at once.

  • Online: a processing fee of 1.5 percent, minimum $1.50, applies on the first $60, and 2.5 percent on anything over $60. Visa, Mastercard, Discover and eCheck work.
  • Mail or counter: a check or money order with the voucher.
  • Fire dues: a signed opt-out form has to accompany the payment, so owners opting out pay by mail or at the counter.

The cancelled check serves as your receipt. If you want a receipt for a mailed payment, enclose a stamped, addressed envelope.

Getting your bill and paying on time

Mailing wraps up in late October. If yours is missing in early November, ask the sheriff for a duplicate rather than waiting. Online lookup and payment open November 1 and stay open until 4 p.m. Central on April 15, so a seller who is away can still pay without a trip to Hardinsburg.

For an in-person visit, the office at 208 South Main Street is open weekdays from eight to four Central. Bring the voucher from the bill. Pay by check or money order, and write the parcel details on the check if you have more than one bill.

Pick your window from the stages above. November takes 2% off, December costs the plain amount, and every later month costs more until the County Clerk takes over.

Before you sign a listing agreement

Taxes touch a sale in a few places, and each one has a person to call. The PVA's number settles what the home is worth on paper. The sheriff settles whether this year's bill is current. The clerk settles anything older. A title company will look at all three before a closing, and it is easier to learn the answers yourself while there is still time to act.

If your valuation looks too high, remember the dispute window opens only in early May. A seller who waits until the house is under contract has usually missed the chance to change that year's number.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Breckinridge County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Taxes when a Breckinridge County house sells

The bill is made out to whoever owned on January 1. Selling after that date still leaves the bill in your name, and you pass it to the new owner. The closing agent usually allocates each side's portion on the settlement statement.

Two prorated checks will not be accepted. Either you or the buyer pays the whole bill, so ask the closing attorney who will carry the payment and whether a credit goes to the buyer.

How an owner disputes a valuation

The PVA values property as of January 1 and sends crews back to each parcel about every four years. When a new number looks wrong, book a conference with the PVA during the inspection period, which starts in early May and runs thirteen days.

A filing with the county clerk, who acts as clerk to the local appeals board, is allowed only after that conference. The board convenes roughly a month after inspection ends. Boards rule on paper, so bring photos, a repair bid, an appraisal or comparable sales. An appeal without them is denied.

Senior and disability exemption

If you are 65 or older, or classed as totally disabled, you may claim the homestead exemption on the house where you live, worth up to $49,100 through the 2026 tax year. Every exemption question goes to the PVA, and a heavy-feeling bill is a good reason to check on one first.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Unpaid Breckinridge County property tax

A bill is delinquent after April 15, or after the tax day set for that year, and extra penalties may apply. The sheriff lets it go and it reappears at the clerk's office as delinquent, with a lien on the property. One percent interest starts each month, clerk and county attorney commissions follow, and notices and advertising come before any sale.

The Department of Revenue posts each county's delinquent list online by June 1, and on a normal schedule a sale can fall between July 14 and August 28. A third party can buy a bill that reaches the sale list.

Anyone selling a house here with old tax owing should order the payoff before closing so the title company can pay it from the sale.

A seller's checklist

  1. Call the sheriff at 270-756-2361 and ask whether the current bill is paid.
  2. Call the County Clerk at 270-756-2246 for any past-due bill and a payoff figure.
  3. Ask the PVA at 270-756-5154 whether an exemption is on file and whether the value has changed.
  4. Tell the closing attorney who will pay the full bill and whether the buyer gets a credit.
  5. Forward the bill to your lender if it pays from escrow.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Breckinridge County sheriff's tax office address?

208 South Main Street, Suite 210, Hardinsburg, KY 40143. Payments by mail go to PO Box 127, and the phone is 270-756-2361.

Can I pay Breckinridge County property tax online?

Yes, starting November 1. A convenience fee applies, and the payment must equal the exact bill amount.

Can I pay Breckinridge County property tax in installments?

No. The sheriff accepts the full amount shown on the bill, though one payment can cover several bills.

When does the 21 percent penalty start in Breckinridge County?

On February 1, and it runs through April 15. After that the bill goes to the County Clerk as delinquent.

Who pays the tax on a Breckinridge County house I sold in June?

The January 1 owner is billed. The closing agent usually prorates the year, but the sheriff still needs the whole bill paid at once.

Which Garrard County office answers which tax question

Value is the PVA's job and the bill is the sheriff's. The PVA does not set rates or collect money, and the sheriff does not assess property, so an argument over the figure goes to one office and a question about paying goes to the other.

Both offices are at 319 Stanford St. in Lancaster. Call the PVA at (859) 792-3291 on weekdays between 8 and 4, or the sheriff at (859) 792-3591. The PVA is a state-supervised office with a local address, and its valuation standard is full fair cash value on each January 1.

Twenty-eight taxing districts are collected by the sheriff, covering state and county levies, school districts, and special districts for fire protection, libraries and similar services. Each October 1 the bills go out with instructions on due dates, penalties, mortgage-company payment and ways to pay. The County Clerk, at 15 Public Square, Suite 5, records deeds and helps notify and collect on delinquent bills.

Garrard County housing and the local market

East-central Kentucky holds Garrard County, mostly rolling Bluegrass farmland, with the Knobs in the southeast corner near Cartersville. Lancaster is the seat and only city, about 28 miles south of Lexington, and the average commute runs 33.1 minutes. Every resident was classed as rural in 2020.

  • Population: 18,207 in the 2025 estimate, up 7.4 percent from 2020.
  • Typical home value: $204,900 in the 2020 to 2024 survey.
  • Homes lived in by their owners: 79.9 percent.
  • New-home permits in 2025: 0.
  • Rent runs a median $794 gross, and household income a median $63,087.

In 2020 there were 7,254 housing units, 9.2 percent of them empty, and 6,584 households. No permits were recorded in 2025, so sales are mostly existing houses and acreage. Buyers of older farmhouses and acreage often ask about the tax record early, so keep last year's receipt and this year's bill together in one folder for showings and for the closing agent.

Due dates and the early-payment discount

The bill is mailed October 1 and falls due December 31, so the discount window lasts about a month. Under KRS 134.015, a bill settled in full by November 1 drops 2 percent. A January payment carries 5 percent extra, and each payment after that carries 10 percent.

If mailing runs late statewide, Revenue can swap in a short calendar of a month with the discount, a month at face, then a month with the 5 percent charge. The January 1 owner is personally liable for that year's tax, so a closing early in the year needs a clear agreement about the bill.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Garrard County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What a late bill costs

Come April 15 the sheriff hands off unpaid bills to the County Clerk, and a lien goes on record against the parcel. Penalties and commissions stack up quickly from there, and each step adds cost for whoever owns the parcel.

How an open Garrard County bill moves through the year
WhenWhat happens to the bill
October 1Sheriff mails the bill
Through November 1Full payment earns the 2 percent discount
November 2 to December 31Face amount is due
JanuaryAn extra 5 percent applies
After JanuaryAn extra 10 percent applies
April 15County Clerk receives the bill and records a lien
Weeks after transferInterest, county attorney letters, then the clerk's sale 90 to 135 days after transfer

Interest builds at 1 percent monthly. A 30-day notice and a second notice come from the county attorney. When a certificate sells to an outside buyer, you owe that buyer plus its additional fees.

Taxes before closing

Make the tax bill part of the sale paperwork. The sheriff mails bills in October, and the debt belongs to the January 1 owner, so a house that closes in spring or summer may still have a bill outstanding in the seller's name.

  • Phone the sheriff's office at (859) 792-3591 for the amount due on the parcel.
  • Ask the County Clerk at (859) 792-3071 how to record the deed, since the clerk's office archives deeds and mortgages.
  • Tell the PVA at (859) 792-3291 who the new owner is so later notices and any exemption follow the right person.
  • Keep the paid receipt with your closing file, because the buyer's title search will otherwise show the balance as open.

Owners who are behind on taxes and facing repairs on an older farmhouse may weigh a direct sale to a buyer that closes as-is. That route avoids carrying the bill through a long listing. With cash there is no lender appraisal or repair list, and the tax payoff is taken from the price at closing. Get the payoff figure in writing so the title company has a firm number.

What the title company checks

Once a Garrard County house is under contract, the title company hunts for open taxes at the sheriff and the clerk. A paid current bill is settled by a receipt. An open one is listed on the settlement statement and paid from the seller's proceeds. If the bill slipped past April 15, the lien sits in the clerk's records, and the title company will want the clerk's payoff instead of the sheriff's.

The timing of your sale decides who is on the hook. A sale before the October 1 mailing leaves the current year's bill to be split in the contract, because it will arrive in the seller's name for the January 1 ownership. A sale after the bill is mailed is simpler: pay the sheriff and file the receipt. Either way, give the PVA the buyer's mailing address after closing so notices stop coming to you.

How to appeal your assessment

Start with a PVA conference. After that, file your appeal at the County Clerk's office. Viewing of the roll runs 13 days from early May. The clerk wants the appeal by the next business day after that ends.

A local review board meets roughly four to five weeks after that. It decides on documents such as comparable listings, construction costs and photographs, and it must put its reasons for any change in writing. A paid representative has to be an attorney, appraiser or another approved professional and must carry your written authorization.

Homestead exemption

For 2025 and 2026, seniors and totally disabled owners lose $49,100 from the assessed value used for the bill. The PVA on Stanford Street takes the application.

A birth certificate, license or passport shows your age. A seller who has held the exemption should tell the PVA after closing so it ends at that address. The buyer then files a fresh application if they qualify. Lancaster staff at the PVA can tell you what documents to bring, and applying early in the year avoids a gap on the next bill.

Frequently asked questions

When do Garrard County tax bills go out?

On October 1 each year. Anyone who pays the entire bill by November 1 saves 2 percent.

Who should I call if a Garrard County tax value looks wrong?

Call the Garrard County PVA at (859) 792-3291. The sheriff's office never assesses value and refers those questions to the PVA.

Where is the Garrard County sheriff's tax office?

Go to 319 Stanford St. in Lancaster, KY 40444, or phone (859) 792-3591. The sheriff collects for 28 taxing districts.

What changes for Garrard County taxes still open on April 15?

The County Clerk receives it as a certificate of delinquency and records a lien. Interest builds monthly, and clerk and attorney commissions follow.

What is the Garrard County homestead exemption worth?

It lowers assessed value by $49,100 for 2025 and 2026 on a home owned by a senior or a totally disabled person.

Brandenburg offices for your tax bill

Nearly everything happens in two suites at 516 Hillcrest Drive. The assessor, formally the Property Valuation Administration (PVA), is in Suite 3 and takes calls at (270) 422-2178 on weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The Sheriff's Office is in Suite 14, where payments are accepted, at (270) 422-4937.

Value is decided in one suite and collected in the other. Walk exemption and value questions into Suite 3. Carry the bill itself to Suite 14. The County Clerk gets involved only after April 15, once unpaid bills have been transferred.

How and when to pay

Payment goes to the Sheriff. Bills are mailed each fall, and when mail runs late the Sheriff's office posts an online lookup so owners can check what they owe while the paper bill catches up. The dates below follow KRS 134.015, but the law allows a different schedule when mailing is delayed, so ask the Sheriff which dates apply to your bill.

Meade County payment schedule
When you payEffect on the bill
By November 12 percent discount
Through New Year's EveNo discount, no penalty
January5 percent added
After January10 percent added

The Sheriff stops collecting on April 15, with the window shutting at 4:30 in the afternoon. Personal checks are refused for the last two weeks of each collection season, so late payers need cash, a card, a money order or a cashier's check. The office calls this a yearly custom, and personal checks are taken again earlier in the season.

What a typical Meade County house owes

A typical owned home here carries a value of $207,900. The state's 2025 rate is 10.6 cents on each $100, and the county, the school district and special districts add their own levies. Owning costs $1,344 a month with a mortgage and $462 without one. A typical renter pays $1,026, and household income is $74,355.

Growth has been steady. The head count climbed from 9,422 in 1950 to 18,938 in 1960 and reached 30,003 in 2020. The July 2025 estimate of 30,699 is 2.3 percent above that. With 165 new-construction permits in 2025, new houses compete with resale listings.

Owners occupy 74.1 percent of homes. In 2020 there were 11,943 housing units, 7.5 percent of them vacant, and tenants lived in 27.2 percent of the occupied ones. A seller with a tenant in place should settle showing access with the tenant before listing.

Homestead exemption

Owners aged 65 or more, and those who are totally disabled, can have $49,100 shaved off assessed value for 2025 and 2026 under state law. Because it comes off before rates apply, every levy on the bill shrinks with it.

The PVA sets a spring deadline each year for applications to make the November bill. Someone turning 65 soon should call the office to learn the current date. Filing early also helps the taxing districts plan their budgets. Proof of age can be a birth certificate, a driver's license or a passport. Disability claims depend on a finding of total disability and must be renewed annually. Renewal is waived for an owner with a service-connected disability and for anyone Social Security or state retirement has ruled permanently disabled.

How to appeal your assessment

Your first step is a conference at the PVA, where staff explain the way your value was built. The state calendar takes over from there:

  • The roll can be viewed for 13 days from the first Monday in May.
  • Hand the appeal to the County Clerk's office by closing time on the next business day.
  • Collect land and building records, such as insurance papers, construction costs and comparable sale listings.
  • Attend the local board of assessment appeals, which convenes roughly a month after viewing for up to five days.

Recording the hearing is allowed. Should the board land above your claim once bills are out, a supplemental bill makes up the difference.

Selling with taxes owed

Selling the house doesn't erase the debt. Whatever is open on April 15 becomes a certificate held by the Clerk, who files a lien and starts 1 percent monthly interest. Under KRS 134.420 the lien may last 11 years under any owner.

Two letters come from the county attorney: the first inside 30 days of the transfer, the second inside 60. The Clerk then sets a sale 90 to 135 days out, and a certificate buyer may add substantial fees. Before April 15 the Sheriff quotes the payoff, and after that date the Clerk does. The closing agent settles it out of the sale money.

Get the payoff on paper and make sure it covers every year with a balance, not just the latest bill.
