Which office does what with your tax bill

Three county offices handle the same bill in turn. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) sets what a parcel is worth, the Sheriff's Office sends the bill and takes payment, and the County Clerk's Office keeps whatever goes unpaid.

Who handles a Henderson County property tax bill
OfficeJobWhen you deal with it
PVAValues the parcelAssessment questions and appeals
Sheriff's OfficeMails the bill, takes paymentFrom November 1 until the bill turns delinquent
County ClerkHolds uncollected bills, runs the tax saleAfter January 1 following the due date

Real estate notices are mailed in late October or early November, and the sheriff accepts payment from November 1. A bill turns delinquent on January 1 after its due date. The sheriff holds the file until uncollected bills are turned over to the clerk.

Delinquency depends on two things: the due date is behind you and any appeal rights have run out. If you are disputing a value, keep the appeal calendar and the payment calendar in front of you at the same time.

Henderson County at a glance

Henderson County sits in far western Kentucky on the Ohio River, across from Evansville, Indiana, and is part of the Evansville, IN-KY metro area. The city of Henderson is the county seat. The 2020 population was 44,793, and the latest estimate is 44,255.

The county has 20,295 housing units, and 64.9 percent of homes are lived in by their owners. About 37 percent of occupied homes were rented at the 2020 census, so there is a real rental market next to the owner-occupied majority. The middle owner home value is $171,900, and the middle gross rent is $777. Buyers who commute from here to Evansville often shop the whole metro area, which is worth remembering when you price.

Who to call for local questions

These local agencies come up most when a house is for sale.

  • The Henderson City-County Planning Commission oversees public and private development inside both city and county limits.
  • Henderson GIS offers maps, data and information on the county.
  • The Henderson Area Board of Realtors and the Housing Authority of Henderson are listed among community organizations.

If a buyer asks about zoning or development near your parcel, point them to the planning commission. Send questions about the tax bill itself to the sheriff or the PVA.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Henderson County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

After a bill goes delinquent

Interest and penalties begin, a lien attaches, and an outside buyer may purchase the debt. The steps run in this order.

  • The bill moves to the County Clerk's Office at 20 N Main Street, 2nd Floor, Henderson, where interest of 1 percent per month and penalties accumulate.
  • A lien stays on the property until payment in full.
  • Any individual or company qualified under KRS Chapter 134 may buy the bill at the clerk's tax sale. The clerk cannot predict or prevent that purchase.
  • The purchaser has 50 days to notify the owner. The owner then pays the purchaser, who sends a release to the clerk for recording.
  • A foreclosure suit by the purchaser becomes possible one year after the certificate of delinquency was created.

You can pay the clerk in person or mail a personal check, cashier's check, money order or certified check. Cards work for an added fee, and the clerk's number for details is 270-827-5753. American Express, Discover and MasterCard are taken, and Visa only as a debit.

How to contest your assessment

Start with a conference at the PVA's office. KRS 133.120 puts that step ahead of any formal appeal. The conference happens during or before the inspection window, and the Department of Revenue may allow up to 25 extra days.

If the conference doesn't settle it, file a written petition with the county clerk. The appeals board holds a public hearing and fixes fair cash value, and the county attorney speaks for the state and county there. If you lose, you can go on to the Board of Tax Appeals, but only after appearing before the county board.

Anyone you pay to represent you must be an attorney, accountant, tax consultant, your own employee, a broker or a certified appraiser. They carry written authorization and disclose any contingency fee, although attorneys need not state its terms. The board can also raise a value, but it must first send you notice and a hearing date.

Selling with taxes owed

Whoever owns the property on January 1 gets the year's bill. Under KRS 134.015 the debt is personal to that owner, and a delinquency lien under KRS 134.420 outlasts any sale. Before the closing date, line up two numbers: what the sheriff shows for the current year and what the clerk shows for earlier ones.

If a prior year sits with the clerk, the 1 percent monthly interest becomes part of the payoff, so ask for a fresh figure close to the signing. The title agent can pay the total out of your proceeds. For recording charges and the real estate transfer tax on the deed, see the Henderson County Clerk page.

A cash sale skips the lender's payoff schedule, but it doesn't skip the lien. The tax still has to be cleared before the deed can pass free of it. If you are behind, getting the clerk's payoff letter early gives you time to decide whether to pay from savings or from the sale proceeds.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Henderson County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What to gather before you list

Pull your last tax bill and any delinquency notice, and note whether the sheriff or the clerk currently holds the file. Bring photo ID if you plan to pay in person at 20 N Main Street. If you filed an appeal, keep the petition and hearing notice handy, since a buyer's lender may ask about an open dispute.

Ask the sheriff for the current-year amount and the clerk for any earlier years, and write both down with the date you called. Interest keeps running at 1 percent per month on anything held by the clerk, so a figure from early in the month may be stale by closing. If a lender is paying off a mortgage at the same table, tell the closer which years are still open so the tax lines are not missed on the settlement statement.

When the clerk's file is clean, the title search moves faster and closing is less likely to slip. When an outside buyer already holds the bill, expect the 50-day notice and the release step to add time, so start early. If you plan to appeal, ask the PVA's office how its conference is scheduled before you call anyone else, because that conference comes first and the petition to the county clerk follows only if it fails.

Frequently asked questions

When does Henderson County start taking property tax payments?

November 1. Notices go out in late October or early November, and the sheriff accepts payment beginning that day. A bill goes delinquent on the following January 1.

Where is a delinquent Henderson County bill paid?

At the County Clerk's Office, 20 N Main Street, 2nd Floor Offices, Henderson, KY 42420. Mailed payments must be a check, money order or other certified funds.

How much interest does the clerk charge on a delinquent bill?

One percent per month plus penalties. A buyer of the bill at the tax sale may add charges allowed under Kentucky law.

Can someone else buy my delinquent Henderson County tax bill?

Yes. Any person or company qualified under KRS Chapter 134 can buy it at the clerk's sale, and the clerk can neither predict nor stop the purchase.

How long before a bill buyer can foreclose?

One year after the certificate of delinquency is created. Some buyers wait longer while the property's equity covers the debt.

Which counter handles which tax question

Property tax questions in New Castle go to one of three offices. Pick by topic: what the house is worth, paying this year's bill, or a bill that is already late.

Where to go in Henry County
OfficeWhere and whenUse it for
PVA23 South Property Road, New Castle, KY 40050 (mail to P.O. Box 11), (502) 845-5740, open 8 to 4:30Assessments, ownership records, homestead applications

County Clerk27 South Property Road, P.O. Box 615, (502) 845-5705, weekdays 8 to 4, closed noon to 1Late bills and deed recordings, with eRecording

The PVA's website links to a bill search run from the sheriff's records.

January 1 is the date for both the assessment and the tax owner. If you buy in June, that year's state bill still goes out in the seller's name, and the new owner appears the following year. The office tries to mail a copy to the new owner from the recorded deed. A buyer who gets nothing can phone the sheriff.

The Henry County housing market

Henry County is a farm and commuter county in north central Kentucky, and it has served as an exurb of the Louisville area since the 1990s. New Castle holds the courthouse, and Eminence is the largest city. Population grew from 15,678 in the 2020 census to an estimated 16,447 in 2025, up 4.9 percent.

Of 6,883 housing units, 76.3 percent are owner-occupied. A typical owned home is valued at $197,900, and typical gross rent is $895. About 89.5 percent of residents lived at the same address a year earlier, so your likely buyer is moving in from elsewhere. Commutes average 30.5 minutes, a selling point for anyone driving toward Louisville. Henry County Schools and the Eminence Independent district both serve the county, and a listing should say which one an address falls in.

Residents 65 and over make up about 20.9 percent of the county, the group the homestead reduction below is written for.

Who can ask the appeals board to change an assessment

Officials can start a review as well as owners. KRS 133.120 lets the board of assessment appeals change a value if the county judge/executive, a city mayor using the county assessment, or a school superintendent asks in writing and names the parcel. The Department of Revenue can make the same recommendation.

If you are the owner, start with a PVA conference. Then file a written petition at the county clerk's office by the workday after inspection ends. Hearings begin 25 to 35 days after inspection closes (KRS 133.030), and the board usually wraps up inside five days.

  • Collect land and building descriptions, insurance policies, construction costs, listings and loan papers.
  • If the board weighs a higher value, you get a notice and a date to protest.
  • A taxpayer who listed their own parcel at fair cash value may ask the board to look at a neighbor's apparent under-assessment, in writing and with comparable sales or cost data.
  • The board can't reopen values across the board.

Keep paying while the appeal runs. Your payment is based on the value you claimed, and the sheriff bills any difference later with interest.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Henry County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Homestead exemption

If you are 65 or older, or totally disabled, your primary residence can qualify for a reduction of $49,100 in assessed value for 2025 and 2026. File the application at the PVA's office.

Bring a birth certificate, license or passport as proof of age. A disability claim needs a federal or retirement-system classification and is renewed every year, with exceptions for service-connected disability and permanent Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems determinations.

If you sell, the exemption ends with your ownership. The buyer has to file their own application if they qualify, so mention it when you hand over the tax paperwork.

Clearing tax debt before you sell

Plan for the debt now. Whoever owned the house on January 1 owes that year's tax personally, and a delinquency lien under KRS 134.420 stays alive for eleven years even after the house changes hands.

Get a current-year payoff from the sheriff. For any year already late, go to the Henry County Clerk, whose website has a delinquent taxes link. Once claims reach the clerk, KRS 134.119 stacks on the sheriff's fee: ten percent of the tax and ten percent of the penalty. Avoiding that starts with the calendar in KRS 134.015, where paying by November 1 saves 2 percent and each late stage after December 31 costs 5 and then 10 percent.

Deed recording also runs through the clerk, and the seller's transfer tax under KRS 142.050 is collected there. Call the office for current charges.

Payment timing and penalties

The state calendar in KRS 134.015 rewards early payment. Pay by November 1 and you save 2 percent. After December 31, each late stage adds 5 percent and then 10 percent. Once the claim lands at the clerk, the sheriff's fee of ten percent of the tax and ten percent of the penalty is added on top.

That makes a payoff figure from the sheriff in October very different from one in March. If you are listing in the fall, paying the current bill before November 1 is a cheap way to take one open item off the title company's list. If you list in spring, call the sheriff first and the clerk second, because the file may have moved between them.

The sheriff is the right call for the current year, and the clerk is the right call once a bill is late. Write down the name of whoever you speak to and the date. If the two offices give different totals, ask the title company to request a written payoff from each, so the closing statement rests on paper and not on a phone call. Ask each office how long its figure stays good.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Henry County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What happens at closing

Expect the title company to ask the sheriff and the clerk for payoff figures. Tell them early who owned on January 1, because the old bill may still carry your name after the deed is recorded. Anything unpaid comes out of your proceeds at the table, and the title agent sends payment to the right office.

A cash sale moves faster only if the tax file is clean. A delinquent year with the clerk adds a payoff step, and a lender or title agent will not skip it. If you owe, call the clerk a week or two before closing for an updated number, then confirm with the title company which office it will pay.

Hold on to every letter the PVA or board sends about a value dispute. A buyer may ask whether an appeal is open, and you can answer with paperwork instead of memory.

Frequently asked questions

Who collects property tax in Henry County, Kentucky?

The Henry County Sheriff, at (502) 845-2909. Delinquent bills go to the Henry County Clerk at (502) 845-5705.

Why does my Henry County bill name the previous owner?

Ownership is locked in on January 1. A purchase after that date leaves the bill under the former owner until the next calendar year.

What is the Henry County homestead amount?

It is $49,100 for assessment years 2025 and 2026, open to owners 65 or older or totally disabled through an application at the PVA.

Who besides the owner can seek a review of a Henry County value?

The county judge/executive, a city mayor, a school superintendent or the Department of Revenue, each by written recommendation naming the parcel.

Does an appeal stop my Henry County tax bill?

No. Pay tax on the value you claimed while the appeal runs, and expect a bill for any increase with interest.

Knox County tax offices and phone numbers

Five phone numbers cover nearly every Knox County tax question, and each office is in the Barbourville courthouse complex at 401 Court Square. The PVA sets the value. The sheriff bills and collects. The clerk takes over what goes unpaid, and the county attorney pursues it from there.

Courthouse doors open weekdays from 8:30 until 4:00. On Saturday mornings until noon, only the county clerk and circuit clerk offices stay open. To record a deed on a Knox County house, carry it to the clerk on the first floor.

Knox County housing and prices

Knox County had 30,193 residents in 2020 and an estimated 29,532 by July 2025. It holds 14,090 housing units, and about one in eight were empty at the 2020 count. A typical owner-occupied home is valued at $118,700, roughly two in three of the 11,711 households own, and a typical monthly rent is $681. At prices this low, a few thousand dollars of back tax takes a large bite out of a sale, so ask for payoff numbers before you list.

Which school district taxes your address

Knox has three public school systems: Knox County Public Schools, Barbourville Independent and Corbin Independent. Two houses a few blocks apart can sit in different systems, and that shows up on the bill. Give the parcel number to the PVA or the sheriff and ask which district applies before you quote a price or compare bills.

Condition, repairs and your assessment

Steady moisture and hard freezes put roofs, gutters, crawlspaces and exposed plumbing at the top of an inspector's list. If you keep receipts for recent repairs, or tell a cash buyer straight what needs work, the back-and-forth gets shorter. The same file supports an assessment conference if the PVA's value assumes a house in better shape than yours.

How to appeal your assessment

Kentucky bars an appeal until you have sat down with the PVA, so book that conference first. Once the May inspection window closes, the county clerk takes the appeal within a day, and a local board of fellow owners hears it a few weeks later.

Bring proof: photos, contractor bids, an appraisal or nearby sales. Show up with nothing and the board will deny you. The PVA appraises everything at full market price, so recent nearby sales make the strongest argument.

Due dates and unpaid bills

The year's property tax comes due at the end of December, and most Kentucky sheriffs begin collecting in October or November. Discount and penalty steps differ across counties, so read the dates printed on your Knox County bill or call the sheriff at (606) 546-3181.

Anything still owed on April 15 goes to the clerk as a certificate of delinquency with a lien on the parcel. The clerk offers a delinquent tax lookup, and the clerk's own figure controls at the time of sale. The state's worked example grows a $1,000 bill to $1,254 at transfer and to $1,659.90 after a June advertisement. Interest adds one percent per month.

  • The county attorney mails a 30-day letter, then a 60-day letter.
  • A sale to a third-party buyer can follow, 90 to 135 days after the transfer.
  • That buyer takes over the lien, and the owner then pays the buyer.

Whoever held title on January 1 personally owes the bill, and under KRS 134.420 the lien lasts eleven years whoever holds the deed. A buyer inherits it with the house, so sellers clear it first.

Homestead exemption

Anyone past their 65th birthday, and anyone ruled totally disabled by a retirement system, can deduct $49,100 from the assessed value for 2025 and 2026 if the house is their residence on January 1. File with the PVA by the end of December. Heirs living elsewhere do not inherit the break automatically.

Splitting taxes when a Knox County house sells

The bill carries the January 1 owner's name, so a March sale still leaves the seller as taxpayer of record. The closing agent splits the year on the settlement statement and pays the sheriff. KRS 382.135(1)(d) requires an in-care-of address on the deed for that year's bill, so supply the buyer's mailing address.

Heirs, owners behind on payments and landlords with a vacant rental often wonder whether a cash buyer can wrap up everything in one closing. It works when the payoffs are known first: the sheriff quotes the current-year amount and the clerk quotes any older certificate. Ask the county attorney's office as well whether a payment plan is on file, because the title agent will ask.

What to bring to the courthouse

Most of your errands happen under one roof, so one trip can cover several. For a conference with the PVA, bring the parcel number, your latest bill and whatever backs up your number: photos, contractor bids, an appraisal or recent nearby sales. For a homestead application, bring proof of age or a retirement system disability ruling, and file before the year ends.

At the clerk's office on the first floor, bring the signed deed if you are recording a sale, and ask for the delinquent certificate balance on the same visit. Keep each receipt. The title agent will want a record that the current year was paid or prorated, and a clean paper trail makes closing smoother for you and for the buyer.

Steps before you list a house with back taxes

Start with two phone calls. The sheriff gives you the current-year amount, and the clerk gives you the balance on any older certificate. Ask both for the figure in writing and for the date it stays good, since interest keeps running each month. If a payment plan exists, the county attorney's office at (606) 546-9515 can tell you where it stands.

Gather the deed, the most recent bill and any delinquent notice into one folder. Hand a copy to the title agent early. A cash sale skips the buyer's loan approval, so the only real delay is usually a payoff that nobody requested ahead of time. Once the figures are in hand, pick a closing date inside the window they cover. If the date slips, call both offices again for updated amounts, because interest and fees change the number from month to month.

Frequently asked questions

Which office takes Knox County property tax payments?

The sheriff, at (606) 546-3181, collects the current bill. After April 15 the clerk, at (606) 546-3568, handles it as a delinquent certificate.

How do I begin disputing a Knox County property value?

Schedule a conference with the PVA at (606) 546-4113. Filing with the clerk comes afterward, before the deadline that follows the roll inspection.

How much does the Knox County homestead exemption remove?

It removes $49,100 of assessed value for 2025 and 2026 for qualifying seniors and totally disabled owners living in the house. Applications go to the PVA before the year ends.

Do late Knox County bills pick up interest?

Yes. After the bill reaches the clerk as a certificate, interest runs at one percent per month, with commissions and fees on top.

Could I sell a Knox County home that has unpaid tax?

Yes. The lien stays attached to the parcel, so the payoff is deducted at closing. Get written amounts from the sheriff and the clerk before you pick a date.

Three Owenton offices, three jobs

Property tax in Owen County runs through three offices in Owenton. One collects the money, one decides the value, and one keeps the records once a bill goes unpaid or an appeal is filed.

The sheriff assigns no values, so a dispute over the amount begins with the PVA, not at the collection counter.

Owen County housing in brief

Owen County covers about 354 square miles of northern Kentucky, with Owenton as the seat and Glencoe and Gratz as the only other cities. It is thinly settled, at 32.1 residents per square mile in 2020, and the entire population lived in rural areas at the last census. The count was 11,278 in 2020, with an estimate of 11,601 for mid-2025.

  • Homes owned by their occupants have a median value of $168,700, and 88.0 percent of the 4,252 households own.
  • Mortgage holders spend $1,385 a month at the median, and renters pay $830.
  • The typical household earns $61,134.
  • Getting to work takes 41.9 minutes on average, a long drive that shapes who buys here.
  • Only 17 building permits were issued in 2025.

Of 5,323 housing units in 2020, 18.3 percent stood vacant, a high share that includes seasonal and unsold property. Expect a quiet market in which many sales are older houses and land.

Payment dates for an Owen County bill

Sheriffs across Kentucky use the schedule in KRS 134.015. Owen County residents get a 2 percent break for paying by November 1, owe the stated amount until year end, and add 5 percent in January, then 10 percent from February.

April 15 ends the sheriff's collection season. What remains unpaid turns into a certificate of delinquency at the County Clerk, with a lien noted against the parcel.

If you are selling in the middle of the year, remember that the owner on January 1 is the one billed. Ask the title agent to prorate the year between you and the buyer, and keep your receipt.

Planning your visit to the PVA

Call 502-484-5172 before you drive over. Tell the office what you want to discuss, whether it is a value, an exemption or the mailing address on a bill, and ask what to bring. Bring your latest bill, and for an appeal add the evidence described below.

Photos that show a leaking roof, a failing septic system or an old furnace are worth more than a general complaint. So are quotes from contractors and the sale prices of houses close to yours. If you own acreage, be ready to describe the land and any outbuildings.

How to contest a valuation

Begin with a talk at the PVA office. Arrive with your own value figure and proof, such as nearby sales, an appraisal, damage photos or contractor quotes. Landlords add rent and expense records.

  1. Talk to the PVA while the roll is open for inspection each spring.
  2. Collect the appeal form from the clerk at 136 W. Bryan Street and return it by the next business day after inspection ends.
  3. Present your evidence to a local board of three residents.
  4. If the ruling stands and you disagree, send the state Board of Tax Appeals a letter within a month of the notice.

You may pay on your own claimed value while an appeal is pending, but a higher final figure produces a supplemental bill.

What happens to delinquent bills?

The clerk's website posts the delinquent list along with investor registration forms. The state revenue department sets a normal-schedule sale between July 14 and August 28, no sooner than 90 days after the bills reach the clerk.

  • Each month adds 1 percent interest.
  • The county attorney sends two letters, and the second names the sale date.
  • Newspaper notices run roughly a month to six weeks before the sale.
  • A certificate that sells to an investor can carry added fees.

If you are selling a listed parcel, ask the clerk (502-484-2213) for a written payoff. The title company will use it to pay the balance from your proceeds, which is usually simpler than letting the debt reach an investor.

Homestead exemption and farm land

Homeowners who are 65 or older or totally disabled can shelter part of a home's assessed value through the homestead exemption. The state sets the amount and reviews it every two years. An owner with a total service-connected disability applies once, but a buyer starts fresh.

Working farm acreage is assessed at agricultural value, not market value, which can cut the taxable amount sharply. Before a farm is sold or split, ask the PVA whether the tract qualifies.

Charges at the closing table

The transfer tax is the seller's: half a dollar per $500 of value, with any partial block counted whole (KRS 142.050). The clerk wants proof of payment before taking the deed.

The deed itself must list the full price, both mailing addresses and a forwarding address for the next tax bill (KRS 382.135), or the clerk cannot file it. If you are inheriting or selling an estate property, ask the clerk what extra paperwork the personal representative needs.

Selling an Owen County house with taxes owed

An open tax balance does not stop a sale. It does need to be cleared, and the order matters.

  1. Phone the sheriff for the current bill, or the clerk once April 15 has gone by.
  2. Ask for the payoff in writing, with the date it stays good through.
  3. Pass the figure to your closing agent so it can be paid out of the proceeds.
  4. Check afterward that the clerk has recorded a release.

A cash buyer can close without waiting on a bank appraisal, which helps when a house has deferred repairs or a long tax history, though the payoff is still due at closing. A clean tax record is one thing a seller fully controls, whatever the market does.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Questions to settle before you accept an offer

Before you sign a contract, answer three questions. Who paid this year's bill, and when? Is anything recorded against the parcel at the County Clerk's office? Does the deed carry an address where the buyer wants the next bill sent? None takes long, and together they remove most of the surprises that slow a closing.

If a buyer asks about the tax bill, point to the printed statement and the sheriff's phone number rather than guessing. For an inherited house, bring the paperwork that shows who has authority to sign.

Frequently asked questions

Which office decides what my Owen County property is worth?

The Property Valuation Administration, 502-484-5172. Collection is the sheriff's job, valuation is not.

Where is the Owen County tax office?

In the sheriff's office at 103 W. Perry St., Owenton (502-484-3363), Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.

Who pays transfer tax on an Owen County sale?

The seller pays it, at 50 cents per $500 of value with partial blocks counted whole. The clerk wants proof of payment before accepting the deed.

What if my bill is still open after April 15?

Phone the County Clerk, 502-484-2213. The bill has become a certificate of delinquency, with a lien and monthly interest of 1 percent.

Is a homestead exemption available in Owen County?

Yes, through the PVA, for residents who are 65 or older or totally disabled. Whoever buys the house applies separately.

Simpson County and Franklin

Simpson County sits on Kentucky's southern edge against the Tennessee line, in the Pennyroyal Plateau region. Franklin is its only city and its seat of government. The county had 20,788 residents in July 2025, up from 19,595 in 2020, living in 9,172 housing units and 8,025 households. The 2020 census counted 10,176 people in Franklin, so about half the county lives in town and the rest in farm and small community settings.

Warren County borders it on the north, Allen on the east and Logan on the west. Franklin's Planning and Zoning Commission follows its Franklin Forward comprehensive plan, which covers land use, housing and community facilities, and the zoning map is posted on the city site.

Home values and ownership

Simpson County housing figures, 2020 through 2024
Housing measureSimpson County

Owners hold two thirds of the occupied homes, so most sales involve a house with a long-term resident rather than a landlord.

How the PVA values property

The Property Valuation Administrator puts every parcel on the roll at fair cash value as of January 1, as Section 172 of the Kentucky Constitution requires. Setting rates and taking payments belong to other offices. The January 1 rule matters at a sale, because a buyer who closes later in the year may never see the bill. If one does not arrive, call the Sheriff at 270-586-7425. The PVA answers at 270-586-4261 on weekdays from 8 to 4.

Who sends and collects the bills

Three offices share the job. The County Clerk prepares and prints the bills and records deeds, the Sheriff collects the county and school portions, and the City of Franklin runs its own tax office at 117 W Cedar for city bills. Franklin's commission sets the city rates using a state formula, and the city office treats a postmark as proof of on-time payment.

City bills follow the deed records in the clerk's office on January 1. When a property sold afterward, the previous owner remains the city taxpayer, and the city office gives original bills only to the addressee. An escrow company that wants an electronic copy of the billing register pays $100, while substitute bills and master payment lists are provided at no charge.

Due dates and penalties

KRS 134.015 sets the schedule. A bill settled in full by November 1 earns 2 percent off. The printed amount carries no penalty through December 31, January adds 5 percent, and 10 percent applies after January ends. City issue, penalty and delinquent dates vary each year, so read the dates printed on each bill.

Anyone with an interest in the property, such as a tenant or a lender, may pay a delinquent bill without the owner's permission if the Sheriff is shown proof, and a payer can ask to be treated as a transferee (KRS 134.119). After the Sheriff files unpaid claims with the County Clerk, the clerk holds them as certificates of delinquency.

How to appeal your assessment

An appeal begins with a conference at the PVA's office. KRS 133.045 keeps the real property roll open for inspection for 13 days from early May, six days a week, and the conference must be requested before that period closes. If you still disagree afterward, file with the County Clerk, and three local residents hear the case informally, with no attorney required.

The local assessment board has three year terms and meets once a year, with seats filled by the city, the Fiscal Court and the county judge. Bring comparable sales, a recent appraisal or photos of damage. A losing owner can carry the case to the state's tax appeals board.

City rules that can hold up a sale

Franklin applies the International Property Maintenance Code through its Code Enforcement department, which takes yard sale permits and public nuisance complaints through its citizen portal. The Planning and Zoning Commission follows KRS Chapter 100, and its staff can be reached at 270-596-2756. The city also keeps a lienholder notification process listed among its services.

A home with a nuisance complaint, an unpaid city tax bill or a permit left open is harder to close. Ask city staff about open cases at an address before you list, and confirm county and city tax payoffs separately.

What a seller owes at closing

Kentucky's deed transfer tax falls on the seller: 50 cents on each $500 of price, taken by the County Clerk at the recording counter (KRS 142.050). Add prorated property tax, any lien payoff and agent fees if you list. Owners who qualify for the homestead or disability exemption should confirm with the PVA that it is on file before the sale, since the PVA administers both. A cash offer avoids agent fees and repair demands, which can matter for an older farmhouse or a rental needing work, but the net after payoffs is the number to compare.

  • PVA: assessments, exemptions and the appeals conference, 270-586-4261.
  • Sheriff, 203 E. Kentucky Ave: collects county tax bills, 270-586-7425.
  • County Clerk, 105 E Kentucky St: prepares tax bills and records deeds, 270-586-8161.

Selling a house with taxes still owed

Two bills can be open on a Franklin address, one from the county and one from the city, so ask for a payoff from each. Get the county figure from the Sheriff and the city figure from the tax office at 117 W Cedar. Both can be paid out of the sale proceeds at closing.

If a lender escrows your taxes, check that the payment actually reached the Sheriff and the city. Then gather your homestead or disability exemption paperwork, the latest bills, and any notices about open nuisance or permit cases. A cash buyer will usually accept the house as is, which removes the repair requests that often come after a buyer's inspection.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Paperwork to gather before you sell

Collect the latest county and city tax bills, proof of any homestead or disability exemption, and a payoff letter from your lender. If you own farm ground or a house outside the city limits, you will only have the county bill, which is simpler. Inside Franklin, expect both.

Call the County Clerk to confirm the deed on record matches the name on your sale contract. A mismatch, such as an old deed that never added a spouse, can stall a closing. Franklin's Code Enforcement department can tell you about any open nuisance case, and the Planning and Zoning staff can confirm how the lot is zoned. Taking care of these early lets you accept an offer without conditions hanging over the sale.

Frequently asked questions

Does Franklin bill its own property tax?

Yes. Franklin sets rates through its commission and runs a tax office at 117 W Cedar, open weekdays until 4 p.m. Central time. Houses inside city limits get two bills, one from the county and one from the city.

Who is billed if I buy a Simpson County house after January 1?

The former owner is the taxpayer of record for that year. The PVA mails the bill to the new owner when it can, and a buyer who receives nothing can call the Sheriff at 270-586-7425.

When does the Simpson County early payment discount end?

On November 1. Full payment by then takes 2 percent off, and the face amount holds through December 31 under KRS 134.015. Penalties of 5 and then 10 percent follow.

Where is a Simpson County assessment appeal filed?

After a PVA conference, file with the County Clerk at 105 E Kentucky St. The conference has to happen while the roll is open for inspection, which starts in early May.

What deed tax comes out of a Simpson County sale?

Fifty cents per $500 of price, with a partial block counted whole. The County Clerk collects it at recording.

Where to take care of tax business

Taylor County stacks its tax offices on one street in Campbellsville. The sheriff, the Property Valuation Administration (PVA) and the county clerk all work out of 203 North Court Street, so a single stop can cover a payoff, an exemption form and a lien check.

Taylor County at a glance

Campbellsville is the seat and the only city, with Acton, Hobson, Mannsville, Saloma and Spurlington among the unincorporated communities. Marion, Casey, Adair, Green and LaRue counties surround the county, which covers 277 square miles, 266 of them land. Campbellsville Independent and Taylor County Schools split the school districts, and Campbellsville University anchors the local economy.

The county has 26,763 residents as of July 2025, a 2.8 percent gain on 2020, and 11,247 housing units. Typical home value is $174,200 and typical rent is $718. Owners live in 68.8 percent of units, so a good share of the market is rentals: the 2020 count found 35.9 percent of occupied units rented, and 28.9 percent of households were one person living alone.

What owners and renters pay

Owners with a mortgage pay a median $1,217 a month for housing, against $432 for owners with none. Household income is $60,456 and the mean commute is 22.7 minutes. Just 9 building permits were issued in 2025, so new construction adds little to the supply, and existing houses make up most of what sells.

Households average 2.45 people, so many homes are small ones. About one resident in five is past 65 (19.5 percent). That group is the likeliest to use the homestead break described below. Landlords will see a different picture: the rental vacancy rate was 5.8 percent in 2020, and 9.2 percent of all housing units stood vacant.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Taylor County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Deadlines and surcharges

State law sends payment to the sheriff, with a due date at the end of the assessment year. The sequence runs:

  • A bill settled by November 1 earns a 2 percent break.
  • Between that date and December 31, the printed amount applies.
  • January brings a 5 percent surcharge.
  • After January 31, 10 percent applies, with the sheriff's add-on fee from the Revenue Department's delinquency worksheet.

Taylor County bills turn delinquent on April 15 each year, when the sheriff's file closes and unpaid bills pass to the clerk.

If your bill is past due

Act before April 15 if you can, because that date moves the file from the sheriff to the clerk and adds commissions. After that, the county attorney's letters begin, and each notice gives you another chance to pay before a company can buy the bill. Calling the clerk at (270) 465-6677 tells you where your parcel stands in that sequence.

Owners who are selling should not wait for the sale date at all. A bill that has been bought by an outside company has to be settled with that company, and its costs are higher than the clerk's. Settling early keeps the closing on schedule and keeps more of your proceeds.

What the clerk does with unpaid bills

Collection moves to the clerk, with the county attorney writing to each owner. Two letters go out and the delinquent list runs in the Central Kentucky News Journal. A bill still open after those three notices can be offered to third-party companies, which buy it and place a lien against the land. No sales happen before August, and the list, with the sale date, is posted on the clerk's page as the day approaches.

Debt grows fast once a bill reaches the clerk. Penalty, the add-on fee and a commission are folded into the certificate, then 1 percent interest accrues monthly, with a 10 percent clerk commission and, after the first notice, a 20 percent county attorney commission. Paying within five business days of the transfer avoids the attorney's share.

How to appeal your assessment

Meeting with the PVA at Suite 6 is the entry point. PVAs value most houses by comparing recent sales, and your conference is the time to ask which sales were used. After the meeting you file with the clerk at the end of the next workday after the May viewing period, a stretch of two weeks that includes Saturdays. A board of local owners hears the case roughly a month afterward.

Come with facts: building characteristics, insurance values, construction costs or listings of similar property. Without them the board denies the appeal. A paid representative needs your written authorization and a recognized credential, for example an attorney, accountant, broker or appraiser.

Farmland follows a separate rule. Kentucky values it at what the land earns in agriculture rather than what it would sell for, which can cut a bill sharply near cities and matters less in rural areas where the two values sit close together. Taxable personal property is listed with the PVA by May 15.

Homestead exemption

Owners past 65, or classified as totally disabled by a federal agency or a retirement system, have $49,100 subtracted from the assessment for 2025 and 2026. File Form 62A350 at the PVA before December 31. A household gets one exemption even if both spouses qualify, and a purchaser must apply again after a sale.

Clearing taxes before closing

Get the sheriff's exact payoff, then ask the clerk whether the parcel carries a certificate from an earlier year. Each year's tax is the January 1 owner's own debt, and a delinquent lien can follow the land for eleven years. When an outside company holds the bill, the money goes to that company instead of the clerk.

Visit Suite 7 for the current year and the clerk's office for anything older, then give both written figures to the closing agent. If you want to sell without repairs or showings, a cash buyer can accept the house as it stands and pay the tax balances out of your proceeds at closing. Compare the amount you would keep after payoffs, not just the offer.

Bring a photo ID and the parcel number to each office. Ask each one to put the amount in writing with an expiration date, since figures change as penalties and interest run. A fresh figure close to the closing date is the one the title agent will trust.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Where can I pay a Taylor County property tax bill?

At the sheriff's office, 203 North Court Street, Suite 7, or through the online portal for 2026 payments. Call (270) 465-4351 to confirm the amount.

When does a Taylor County bill turn delinquent?

On April 15 of the following year. The sheriff's file closes and the clerk takes over collection.

Will Taylor County sell my overdue tax bill to a company?

It can, after the three notices. No sales happen before August, and the buyer's lien then attaches to your property.

How do I apply for the homestead exemption in Taylor County?

Take Form 62A350 to the PVA at (270) 465-5811 before December 31. The home must be your residence on January 1, and you must qualify by age or disability.

Can I sell my Taylor County house with back taxes owed?

Yes. The payoff comes out of your sale money. Bring written payoffs from the sheriff and the clerk so the closing agent can clear every open year.

Adair County property tax offices

Value and payment sit in different hands here. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) sets what each parcel is worth, while the sheriff collects the money. Tax rates come from the taxing bodies themselves, including the fiscal court and the school board.

The PVA is at 424 Public Square, Suite 2, Columbia, KY 42728, telephone (270) 384-3673, weekdays eight to four. Deputies there process deed transfers, including partial sales, and adjust vehicle values. The sheriff is at (270) 384-2776 and the County Clerk at (270) 384-2801.

Kentucky fixes values on January 1, so a parcel is appraised as it stood that morning. If you close in February, the year's bill will usually be addressed to the seller, so the sale contract should say who repays whom.

When Adair County tax bills are due

KRS 134.015 sets a payment schedule, and the sheriff collects at each stage.

Pay duringResult
Through November 12 percent discount
Rest of November and DecemberPlain bill, no extras
All of January5 percent added
February onward10 percent added

If the state mails bills late, every date can slide back a month. Collection season normally ends April 15. Any balance still open on that day moves to the County Clerk, and a lien is recorded against the property.

What an Adair County owner pays

For 2025 the state rate is 10.6 cents per $100 of assessed value, lower than the 10.9 cents of 2024. That covers the state's share only. County, school and other districts add their own, so the PVA or the sheriff can give you the combined figure for your address.

A payment made by November 1 takes 2 percent off the total. At a sale, someone has to split the year's bill between buyer and seller. Find out how your contract does it, and check with the sheriff on what the account has already paid.

How to challenge an Adair County value

Meet with the PVA or a deputy first. Then use the public viewing of the roll, which begins the first Monday in May and runs two more weeks, to state your objection. If notices have already gone out, you can raise it sooner.

  • Ask the PVA to show how the number was built. The meeting gets written up.
  • Take the appeal to the County Clerk no later than the workday following the close of viewing.
  • Back it with proof: descriptions of land and buildings, insurance papers, what the building cost, and similar sales or listings. No proof, no relief.
  • Show up at the hearing, held some weeks afterward. Skipping it after filing costs you any later review by the Kentucky Claims Commission.

Anyone you hire to speak for you must come from an approved list, such as attorneys, CPAs, brokers or certified appraisers, and carry your signed authorization. A board result above your claimed figure brings a supplemental bill.

Homestead exemption for older owners

Kentucky lets owners aged 65 or over, and owners treated as totally disabled, deduct $49,100 from assessed value for 2025 and 2026, as set by the Revenue Department. The deduction is taken before the rate is applied.

Send the PVA the form in the year you want the break, by mail, fax or email. A license, Medicare card or birth certificate shows your age, and a Kentucky license or ID shows where you live. A household cannot claim two, and one spouse at 65 qualifies it.

It stays in place while you own and live in the house. After you sell, tell the PVA so it is removed from the old address.

Selling with taxes unpaid

Unpaid tax follows the house. Under KRS 134.015 it is the owner's own debt from the assessment date, and the lien lasts until it is paid or eleven years pass under KRS 134.420. A new deed does not erase it. Ask the sheriff for a payoff number before you list.

Interest of 1 percent a month builds once the clerk has the account. Commissions to the clerk and county attorney, plus a lien recording fee, pile on top. Two notices come by mail, and from 90 to 135 days after the handoff the certificate can be sold to someone who may add fees.

Settle with the sheriff before April 15 and you avoid all of it.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Adair County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Adair County for a seller

Columbia, the county seat, is also the one incorporated city. Population reached 19,423 in 2025, and 77.2 percent of homes are lived in by their owners. Livestock, dairy, corn and tobacco anchor the farm economy. With only six building permits in 2025, almost every sale is a house that is already built.

Columbia keeps Central time while Taylor and Casey counties to the north run on Eastern, which is worth remembering when you schedule a closing with out-of-county parties.

What Adair County buyers look at

Because Adair County is rural, buyers often weigh acreage, outbuildings, road frontage and the distance to Columbia. A house on a small tract near town tends to draw commuters, while a farm property draws buyers who want land. Before you list, find out whether the parcel includes more than one tract, since partial sales are handled by the PVA and can affect the deed you need.

Walk the property lines, note any shared drives or wells, and keep photos of any repair already done. A cash buyer will still look at these details, but can usually make a decision without waiting for a lender.

A sample timeline for an Adair County seller

Suppose you decide in late summer to sell a house in Columbia. Before anything else, phone the sheriff and learn what is owed on the account. If the bill has not been mailed yet, ask when it will be, since the November 1 discount could still be yours to claim. Next, drive to the PVA office on Public Square and confirm the parcel details and whether your homestead exemption is on file.

When a buyer is found, the title company takes over the lien search and the deed. Your job is to answer questions quickly and keep copies of every notice. If a closing falls between January and April, expect the tax bill to be the main item on the settlement sheet, because penalties may already be running and the clerk's account may be close.

After closing, call the PVA once more. The exemption, if you had one, should come off the old address, and the deed transfer needs to be recorded in the property record so that next year's bill goes to the right person.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Listing versus a cash sale in Adair County

A listing in a small county can take a while, and buyers who rely on loans often want repairs finished and the tax account current before they close. Selling for cash is faster and simpler when the house is dated, needs work, sits on land you cannot easily maintain, or belongs to an estate. We buy houses in Adair County as they are. If yours is in good shape and you are in no hurry, a listing may bring a higher price, and we will say so when you call.

Steps to close an Adair County sale

First call the sheriff for the account balance and the PVA to confirm the parcel and the owner name on record. With a mortgage open, ask for a payoff figure. The title company will then search for liens, draft the deed and share the year's tax bill with the buyer. Afterward the PVA handles the deed transfer, and a partial sale calls for a copy of the recorded deed.

A house that needs repairs or carries back taxes can be sold for cash as-is, clearing both at one closing. The buyer accepts the present condition, and any unpaid balance comes out of your proceeds at the table.

Frequently asked questions

When is the discount deadline for Adair County property taxes?

November 1 is the cutoff. Pay the whole bill by then and you save 2 percent. The face amount applies through December, and penalties begin in January.

Who takes payment of Adair County tax bills?

The Adair County Sheriff, at (270) 384-2776. The PVA, reachable at (270) 384-3673, only values property and never takes payments.

Where do I go to ask about my Adair County property value?

The PVA office, 424 Public Square, Suite 2, in Columbia, open weekdays eight to four. The phone number is (270) 384-3673.

Can I appeal my Adair County assessment after the deadline?

No. The PVA conference comes first, and the clerk filing is due the workday after viewing ends. Viewing opens the first Monday of May and runs 13 days.

Does the homestead exemption move with me when I sell?

No. Tell the PVA after the sale so it comes off the old address, then request it again for the new house. The deduction is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026.

Which offices handle a Murray property tax bill

Valuing and collecting sit in separate hands. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) decides what the house is worth, while the Sheriff's Office sends the bills and takes the money. Its tax desk processes tens of thousands of bills a year and serves Murray and the rural parts of the county alike.

Take value questions and homestead or disability forms to the PVA, 270-753-3482. Take payments to the tax office, 701 Olive Street. After the sheriff's season closes, bills still unpaid are the county clerk's.

Murray State University is in Murray, and with a large rental share the housing stock turns over differently here than in farm counties.

Discount, penalties and due dates

Under KRS 134.015, early payers get 2% off, the next stretch costs face value through December 31, and penalties follow. The Calloway discount ends early, on a November 15 postmark.

Your bill carries its own dated schedule in the top right corner, and the amount climbs with each later date.

Calloway County payment steps
When you payWhat you owe
By November 15 (postmark)Face amount less 2%
Mid-November through December 31The printed amount, no extras
Throughout January5% penalty
Starting February 110% penalty and a sheriff's add-on fee

Cash, check, money order and online card payments are all taken. A bounced check costs $50, and penalties may apply again when you resend. Do not mail cash.

Where and how to pay in Murray

You can pay through a drop box, the mail, the counter or the website. The drop box, on the west side of 701 Olive Street, is never locked. The counter is staffed on weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and you should carry the bill.

  • Mail: stub plus check to 701 Olive St., Murray, KY 42071. Include a stamped return envelope if you want a receipt.
  • Website: the tax search page finishes with a receipt you can print.
  • Several bills together: fine by mail or at the counter when every stub is enclosed.
  • Phone: (270) 761-4TAX.

Pay the single balance due figure for your date. Splitting the payment among the state, county and school lines is not allowed.

Who pays the tax when a Calloway County house sells?

Typically the seller covers a prorated slice of the year at closing, and the buyer pays the full bill when it is issued. The settlement statement shows how yours works.

If closing comes before bills are issued, the title company holds back an estimate. Get the current balance from the tax office, and ask whether an older year is open, because past-due taxes are paid at the clerk, not the sheriff. An owner whose lender escrows still gets a copy of the bill.

The City of Murray lists property taxes on its online payments page too. Ask the city whether a bill is open on your parcel before choosing a closing date, and keep every receipt.

  • Request the sheriff's balance for the parcel.
  • Ask the clerk about any older delinquent year.
  • Check with the PVA that an exemption, if you have one, is on the account.
  • Hand the title company the bill number from your stub.

How to contest a Calloway County value

Talk to the PVA first and file with the clerk after the roll closes. The roll is open to the public for 13 days beginning the first Monday in May, and no appeal to the local board is allowed until you have had a PVA conference.

These hearings turn on proof. The board looks at land, buildings, rebuild cost and nearby sales. Because neighboring sales get adjusted for differences such as a basement, gather three or four recent Murray sales and note where your house differs.

File and then skip the hearing, and you cannot take the case further. Go with your papers. The board owes you a written reason for any increase or decrease, and you may record the hearing on audio.

Exemptions

If you live in the home and are 65 or older, or totally disabled, the homestead exemption may apply. Phone the PVA (270-753-3482) before paying if you think you qualify.

Only one exemption is allowed per household, and it belongs to the owner instead of the property, so your buyer files a new form. Owners who are totally disabled with a service-connected disability do not refile each year.

Under Section 172A of the Kentucky Constitution, farm acreage is valued on what it can produce, not on market price. That gap can be wide near town, so anyone selling acres should ask the PVA how the parcel is classed.

Preparing a Murray house for sale

Taxes are easiest to handle in a set order. Start with the PVA at 270-753-3482 and confirm the value and any exemption. Move to the tax office at 701 Olive Street and ask for the balance on your bill number. Then ask the clerk whether any earlier year is open, because those are paid there and not at the sheriff's counter.

With that done, you can tell a buyer or title company exactly what is owed and what is paid. Keep the printable receipt from the website, or the cancelled check if you mailed one, so there is proof when the closing agent asks. If you own acreage or a rental near campus, add one more call to the PVA about how each parcel is classed.

Why keep receipts

A paid receipt is the quickest way to settle a question from a lender, a buyer or the title company. The website produces one at the end of an online payment. By mail, the stamped return envelope brings one back, and a cancelled check can stand in. At the counter, ask for one. File whichever you get with your closing papers, along with a note of the bill number, so any later dispute about a missed year can be answered in minutes rather than weeks.

If a lender pays your tax from escrow, you can still ask the tax office to confirm the bill shows as paid before you set a closing date.

Calloway County housing market

Calloway's typical owner-occupied home is worth $183,200 (2020 to 2024), and typical rent is $870 a month. Just 63.9 percent of homes are owner-occupied, and renters held 35.8 percent of occupied units in the 2020 count. Residents number 39,421 as of 2025, a 5.0 percent increase over 2020, with 20 permits issued in 2025. Commutes average 17.3 minutes, so a house near jobs and campus in Murray carries built-in appeal.

A courthouse fire in 1906 destroyed almost all of the county's early records, which is why old title questions sometimes need extra research.

A landlord with a rental near campus, an heir with a house in Murray, or an owner of a vacant farmhouse may sell as-is to a cash buyer, skipping financing delays and inspection repair requests. Any signed offer still depends on the tax payoff figures above, so line them up before you accept a closing date.

Frequently asked questions

By when must I pay to get the Calloway County discount?

Payments postmarked by November 15 earn the 2% discount. The dated schedule on your bill is the final word.

Where is the sheriff's tax office in Murray?

701 Olive Street. It serves weekdays until 4:30 p.m., and a drop box on the west side stays open all day and night. The phone is (270) 761-4TAX.

Does the sheriff take credit cards?

Yes, but only through the sheriff's website. Cash, check and money order are also accepted, and cash should never go in the mail.

Who pays the bill if my Murray house sells mid-year?

Normally you pay a prorated share at closing and the buyer pays the full bill once issued. The settlement statement shows the split.

Must I fix up a Calloway County house first?

No, a cash buyer can take it as-is. Unpaid property tax is settled from the proceeds, so request payoff amounts from the sheriff and clerk first.

Selling in Casey County?
We buy Casey County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

Casey County in brief

Casey County covers about 446 square miles with one city, Liberty, and the 2020 census classed the whole population as rural. The count was 15,941 people in 6,270 households and 7,366 housing units, and 14.9 percent of those units stood empty. About 76 percent of occupied homes are lived in by their owners, which means a typical sale here is someone leaving their own home.

Most parcels are farm tracts, hill lots in the Knobs or houses along the state routes. Hillside access, wells, septic systems and road frontage are worth documenting before you list. Only homes inside Liberty raise city tax questions. For everyone else, the assessed value is the first number to examine.

Which office handles which tax question

The year runs on the standard Kentucky cycle: value fixed by the PVA as of January 1, collection by the sheriff from early October to April 15, and leftovers passed to the county clerk. Ask the PVA about value, the sheriff about this year's amount, and the clerk about anything delinquent.

Casey County offices for property tax questions
OfficeWherePhoneHandles
Property Valuation Administrator133 Courthouse Square, Liberty (mail: P O Box 38)606-787-7621Assessments, homestead applications, appeal conferences
County Clerk625 Campbellsville Street, Liberty (mail: P.O. Box 310)606-787-6471Delinquent tax bills, the annual tax sale, lien releases

The clerk keeps weekday hours of 8:00 am to 4:30 pm, except holidays. For the sheriff's address and number, the clerk or the PVA can point you the right way.

Payment dates and penalties

Your sheriff's bill sets the base amount, and the payment date adjusts it. KRS 134.015 gives 2 percent off for paying everything by November 1, charges face value through the end of December, tacks on 5 percent for January, and moves to a 10 percent penalty on February 1 plus the sheriff's add-on fee.

Unpaid tax clings to the parcel as a lien for eleven years, no matter who owns it. If collection starts late in a given year, the Department of Revenue can substitute a schedule that gives owners 30 days at each stage.

If you've lost your bill, get the parcel number from the PVA or clerk and ask the sheriff for a copy. Mortgage escrow doesn't take the bill out of your name, so confirm the payment posted before closing.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Casey County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How to contest a Casey County valuation

Request a conference with the PVA during the public viewing of the tax roll. That period lasts thirteen days from the first Monday of May, and you can ask to do the conference by phone.

If that fails, mail or deliver a written petition to the county clerk by the workday after viewing ends. Include the parcel, your reasons and your opinion of fair cash value. A hearing follows about a month later. Evidence carries the day: sales of similar houses, construction cost records, an insurance policy or a recent appraisal. Under KRS 133.120 the board denies an appeal when the owner won't supply reasonable value information on request.

  • Hold the PVA conference first, because skipping it closes later doors.
  • Keep paying on the value you claimed while the case is pending.
  • A raised value brings a supplemental bill, due the day it is prepared.

The delinquent tax sale

After April 15 an unpaid bill goes to the clerk and can be sold to a private buyer at an annual summer sale. The clerk receives the sheriff's list in April, runs a notice in The Casey County News in July, and holds the sale in August at 9:00 am in its office on Campbellsville Street. Call 606-787-6471 for the current year's dates.

Owners can pay up to the moment the sale opens. Bidders register with the clerk ten days ahead and pay a recording fee of $46 per lien assignment. A buyer who wants more than three certificates in the county, or more than five statewide, must also register with the Department of Revenue.

The sale runs like a draft. Registered buyers draw numbers at random, then take turns picking certificates from the lists they filed, sometimes one certificate per round when the volume is high. The clerk's office tells buyers it won't research bills for them, so a parcel with a problem, such as a bankruptcy filing, is the buyer's risk. Once someone buys your certificate, you owe that buyer and fees can grow. Paying earlier prevents it.

If you already know a bill is going to the clerk, ask whether a payment arrangement is possible and whether the clerk will take a partial payment. Get any agreement in writing, and make sure it covers the fees the certificate has picked up.

Homestead exemption

Kentucky's homestead exemption covers owners in their retirement years or with a total disability. A fixed dollar amount comes off the home's assessed value. The Department of Revenue set it at $49,100 for 2025 and 2026 and publishes a new amount every second year. File with the Casey County PVA and bring proof such as a driver's license or passport.

Only the resident owner gets it. Moving into care or selling mid-year? Let the PVA know so the next bill is right.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Casey County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Closing a sale when tax is unpaid

Collect written balances from both the clerk and the sheriff for your closing agent. Whatever is still owed at the table is deducted from your price, and a lien the clerk filed has to be released before the buyer takes clean title. Releases are recorded at the clerk's office for a posted fee.

For an inherited, empty or worn-down house, a cash buyer that takes the property as is can pay the tax from the price. That keeps your parcel off the August list, where delinquent bills become public.

Work through it in this order. Call the PVA to confirm the parcel and the exemption on file. Ask the sheriff for the current balance. Ask the clerk whether any earlier bill was certified and what the release will cost. Then bring the figures to your closing agent before you sign a contract, so the buyer's offer is based on the real payoff.

Expect the lien release to take a little time to record, so ask the clerk how long it runs. Selling before the next penalty date keeps the amount from rising while you wait. If the property is farmland or hill acreage, confirm the acreage on the PVA's map matches your deed, since the bill follows the PVA record and not your memory of the boundaries.

Frequently asked questions

Where do I find my Casey County property tax bill?

Ask the Casey County sheriff's office, which sends the bills. If you lack its number, the clerk at 606-787-6471 or the PVA at 606-787-7621 can point you to it and help identify your parcel.

When is the Casey County tax sale?

The clerk holds it each August at 9:00 am at 625 Campbellsville Street in Liberty. Owners can pay their unpaid bills up to the start of the sale.

How big is the homestead exemption for Casey County owners?

The state figure is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, subtracted from the assessed value. It is open to owners 65 and up or totally disabled, and you apply through the Casey County PVA.

Is it too late to appeal if I missed the May viewing period?

Usually yes. The PVA conference and the clerk filing both fall inside that window, unless the state approved an extension of up to 25 days. Ask the PVA whether one applied.

Does unpaid tax stop me from selling Casey County land?

No. The bill and any lien get cleared at closing from your proceeds. Ask the sheriff or clerk for payoff amounts first so the title company can deduct them.

Christian County in brief

Christian County is large: 724 square miles, the second-largest in Kentucky by area. Hopkinsville holds the courthouse, and Crofton, LaFayette, Oak Grove and Pembroke are the smaller cities. Central time applies, the Clarksville metro area reaches in, and Fort Campbell lies along the southern side.

Housing here leans toward rentals. The 2020 census counted 26,435 households in 29,206 housing units, with 49.9 percent owner-occupied and 50.1 percent renter-occupied. Vacancy stood at 9.5 percent, and about 71 percent of people lived in places the census calls urban. Many sellers are therefore landlords, and military moves tied to Fort Campbell can leave little time between an order and a closing.

Who to call for each tax or records task

The county clerk at 511 South Main Street in Hopkinsville handles most seller paperwork, with weekday hours from 8:00 am until 4:00 pm. Its phone menu routes the usual requests.

Christian County Clerk phone routing for sellers
What you needNumberNotes
Main clerk line(270) 887-4105Menu extension 3 covers copies of a deed or a plat
Legal records division(270) 887-4109Deeds, mortgages, tax liens and releases filed since 1797
Delinquent tax sale questions(270) 887-4109Same line as the tax sale registration notice
Probate and court records(270) 889-6539Justice Center, not the clerk

For what the house is worth, phone the Christian County PVA. For the current bill, the sheriff's tax office is the place. A missing number? The clerk's main line can redirect you. The legal records division keeps deeds back to 1797, which helps when a chain of title crosses several generations of owners.

Landlords and tenants

Renting the unit out doesn't shift the tax to your tenant. The assessment date makes it your personal debt, and any year left unpaid travels with the parcel into a sale. Landlords gain the most from early payment, since 2 percent off on several rentals adds up. If a servicer or property manager pays your bill, confirm each year that the payment actually went through.

Fort Campbell families are zoned to the federal DoDEA schools, while Christian County Public Schools serve most other households. Buyers ask about schools early, so know which system your address falls in.

Due dates and penalties

Dates come from KRS 134.015. Pay in full by November 1 and you get 2 percent off. Pay by year end and you owe the printed figure. January costs 5 percent more, and anything after that costs 10 percent more. Once the bill moves to the clerk, the sheriff's fees and a clerk commission are added, and the state's sample shows the total growing by about a quarter.

If your house lies inside Hopkinsville, Oak Grove or another city, ask that city whether it bills its own tax and on what dates.

How to dispute an assessment

Your first step is a conference with the Christian County PVA, held while the roll is open for public review. Expect the PVA to walk you through how the value was set. Phone conferences are available on request.

No deal? File a written appeal with the county clerk by the workday following the end of the review. The local board sits roughly a month on and looks at comparable sales, contracts, insurance policies and, for rentals, income and expense statements. A paid representative has to be an attorney, accountant, tax consultant, broker, appraiser or your own employee, with written authority from you.

  • The board can raise a value as well as lower it, so bring evidence for your number.
  • The state's tax appeals board hears later appeals, but only from owners who first used the county board.
  • Payment on the value you claim stays due while the appeal runs.

The delinquent tax sale

Expect a single sale each summer, run by the clerk. The county website lists the date and a registration cutoff a few weeks before. The legal records division at (270) 887-4109 can give you this year's schedule.

State rules frame the timing. Bills move to the clerk on April 15 and the sale must come 90 to 135 days later. The county attorney sends notices in between, and the clerk advertises the list no fewer than 30 days before the sale. A buyer who wants more than three bills in the county, or more than five statewide, must register with the Department of Revenue 60 days before the sale.

Once a bill is a certificate of delinquency, a lien sits on the parcel and interest of 1 percent a month plus clerk and attorney fees accrue. Pay before the sale and the matter is closed. Pay after it and you're dealing with whoever bought the lien.

Homestead exemption

If you're 65 or older, or totally disabled, and the house is your residence, you can claim it. The deduction is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, and it comes off the assessed value ahead of the tax calculation. Apply at the Christian County PVA with proof of age or disability. Disability claims renew each year, except for owners with a service-connected disability and owners with permanent findings from Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

Thinking of renting the house out or moving? Ask the PVA what that does to the exemption first.

Selling a Christian County house that owes tax

Pull payoff figures before you set a price. The sheriff's tax office can state a current balance, and the clerk can say whether an earlier year was filed as a delinquency. The title company subtracts both at closing and records the release.

Penalties land on fixed dates whether or not you're mid-move. A purchaser willing to take the house without repairs can close on your date and clear the tax from your proceeds, which beats catching up in cash while you pack. Before agreeing to a price, ask any buyer to show how the tax payoff and lien release will appear on the closing statement.

If a tenant is living in the house, tell the buyer and the closing agent early. Rent, deposits and the lease terms all need to be handled in the contract, and the tax split should follow the deed date.

Sellers relocating on military orders sometimes need to close by a set date. Tell the closing agent that date at the start so the payoff letters, lien release and recording are lined up in time. Ask the sheriff and the clerk how long each will take to produce a written balance, because the clerk's legal records division also handles deed copies and releases and can get busy.

Frequently asked questions

What is the county clerk's address in Christian County, Kentucky?

The clerk is at 511 South Main Street, Hopkinsville, KY 42240, phone (270) 887-4105, on weekdays between 8:00 am and 4:00 pm. The legal records division is at (270) 887-4109.

When is the Christian County delinquent tax sale?

Once a year in summer. The county website posts the date and a registration deadline ahead of time, so call (270) 887-4109 for the current schedule.

What happens to a Christian County tax bill after April 15?

The bill moves from the sheriff to the county clerk as a certificate of delinquency, and a lien attaches to the parcel. Interest of 1 percent a month and clerk and attorney fees are then added.

Do I still owe tax if a renter lives in my Christian County house?

Yes. Property tax is the owner's personal debt from the assessment date, no matter who occupies the house.

Can a Christian County owner past 65 reduce the tax?

Yes, through the homestead exemption, which is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026. Apply at the Christian County PVA and show proof of age.
