Does Bell County give seniors a homestead break?

Yes. An owner who has reached 65, or who is totally disabled, can claim it on a residence. Apply at the Bell County PVA, and approval trims the assessed value by a fixed amount.

The figure began at $6,500 in 1972 and has been indexed to inflation since. The Bell County PVA can confirm what your bill uses. A household receives a single exemption, even when both spouses qualify.

  • Approval carries forward as long as the applicant stays in the house.
  • A buyer starts over with a new application.
  • Disabled owners under 65 refile yearly, except owners with a service-connected rating and owners with a permanent finding.

After a death, an heir who sells should notify the PVA so the address loses the exemption.

Population, prices and what they mean for a sale

Bell County lost about 5.3 percent of its people between the 2020 census count of 24,097 and the 2025 estimate of 22,829. That shows in the housing stock. The middle owned home is $89,000 and the middle household income is $31,354, with rent at $592 a month. The 2020 census found 11,517 housing units with 13.8 percent vacant, and only 41 building permits were issued in 2025.

At prices this low, a tax lien plus clerk fees and interest can swallow a big slice of a sale, so check the tax status first.

A short plan for Bell County sellers

  1. Get the bill. If none came, the sheriff can provide a duplicate, and so can a call to the sheriff's office after you sell.
  2. Check the account. Ask the sheriff whether this year's bill is paid and whether earlier years are open. After April 15, the clerk is the office to ask.
  3. Look at the exemption. If you've held a homestead exemption, remember that a buyer starts over with a new application and the PVA needs to know about the sale.
  4. Review the record. The clerk's books are where a title examiner reads the chain of ownership, and since the courthouse lost records to fire and flood, ask early if anything on an old parcel looks incomplete.
  5. Settle the year. A spring closing means the seller owes that year's bill unless the contract shifts it, so decide who pays before signing.

With values near $89,000, every few hundred dollars matters in the final numbers. A seller who knows the exact payoff, the exact exemption status and the exact closing split avoids the surprise deductions that come when these items are sorted out at the last minute.

Selling with unpaid taxes

A seller can pay ahead of closing or have the closing agent pay out of proceeds. Either way, ask the sheriff or clerk for a written payoff, since the total grows month by month after April 15.

After that the clerk holds a delinquency certificate and a lien. Interest grows at 1 percent a month, clerk and attorney commissions of 10 and 20 percent arrive, and a summer sale can pass the certificate to a private investor. KRS 134.015 lets the lien last 11 years even if the house changes hands.

Bell County has three public school districts: Bell County, Middlesboro Independent and Pineville Independent. The sheriff can say which school district and city rate appear on your parcel's bill. Heirs and owners of vacant houses who want to skip repairs and carrying costs may favor a cash sale, which clears liens at closing against a written payoff.

Frequently asked questions

Who takes Bell County tax payments?

The Bell County Sheriff. City of Pineville tax appears on the same bill as county tax, so one payment covers both.

How late can a Bell County appeal be filed?

File with the county clerk by the next business day after the May inspection period ends. A conference with the PVA must come first, and the period opens on the first Monday in May.

What does a typical Bell County house cost?

Half of owned homes are worth more than $89,000. Median household income is $31,354.

What do late Bell County payments cost?

On the usual calendar, 5 percent is added in January and a combined 21 percent applies from February 1 to April 15. After April 15 the clerk adds interest and fees.

Does a lien stop a Bell County sale?

Not by itself. The lien stays with the property until paid, so the payoff is usually taken from the seller's proceeds at closing. Get the figure in writing from the sheriff or clerk first.

Which Clay County offices deal with property tax?

Responsibility in Clay County splits into three. One office, the Property Valuation Administrator, puts a worth on each parcel. The Sheriff prints the bills and collects. The County Clerk accepts appeal papers and eventually receives any bill the sheriff couldn't collect. Knowing which desk owns which question saves a seller several wrong-number calls.

All three share one building, 102 Richmond Road in Manchester. Don't bring a check to the PVA: it sets no tax rate and takes no payments, and its job stops at the number on the roll.

Clay County housing market

Clay County covers 471 square miles of Appalachian hills, with Manchester at the center. The 2020 count was 20,345 people, and the July 2025 estimate of 19,465 is 4.3 percent lower, so a listing draws from a shrinking local pool.

There are 7,288 households living in 8,781 housing units, and owners head 76.4 percent of them. The typical home value is $90,700. Typical rent is $724 a month, and typical monthly owner cost is $978 with a mortgage and $367 without. With prices in that range, unpaid tax takes a noticeable bite out of your net, so learn the balance before you pick an asking price.

How the PVA values a house

Every assessment is anchored to January 1. The standard is fair cash value, the price a willing buyer and seller with full information would agree on. Every parcel gets a staff visit at least once per four years, and new construction is added annually.

A recent purchase can simplify things. Bought last year? Your deed price can become next January's value provided the building is unchanged. Frankfort assesses only public service companies, bank shares, omitted tangible property and vehicles, and the local PVA handles all other real and personal property.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Clay County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Checking your PVA record

Beyond the annual value, the PVA's office follows ownership changes, maintains parcel maps, updates building details and administers exemptions on real estate. Before listing, ask staff three things: does the map show your true acreage, does the building file include a finished basement or a shed that's gone, and does the exemption record still fit the owner.

Errors in those records flow straight into the bill. A garage that came down years ago but still sits on the record keeps lifting the value until someone asks for a correction. Stop in on a weekday between 8:00 and 4:30, or mail the office at 102 Richmond Road, Suite 200, Manchester, KY 40962.

When the bill is due

Collection runs from fall into spring under the sheriff. Parcel lookups sit behind a View Property Tax Bill button on the sheriff's page of the Fiscal Court site. For the exact opening date, ring 606-598-3471, because the state allows 30-day phases when a county needs another calendar.

Under the standard pattern:

  • October 1 to November 1: 2 percent off
  • November 2 to December 31: face amount
  • January: 5 percent added
  • February 1 to April 15: 21 percent added

Because value freezes on January 1, a mid-year sale can leave the old owner's name on the bill.

How to contest a valuation

Follow these steps in order. Skip one and you're out.

  • Watch for the notice the PVA mails after raising a value.
  • Ask the PVA or a deputy for a conference while the roll is open for inspection: two weeks, Monday through Saturday, beginning the first Monday of May.
  • If talks fail, file the appeal paper with the County Clerk by close of business the next workday after the window ends.
  • Attend the local board hearing, held 25 to 35 days after inspection. The board gets five sitting days unless the state grants more.
  • Bring proof: sales of similar houses, an appraisal, or building costs. With no facts, the board has to deny you.

Filing without showing up for the hearing forfeits your right to go further. After the board rules, you can still take the case to the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals.

Homestead exemption

The exemption goes to residents of the home who are 65 or older, or classified as totally disabled. For assessment years 2025 and 2026 the amount is $49,100, taken off the valuation before tax is figured.

The application goes to the PVA in Manchester, 606-598-3832. To prove age, use a driver's license, birth certificate or passport. A disability claim needs paperwork from the federal agency or retirement system that made the classification. Most disability claims renew annually. Exceptions cover owners with a service-connected disability and owners ruled permanently disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

What happens to an unpaid bill

At close of business on April 15 the sheriff passes the bill to the County Clerk, where it turns into a certificate of delinquency and a lien against the parcel. Interest starts at 1 percent a month, with 10 percent more for the clerk and 20 percent for the county attorney.

The county attorney writes to owners in May and, if necessary, June, and can arrange installments. From mid-July, certificates may be sold to outside buyers through late October. After a sale you owe the buyer, and more fees follow. The County Clerk's website posts a delinquent tax page for each year, which is the place to check whether a parcel was advertised for sale.

Online records

The Fiscal Court website, claycountyky.com, has a page for each department with contact details and hours, and the sheriff's page holds the bill lookup. The County Clerk's own site lists Recordings, Fees, Forms and an Open Records Request page.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Handling the tax bill when you sell

Normally the closing agent pays this year's bill from your proceeds and prorates it with the buyer. Any open delinquency comes first, since the lien stays on the land. Request a payoff from the sheriff before you sign, and check with the PVA on whether an exemption ends at transfer.

The deed adds a separate charge. Kentucky taxes the seller $0.50 for every $500 slice of the price, and a partial slice counts in full. The clerk takes it at the recording counter. Foreclosure deeds, divorce transfers, correction deeds and nominal gifts between parent and child fall outside the tax.

Put these on your list in the weeks before closing: the sheriff's payoff, the clerk's total if any bill is delinquent, and the amount of deed tax. Having each number on paper early keeps the closing date from slipping.

Frequently asked questions

Who mails the Clay County tax bill?

The Sheriff. If nothing shows up in your mailbox, phone 606-598-3471 or search the parcel online.

Can a Clay County owner contest a value in summer?

Generally no. Both the conference and the clerk filing must land in the May inspection window, with the filing due the next workday after it ends. Phone the PVA at 606-598-3832 in spring.

Does the Clay County PVA take tax payments?

No. That office only values property and processes exemptions. Money goes to the sheriff, then to the County Clerk after mid-April.

Is transfer tax owed on a Clay County sale?

Typically, and the seller pays it: $0.50 per $500 of price, collected by the clerk at recording. Foreclosure deeds, divorce transfers and correction deeds are exempt.

Can a Clay County house with a delinquent bill still be sold?

Yes. Pay the delinquency at or before closing, and ask the County Clerk for the full total with interest and fees so the payoff is right.

Who to call about Fleming County property tax

Two offices on Court Square carry most of the load, and a third takes over when a bill goes bad. The PVA answers value questions at 606-845-1401 with the office open 8 to 4:30 on weekdays. The sheriff bills and collects at 201 Court Square in Flemingsburg. Phones there are answered at 606-845-4701 (press 1) from 8 until 4:30, Monday to Friday. Once a bill is delinquent, the county clerk handles it.

The PVA appraises property at fair cash value, maintains tax maps and ownership records and processes exemptions. It does not write laws or set rates. Rates come from the fiscal court, city councils, the school board and other districts. The fiscal court meets at the courthouse, 100 Court Square, on the second Tuesday of every month at 9 a.m. Eastern.

Every property gets a visit from the PVA or a deputy at least once every four years, and the outside of a building can be measured with or without the owner present. Send the PVA any new mailing address in writing so notices do not go astray.

Tax year, due dates and penalties

Fleming follows the standard Kentucky calendar, which opens October 1. Statements usually leave the sheriff's office near the end of September. A missing bill changes nothing about the debt, so owners without one should phone 606-845-4701 and ask for the balance, or use the sheriff's online tax record search.

Fleming County Sheriff collection periods and the share of the bill each one asks for
Payment datesShare of the bill due
October 1 to November 198 percent
November 2 to December 31100 percent

The discount ends every November 1. From then through December 31 the plain bill amount is due. Waiting until February raises the cost by a fifth.

  • At the counter, pay with cash, a money order, or a check made out to the Fleming County Sheriff.
  • Card payments, in person or by phone, carry a 2.5 percent service charge.
  • Mailed payments need a postmark dated on or before the due date.
  • A drop box at the sheriff's door stays open at all hours and is emptied at 8 each morning under camera watch.

How to dispute your assessment

Start with the PVA, because the board will not hear anyone who skipped that step. Every May, starting on the first Monday, the roll sits open to inspection for thirteen days. Holding a conference in that period preserves your right to file with the county clerk until the next business day after inspection ends. If inspection runs from May 3 to May 17, for instance, the clerk must have the paper by the close of May 18.

The local board of assessment appeals then sits 25 to 35 days afterward. Bring paper. The board turns down any appeal lacking insurance policies, building costs, sale listings or similar proof.

  • The PVA owes you an explanation of how the value was reached at the conference, and must write down the outcome.
  • A paid representative has to come from a profession on the state's list, among them attorneys, CPAs and certified appraisers, and must bring your signed authorization.
  • Hearings may be audio-recorded by the taxpayer.

The sheriff will redirect any value complaint to the PVA. Filing and then missing the hearing closes the door to the Kentucky Claims Commission.

Homestead exemption

For a qualifying owner it is worth claiming. On the 2025 and 2026 rolls the state takes $49,100 off the home's assessed value, and tax is figured on the remainder. The typical owner-occupied house in the county is valued at $134,700, so the deduction removes a large slice of a typical assessment.

The PVA takes the form. Owners show their age with a birth certificate, license, passport or comparable record. Total disability must be certified by a federal agency or a retirement system, with benefits paid across the entire year, and most such claims have to be re-filed each year. The yearly re-filing does not apply to owners with service-connected military disabilities or those ruled permanently and totally disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

When a lender pays from escrow, the owner is still expected to confirm the payment arrived on time. Check the sheriff's record search after the discount period closes.

Selling with taxes owed

The tax follows ownership, and the sheriff will talk through proration for any buyer or seller who calls with a closing date. Under KRS 134.015 the owner personally owes the tax from the assessment date, and under KRS 134.420 a lien on an unpaid parcel can stay for 11 years after a sale. A sensible order of events: get the balance from the sheriff before listing, then have the closing agent settle the year's bill.

When the sheriff's office closes on April 15, whatever is unpaid goes to the Fleming County Clerk under KRS 134.122. Expect interest of 1 percent monthly, plus commissions and a lien fee, and two letters from the county attorney. The clerk's tax sale follows once 90 to 135 days have gone by.

The deed also carries a state transfer tax, which the seller pays. The seller owes $0.50 for each $500 of price, rounding a partial block up.

If you are listing soon, ask the sheriff whether the current bill has been paid and keep the receipt. A buyer's title company will look for it, and a paid-up record shortens the closing checklist.

Ask the clerk's office in Flemingsburg for a payoff on any transferred bill, and tell the PVA about a new mailing address after closing. At the closing table, the title agent will want the paid receipt for the current year or a payoff letter, so request one from the sheriff ahead of time.

Fleming County housing and the local market

Flemingsburg is the county seat and Ewing is the second city. Population is 15,787, and owners live in 74.8 percent of housing, across 5,859 households. Typical home value is $134,700 and typical monthly rent is $715. No building permits were issued in 2025.

Without new construction, nearly every buyer is shopping among older houses, so condition matters. A seller who owes taxes or faces repairs can weigh the cost of fixing up a listing against an as-is cash offer. Selling for cash skips the appraisal, loan approval and repair requests. Any tax balance comes out of the proceeds at closing. Before listing, make a short folder with the latest tax bill, the sheriff's payoff figure and the deed, so a buyer or title agent can move quickly.

Frequently asked questions

When do Fleming County tax bills arrive?

Bills usually mail late in September, and the 2 percent discount begins October 1. An owner who has no bill by then can call 606-845-4701 and press 1.

How much extra does a late Fleming County payment cost?

January adds 5 percent. Between February 1 and April 15 the total climbs to 121 percent, and whatever is still open afterward is turned over to the county clerk.

Where is the Fleming County Sheriff's tax counter?

Find it at 201 Court Square in Flemingsburg, weekdays 8 to 4:30. The entrance drop box accepts payments at any hour.

Who changes a Fleming County property value?

Only the PVA, at 606-845-1401. The sheriff has no say over assessments, and an appeal must be preceded by a PVA conference.

Who gets the Fleming County homestead exemption?

Owners who live in the home and are 65 or older or totally disabled. The exemption takes $49,100 off the value on the 2025 and 2026 rolls.

Call the Sheriff to find out which payment methods and counter hours apply. The offices sit close together in McKee, so a seller can usually settle the bill, ask a PVA question and drop off a deed in a single trip if the phone calls come first.

Due dates and penalties

No local calendar overrides the state one. The bill is due by December 31 under KRS 134.015, and a 2 percent discount goes to anyone who pays the whole thing by November 1.

Paid by November 1, the bill is 2 percent lighter. Through the rest of December the printed figure is what you owe. In January a 5 percent penalty arrives, and from February onward it is 10 percent.

If bills go out late, Revenue can set a stretched schedule with a month per stage. The Sheriff stops collecting on April 15, and the Clerk holds whatever is left. Didn't get a bill? Phone the Sheriff anyway. A lost bill won't cancel a penalty.

How to dispute your assessment

Begin with the PVA. KRS 133.120 requires a conference first, held before or during the inspection period. Can't get to the office? Ask for a phone call.

Still unhappy afterward? Put your reasons in a written petition, identify the parcel, say what you believe fair cash value is, and deliver or mail it to the County Clerk. Get it to the Clerk by the first workday after inspection wraps up. The bill itself arrives too late to contest, so watch for the inspection notice instead.

The board of assessment appeals then holds a public hearing. Before it meets, pull together whatever proves your number:

  • A description of the land and buildings.
  • Insurance policies and construction costs.
  • Listings, contracts or a recent appraisal.
  • Loan or mortgage papers on the parcel.

Rural parcels are hard to compare, so a recent appraisal or a sale of a similar tract nearby carries more weight than a general complaint. Without evidence, the petition may simply be denied. While the case runs, keep paying tax on the value you claimed.

Homestead exemption

An eligible owner takes $49,100 off the assessed value in 2025 and 2026. With a middle home value of $111,500 in this county, that takes out a big slice of the taxable base.

Two tests apply: it must be your own home, and you must be 65 or older, or totally disabled by a federal or retirement-system standard. Age is proven with a birth certificate, driver's license or passport brought to the PVA. Disabled owners reapply annually, unless the disability is service-connected or Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems has ruled it permanent.

The break belongs to the home where you live now. Once you sell and move, notify the PVA and apply at the new address.

Selling with taxes unpaid

Budget to clear it from the money you receive at the sale. The tax is a personal debt that dates from the assessment date. A lien on the land can last 11 years. On April 15, an open bill becomes a certificate of delinquency at the Clerk.

From there the schedule moves quickly. A County Attorney notice goes out within 30 days of transfer, and a second one within 60 if needed. Under KRS 134.128 the tax sale follows 90 to 135 days after transfer, with the Clerk advertising the list 30 to 45 days beforehand. Commissions and interest accumulate in that window, so call the Jackson County Clerk at (606) 287-7800 for an actual payoff.

Request the figure in writing, ideally before the listing agreement is signed. The title company can then send the Clerk a check from your proceeds. Selling to a cash buyer changes nothing here, since the debt stays with the land until it is paid.

Recording the deed and transfer tax

The County Clerk's McKee office records your deed. That office also issues vehicle and marriage licenses, keeps wills and notary bonds, and collects the state transfer tax before it accepts a deed.

Under KRS 142.050 the seller, as grantor, owes 50 cents on each $500 of value. A few transfers owe nothing, including gifts of nominal value, transfers between divorcing spouses and foreclosures.

Recording fees come from statute and can change, so get today's amount from the Clerk ahead of closing.

Jackson County housing at a glance

Jackson County has 13,325 residents, up 2.8 percent since 2020. About 77.4 percent of homes are owner-occupied. The middle home value is $111,500, median gross rent is $665 and median household income is $40,000. A typical commute runs 37.7 minutes.

Monthly owner costs average $1,101 with a mortgage and $355 without. Most residents stay: 91.9 percent lived at the same address a year earlier. Nearly every sale is of an existing house, and its assessment goes back to the PVA's value on January 1.

McKee is the county seat and Annville is the largest community. Three industrial parks, in Annville, McKee and Sandgap, anchor local jobs.

What to bring to the offices

Pull out your newest tax bill and your deed before listing. If you are contesting a value, add photos, an appraisal or comparable sales. For the homestead exemption, bring proof of age. Mail is slow in a rural county, so call first and ask whether the office wants originals or copies. Ask too whether the Sheriff takes cards or only checks and cash.

At closing, the title company usually makes the recording trip. Confirm with the Clerk that the transfer tax and recording fee will be collected at filing, and keep the receipt for your records.

If you want to sell fast

A quick sale works best when the paperwork is ready. Find out which office holds your bill today: the Sheriff before April 15, the Clerk after. Get a written payoff, check that the deed is in your name, and confirm whether a homestead exemption is on the account. A buyer paying cash can close in days, but the tax payoff and the deed recording still have to happen first.

If you are behind on several years, ask the Clerk whether any certificate has been sold, because a buyer's added charges raise the payoff.

Frequently asked questions

How do I reach the Jackson County PVA?

Send mail to P.O. Box 249, McKee, KY 40447. The phone is (606) 287-7634 and the fax line is (606) 287-7079.

What is the discount for paying early?

The discount is 2 percent, and it requires paying the full bill by November 1 under KRS 134.015. From then until year end you owe the printed amount.

What does a late payment cost?

A 5 percent penalty applies in January, then 10 percent. A bill still open on April 15 goes to the Clerk, where 1 percent monthly interest and commissions begin.

Can a seller keep the homestead exemption after leaving?

No. It covers only your current residence. After closing, tell the PVA and apply again for your new residence.

Is the deed recorded at the McKee courthouse?

Yes. The County Clerk handles it and collects the transfer tax, 50 cents per $500. Call (606) 287-7800 to confirm current fees.

Two offices share one address in Vanceburg. Both sit at 112 Second Street, one in Suite 101 and the other in Suite 102, which makes it easy to settle a question about value and a question about payment in the same trip.

Some bills also carry charges for fire protection or library districts, which the sheriff collects too. The PVA writes no laws and sets no rates. Those belong to the fiscal court, city officials and school boards, and the PVA only assigns value. Under state rules the office walks every parcel at least once each four years, and since 1992 it may measure the outside of a building with no one home.

Lewis County housing at a glance

Lewis County sits in Kentucky's northeast along the Ohio River, with Vanceburg as the seat. Vanceburg and Concord are the only cities. One school district serves the whole county. An estimated 12,901 people lived here in mid-2025, down 1.4 percent from the 2020 count. A typical owned home is worth $96,000, and 79.2 percent of homes are lived in by their owners. Median rent is $751 and median household income is $46,838. The average trip to work takes 38.6 minutes, so buyers often commute out of the county.

How to pay the sheriff

The sheriff takes payment three ways. Mail the stub and a check to 112 Second Street, Suite 102, Vanceburg, KY 41179, pay in person at the office, or pay by debit or credit card over the phone or at the counter. Card payments add a fee tied to the bill's amount. Make checks out to the Lewis County Sheriff's Office, write the property ID from the bill on the check, and never mail cash.

Pay only the single figure in the "If Paid By" box at the bottom right of the bill. The subtotals for each taxing jurisdiction are shown for information, and separate payments for each would only cause confusion. A bounced check draws a $25 charge, and the late-payment tiers keep running while you replace it. If you overpaid, phone the sheriff, who may ask for paperwork before refunding. A single payment can cover several parcels as long as each stub is enclosed.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Lewis County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Due dates and penalties

Statute sets the calendar. The state ladder is simple: a 2 percent reward for settling early in the fall, no adjustment during the last two months of the year, then a 5 percent charge in January and 10 percent beyond that. Your own statement prints the exact dollar figure for each window, so trust it over any summary.

When a bill goes unpaid past April

Mid-April is the handoff. Whatever the sheriff has not collected by then goes to the clerk as a certificate of delinquency, with a lien recorded against the house. After that the debt grows by a percent each month, plus commissions for the clerk and the county attorney.

The state's illustration starts with a $1,000 bill. Clear it within five business days of the handoff and the total is $1,387.79, with the attorney's cut waived. Let the first attorney letter go out and it becomes $1,611.30. Investors can buy these debts at a clerk's sale, which in a usual year lands somewhere between July 14 and August 28.

One exception to the calendar: a bill covering property missing from the roll, or a value that went up on appeal, is payable the day it is drafted, and another 10 percent attaches after a month of silence.

How to appeal your valuation

Ask the PVA's staff for a face-to-face review first. No appeal is accepted without one, and it has to be held ahead of or during the public viewing period.

Viewing runs thirteen days from the opening Monday of May. Having met with the PVA, you can lodge the appeal at the clerk's office until the following workday ends. State law seats the review panel in the county seat, which puts Lewis County hearings in Vanceburg about four to five weeks after viewing wraps up.

  • The board hears only evidence presented with both you and the PVA present, so plan to attend or send an authorized representative.
  • Useful evidence includes photos, insurance policies, construction costs, an appraisal, and nearby listings or sales.
  • Audio recording is your right. The PVA may record only if it gives you written notice.
  • Skipping the board forfeits any later appeal to the Kentucky Claims Commission.

Homestead exemption

The break is for people who live in the house and are either 65 or older or rated totally disabled. The statewide figure for assessment years 2025 and 2026 is $49,100, subtracted from the assessed value before any rate is multiplied.

Applicants go to the PVA at 606-796-2622. A household gets one, even when both spouses qualify, and a manufactured house or a mobile home taxed as real estate can serve as the residence. After a sale the buyer files fresh, and the seller tells the PVA that title has moved.

Taxes when a Lewis County house sells

Sellers typically cover a share at the closing table that matches their months of ownership, and the buyer writes the check for the whole bill when it comes. The closing paperwork shows how your deal split it. A mortgage servicer that pays from escrow still lets the owner see the bill, and the owner stays legally responsible for it.

The bill is sent to whoever owned the property on January 1, unless a deed filed afterward carries specific tax bill instructions for the current year. Recording the deed also triggers Kentucky's transfer levy under KRS 142.050, half a dollar for each $500 of price, which the clerk collects. Foreclosures, divorce settlements and gifts from parent to child are among the exemptions. If a tax bill is delinquent, expect the title agent to require a payoff from the sheriff or the clerk before funds are released.

Before you list

Visit Suite 102 first and ask for the current-year amount and any older year still open. Then ask the clerk whether a certificate of delinquency exists on the parcel. Write down each figure with the date, since monthly interest changes it. At Suite 101, ask the PVA whether your homestead exemption ends at the sale and whether the address and parcel details on file are right.

A cash sale does not change who owes what. The buyer's closing agent still pays back taxes out of your proceeds, and the deed and transfer levy are handled the same way. What a cash sale can skip is the wait for a lender's appraisal and underwriting, so the only delay left is usually a payoff nobody requested early.

Frequently asked questions

Which phone line answers Lewis County tax questions?

Call the sheriff at 606-796-2912 about payment, and the PVA at 606-796-2622 about value or exemptions. Both offices are at 112 Second Street in Vanceburg.

Can I pay my Lewis County tax with a card?

Yes. The sheriff takes debit and credit cards over the phone or at the office and charges a convenience fee based on the bill's size. Checks go to the Lewis County Sheriff's Office with the property ID written on them.

What does a bounced check cost in Lewis County?

The fee is $25, and the late-payment schedule printed on the bill still applies when you send a replacement payment. Pay the amount for the date your funds actually arrive.

Does my mortgage lender handle the Lewis County bill?

Often, but you still receive a copy and remain legally responsible. If you think escrow covers it and you are unsure, ask the lender, and ask the sheriff if the bill is missing.

Who covers the tax when a Lewis County house is sold?

The settlement statement decides, and sellers usually cover a prorated share for the months they owned the house. The buyer pays the full bill when it comes, and unpaid back taxes must be cleared before the title is clean.

That slow decline limits the number of buyers. About 82.8 percent of homes are owner-occupied and median rent is $641. Just two building permits were issued in 2025, which means buyers are nearly always shopping for an existing house.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your McLean County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Homestead exemption

Every Kentucky county has one. A deduction of $49,100 from assessed value covers 2025 and 2026 for anyone who is 65 or older or has been found totally disabled. Roughly 22.5 percent of McLean residents have reached 65, so plenty of households qualify.

Take a driver's license, birth certificate or passport to the PVA when you apply. Disability claims need a government or pension finding and renew every year. Owners with a service-connected disability, and people Social Security or the Kentucky Retirement Systems has ruled permanently and totally disabled, skip the renewal. When the house sells, tell the PVA so the deduction comes off the old address.

How to appeal your assessment

Your first stop is the PVA. The board of assessment appeals listens only to owners who made that visit. After it, the calendar runs like this:

  • The roll is open for 13 days from the first Monday in May. The county's largest newspaper advertises the dates.
  • At the meeting, the PVA explains your number and a form records the conversation.
  • File the appeal with the County Clerk before closing time on the business day after inspection ends.
  • Bring paper: land and building descriptions, insurance records, construction costs, and listings or sales of similar property. Bare claims are rejected.

The board sits about a month later and owes you written reasons for any change. A paid representative must come from the state's list of professions and show your written authority. If you skip the hearing, the Kentucky Claims Commission is off the table.

Selling with taxes owed

A tax lien attaches to the parcel itself, not to the seller. After April 15 the County Clerk carries open bills as certificates of delinquency, records the lien and starts charging 1 percent a month. Under KRS 134.420 the lien lasts 11 years and binds the next owner too.

Charges pile up in layers. The Clerk adds 10 percent and the county attorney adds 20 percent once notices go out, with postage, advertising and lien fees besides. Ask the Sheriff for a payoff figure until April 15 and the Clerk after that. A certificate can be auctioned 90 to 135 days after the transfer, and the buyer may add charges of their own.

Have the payoff in writing before you accept an offer. The closing agent pays it out of the sale money, so it sets what you net.

Selling a home in McLean County

McLean County was formed on February 6, 1854 from parts of Daviess, Ohio and Muhlenberg counties. It covers 256 square miles of the Western Coal Fields inside the Owensboro metropolitan area, and the Green River crosses it from southeast to northwest. Calhoun is the seat and Livermore is the largest community. The county is dry, so alcohol sales are prohibited. One county-wide school district serves the whole county. The Green River has bridges at Calhoun and Livermore, and a Corps of Engineers lock and dam sits at Calhoun, so river frontage and flood questions may come up with buyers. Clocks follow Central time.

Median household income is $65,596 and the average commute is 31.4 minutes, which suggests many workers drive out of the county, with Owensboro the nearest big job market. A cash sale as-is suits an inherited house, a rural parcel or one with tax still owing. Collect the payoff from the Sheriff and the parcel record from the PVA before naming a price.

Steps before closing

Three offices each keep a different record on one parcel, so check with all of them before you pick a closing date. The PVA can confirm the acreage, owner name and any homestead claim. The Sheriff or Clerk, depending on the calendar, gives the payoff. The County Clerk records the deed and any lien.

Have a photo ID and your latest bill handy when you call. A property that came from an estate needs the papers showing who may sign. After closing, let the PVA know the new owner's name so the next bill is mailed correctly and the old exemption ends.

If the house is vacant or needs work, a buyer who pays cash as-is can close without repairs, inspections that depend on lender rules, or a long wait. That can matter when a bill is close to turning delinquent and the penalty steps are counting down. Ask each office what it needs in writing, since a verbal quote is hard to rely on at the closing table.

For an inherited house, find out early who holds the deed and whether any bill from earlier years is still open. Old balances can sit on the parcel for years, and they show up at the payoff request. Sorting this out before listing keeps a sale from stalling after you have signed a contract.

Frequently asked questions

Does the McLean County PVA take payments?

No. Call the PVA at (270) 273-3291 about assessments and exemptions, and pay the Sheriff.

When does a McLean County bill turn delinquent?

The 10 percent penalty starts when January ends. After April 15 the County Clerk gets any open bill, adds a lien and begins monthly interest of 1 percent.

What is the McLean County homestead exemption worth?

It cuts $49,100 from assessed value for 2025 and 2026. People 65 or older, or totally disabled, apply with the PVA in Calhoun.

What rate does the state charge?

The state's 2025 rate is 10.6 cents per $100 of assessed value. Local taxing bodies add their own rates.

Who decides a McLean County assessment appeal?

A local board made up of area property owners. It meets about a month after the roll inspection, and you file through the County Clerk once you have seen the PVA.

Hazard offices for Perry County property tax

Everything a seller needs is in Hazard. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) values parcels on an upper floor of the courthouse at 481 Main Street, and the County Clerk sits on the ground floor. Bills are mailed and collected by the Sheriff's Office on East Main Street.

  • Sheriff's tax office: 124 East Main Street; letters go to box 7309, Hazard 41702. It is open weekdays from 8:00 to 4:00 except holidays. The number is 606-439-4523, option 2.
  • PVA: 606-436-4914. A link to the PVA's parcel search sits on the sheriff's tax page.
  • County Clerk: 606-436-4614.

Checks to the sheriff are made payable to "Perry County Sheriff." A separate billing provider handles online payment and adds its own convenience fee.

Tax calendar and penalties

Perry County runs on the standard Kentucky calendar from KRS 134.015.

Perry County payment calendar
When you payWhat applies
By November 12% discount for paying in full
Through the end of DecemberAmount on the bill
January5% penalty
After January 3110% penalty
Close of business April 15Sheriff's collection year ends

Mailing dates shift from year to year, so call the tax office at 606-439-4523 to confirm the dates printed on your bill. The sheriff collects state, county and district taxes, and earns a commission on the collections. In a year when bills go out late, each stage lasts a full month instead.

Paying the sheriff: your options

You can pay in person at 124 East Main Street on weekdays, 8:00 to 4:00, holidays excepted. For a mailed payment, make the check out to "Perry County Sheriff" and send it to box 7309, Hazard 41702. Online payment goes through a separate billing provider that charges its own convenience fee, so a check or a counter payment costs less. If something about the bill looks wrong, call 606-439-4523 and press option 2 before you pay, and ask the PVA at 606-436-4914 about any question of value.

Save the receipt, because the buyer's title company will want proof of payment or a figure to prorate.

What delinquency costs

Every month of delinquency adds cost. Any bill open after April 15 shifts to the County Clerk, where one percent monthly interest and clerk and attorney commissions begin to accrue. A clerk's sale follows 90 to 135 days after the transfer.

The County Clerk's website points to a delinquent tax application, and the county attorney's office can set up an installment plan on a current delinquency. If you are selling, ask for a payoff in writing, because the balance changes every month the bill stays open.

Can a Perry County owner contest the value?

Yes. Begin at the PVA's office and meet with staff before filing anything. Next, deliver the written appeal to the clerk's desk by the end of the day after the thirteen-day roll inspection closes. A local board of neighbors hears it, generally within five weeks, and it weighs hard evidence such as appraisals, repair bids and nearby sales. Bring photos of any defects the PVA may not know about.

Homestead exemption

A homeowner who is 65 or older, or who is classed as totally disabled, can claim $49,100 off assessed value for 2025 and 2026.

Bring a birth certificate, license or other proof of age when you apply,.

What a seller pays to record a deed

Kentucky's transfer tax falls on the grantor. Under KRS 142.050 it is a half dollar per $500 of the price on the deed, a partial $500 counted as whole, and the clerk takes it before accepting the instrument. The Perry County Clerk's published minimums are $50 for a deed and $80 for a mortgage, and a deed adds $3 for each page after the fifth.

Expect the title company to ask for three things: proof that the current bill is paid or prorated, a payoff from the clerk when an earlier year went delinquent, and an in-care-of address on the deed. Clerk staff will quote a total on any document but will not search titles, so hire an attorney or abstractor for that.

Perry County housing in brief

Perry County is an inexpensive market. A typical owned home is valued at $91,800, owners occupy 70.4% of homes, and the household income midpoint is $42,181.

  • The 2025 estimate of 26,555 people is 6.7% below the 2020 count of 28,473.
  • Median rent is $798. An owner with a mortgage spends $1,167 monthly and one without spends $379.
  • The 2020 census found 13,213 housing units, 13.1% vacant. By 2025 the count was 13,425 units, and no building permits were issued.

With a falling population and many empty units, price carefully and be ready to show the condition of the house.

Setting and taxes for business sellers

About 343 square miles of Appalachian coalfield make up Perry County, whose only incorporated cities are Hazard and Buckhorn. Two school systems, Perry County Schools and Hazard Independent Schools, serve homes here, so know which one covers your address.

Perry County also levies an occupational license tax of 1% on wages and net profit, and people who work inside Hazard pay both the county and the city. If you are selling a rental or commercial building, ask an accountant how that affects you.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Selling with taxes owed, step by step

A delinquent year does not stop a sale. What you need is the exact payoff and a plan to clear it at closing.

  1. Locate the bill: the sheriff holds it until April 15, and the County Clerk holds it after.
  2. Request a written payoff. Interest and commissions change monthly.
  3. For a large debt, the county attorney's office can discuss an installment plan on a current delinquency.
  4. Hand the payoff to the title company for payment out of your proceeds.
  5. Verify that a release was recorded, and file a copy.

A cash purchase means no waiting on a buyer's loan or appraisal. The tax debt gets paid at closing regardless. Handle it early, and the rest of the sale is simpler.

Phone calls to make before you list

Three short calls will save a seller time. Ring the sheriff's tax office at 606-439-4523, option 2, and ask whether the current bill is paid and whether anything older is outstanding. Call the PVA at 606-436-4914 and ask what value and classification are on the roll for your parcel. Then call the clerk at 606-436-4614 and ask whether a certificate of delinquency or any other lien is recorded against the house.

Write down the name of whoever you speak with, the date and the figure you were quoted, and pass those notes to the closing agent. A clear record at all three counters makes the title work simpler.

Frequently asked questions

Where do I pay Perry County property tax in person?

Go to the Sheriff's Office at 124 East Main Street in Hazard, open weekdays 8:00 to 4:00. To pay by mail, use box 7309 and make the check out to Perry County Sheriff.

How much does the homestead exemption take off a Perry County home?

It subtracts $49,100 from assessed value for 2025 and 2026 if you are 65 or older or totally disabled. Get the form from the PVA.

What transfer tax applies to a Perry County sale?

Sellers pay fifty cents per $500 of the deed's stated price, collected by the clerk ahead of recording.

Where do unpaid Perry County bills go after April 15?

The county clerk receives them as certificates of delinquency, and one percent monthly interest starts, plus clerk and attorney fees.

Who decides a Perry County assessment appeal?

A local board made up of area property owners. You meet the PVA first, then file with the clerk no later than the workday after inspection ends.

Trigg County tax offices

Every tax office sits in Cadiz, the county seat. The clerk's real estate line is (270) 522-6661, and the office at 38 Main Street opens weekdays from 8:00 am until 4:00 pm.

  • Sheriff, (270) 522-6014: collects the current year's bills.
  • Property Valuation Administrator (PVA), (270) 522-3271: assigns values, takes exemption applications and holds the meeting that has to precede any appeal.
  • County clerk, (270) 522-6661: handles recording, marriage licenses and delinquent taxes. Vehicle titles and renewals use (270) 522-0217.
  • County attorney, (270) 522-4733: mails the notices that precede a delinquent tax sale.

The clerk's office closes for part of the Trigg County Ham Festival each October, so plan payoff requests around festival week.

Lakes, second homes and the local market

Water shapes everything here. Trigg covers 481 square miles, 40 of them water, on the far southwest edge of Kentucky beside Lake Barkley. Land Between the Lakes National Recreation Area reaches into the county, and Lake Barkley State Resort Park and Prizer Point Marina pull visitors to the shore. Cadiz is known as the Antique Capital of Western Kentucky. Lyon, Caldwell, Christian, Calloway and Marshall counties border it, along with Stewart County, Tennessee.

Population was 14,061 in 2020 and is estimated at 14,512 for July 2025. The county has 7,733 housing units but 6,060 households, and 23.4 percent of units were vacant in 2020. Rentals stood empty at a rate of 11.7 percent. A county built around two large lakes can show that pattern, and it means a seller may compete with seasonal and vacant homes.

Due dates and penalties

The regular due date under state law falls at year end. Early payers by November 1 get a 2 percent discount; the printed amount applies through year end; January payments carry 5 percent; anything later carries 10 percent. If the state delays bills, the Department of Revenue can swap in an alternative schedule: two full months to pay after mailing, discount in month one, printed amount in month two, a 5 percent penalty for a month and 10 percent after.

Bills unpaid when the sheriff's period closes on April 15 go to the clerk as certificates of delinquency.

The delinquent tax sale

The clerk runs one delinquent tax sale a year, at the end of July in the year after the taxes were due. The order of events is the same each year.

  • The list of certificates is published in the Cadiz Record in early June.
  • Buyers register by close of business in early July.
  • The sale takes place at the clerk's office, 38 Main Street, at 9:00 am in late July.

The list is open for viewing at the clerk's office on weekdays and on the clerk's website. Owners can pay at the clerk any time before the sale; money that arrives afterward is returned. Some advertised bills are excluded under KRS 134.504(10)(b). Each year's dates appear on the clerk's delinquent tax page.

If your bill is past due

Pay before April 15 if you can. After that date the file moves from the sheriff to the clerk, and the county attorney starts mailing notices. The second notice names the sale date, and the list is published in the newspaper ahead of it.

You can still pay at the clerk's office up to the day of the sale. An owner who is selling should settle early, because a bill bought by an investor has to be paid to that investor, usually at a higher cost. Ask the clerk whether any older year is open on your parcel, so none of them turns up at closing.

How to challenge an assessment

The PVA's conference comes first, before or during the inspection period, and the roll stays open to view for two weeks in May. An owner who has been through the conference files with the county clerk on the next workday after that window.

The local board then convenes within roughly five weeks and can sit for up to five days. The board expects paper, such as lot and building details, insurance policies, what the house cost to build or comparable listings, and rejects an appeal without it. Separately, the PVA appraises most homes from nearby sales and walks each parcel at least every fourth year. Personal property that is taxable must be listed with the PVA between New Year's Day and May 15, and a later filing is treated as omitted.

Homestead exemption

A resident owner who is 65, or totally disabled, can deduct $49,100 from the assessment for 2025 and 2026, provided the house is owned, lived in and kept up on January 1. Applications go to the Trigg County PVA before December 31. Someone classified as totally disabled by an agency outside Kentucky renews every year. Owners with a service-connected total disability and people found totally and permanently disabled by Social Security file once.

Settling taxes when you sell

Request the current payoff from the sheriff and ask the clerk if a certificate of delinquency exists. Under KRS 134.015 the January 1 owner carries that year's tax as a personal debt, and a delinquency lien can outlast a transfer by up to eleven years. When an investor bought the certificate at the July sale, the payoff goes to that investor.

Gather the figures before you list. Call the sheriff at (270) 522-6014 for the current bill, then the clerk at (270) 522-6661 about any older certificate. Give the written amounts to the closing agent so they come out of your proceeds. A cash buyer can take a lake-area house as it stands, with no staging or repairs, and the tax balance is paid at closing. Compare what you would keep after payoffs rather than the headline offer.

Bring a photo ID and the parcel number to each office, and ask for a written figure with the date it was calculated. Penalties and interest change the amount, so a figure from close to the closing date is the one a title agent will use. If you inherited the house, bring the paperwork showing who has authority to sell it.

Keep copies of every receipt you collect along the way.

Who collects current property tax in Trigg County?

The sheriff, at (270) 522-6014. After the April 15 cutoff the county clerk, (270) 522-6661, takes over unpaid bills.

When does the Trigg County clerk hold its delinquent tax sale?

Once a year, near the end of July. Each year's dates are posted on the clerk's delinquent tax page.

Can I still pay after my Trigg County bill is advertised?

Yes, up to the sale. The clerk's office at 38 Main Street accepts delinquent payments before that date and returns any that arrive afterward.

What is the Trigg County homestead exemption worth?

$49,100 in assessed value for 2025 and 2026. Seniors and totally disabled owners can file with the PVA at (270) 522-3271 before the year ends.

Can I sell a Trigg County house that owes back taxes?

Yes. Closing clears the lien out of your sale money, so collect written payoffs from the sheriff and the clerk beforehand.

Union County tax offices

Tax work stays in Morganfield, where the PVA and the sheriff share the 100 West Main Street address. The PVA is a state office with county jurisdiction, charged with valuing property as of January 1. Rates, the arithmetic and the collecting all belong to others.

  • PVA: PO Box 177, Morganfield, KY 42437. Call (270) 389-1933 between 8:00 and 4:00 on weekdays. Exemption forms go here.
  • Sheriff, the payee: PO Box 30, Morganfield, KY 42437. Phone (270) 389-1303, with the same weekday hours.
  • County Clerk, who records deeds and later holds unpaid bills: (270) 389-1334.

The county government site adds a tax roll search, a tax calculator and a rate page under the PVA menu, handy for checking a parcel before you call.

Union County housing numbers

Union occupies the northwest tip of Kentucky, looking over the Ohio River. Four cities share the county: Morganfield, the seat and largest, plus Sturgis, Uniontown and Waverly. US 60, KY 56 and KY 109 carry the traffic. Union County Public Schools runs schools in the same three towns that have library branches.

The county has been losing people for decades: 13,668 in the 2020 count and an estimate of 12,839 for July 2025.

Housing measureUnion County

With no building permits in 2025, buyers are choosing among existing houses and will price in how well each one has been kept.

The state rate and the homestead deduction

Frankfort's real property rate for 2025 is 10.6 cents on each hundred dollars of assessed value, lower than the 10.9 cents charged in 2024. County, school and other districts bring the full bill well above it.

The $49,100 homestead deduction lowers the taxable base on a qualifying house. About 21.9 percent of residents are 65 or older, and 23.1 percent of those younger than 65 live with a disability, so many households may be eligible. Apply at the PVA on West Main. A disability based claim needs yearly renewal. Owners with service connected disabilities and owners deemed permanently and totally disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems do not have to renew.

Payment calendar

KRS 134.015 sets one schedule for all counties. Union's sheriff takes 2 percent off before November 2, bills the face amount until the year ends, charges 5 percent for January and 10 percent once February arrives, and tacks on a sheriff's fee.

On April 15 the sheriff gives the County Clerk its list of overdue bills and a lien goes on each parcel. The sale of those bills normally falls in September, a year after the tax year, with the date put on the website roughly a month earlier. Anyone who wants to bid registers with the clerk first, and the state also requires registration for a buyer taking more than three certificates in this county, more than five statewide, or putting in more than $10,000.

What a late bill grows into

A late bill grows in steps. A 10 percent penalty, the sheriff's add on and a commission lift it by the time the clerk receives it. Interest of 1 percent a month then runs, and commissions follow the interest. Each notice the attorney sends adds cost, and the figure is higher again once the newspaper notice runs. An investor who buys at the sale then adds charges of their own.

Under KRS 134.420 the lien can last eleven years, and a new owner inherits it along with the land. If you owe back taxes, ask the clerk for a payoff number and let the title company send it at closing.

How to dispute your assessment

Meet with the PVA before filing anything, since the state refuses appeals that skip that conversation. Each May the roll is displayed for thirteen days, beginning with the first Monday. After the meeting, hand the appeal to the clerk before the next day ends once display closes.

Local owners acting as the board of assessment appeals convene 25 to 35 days later, for as many as five days. It denies an appeal that lacks factual support, so collect sale comparisons, repair bids and photos. An owner who neither files nor shows up cannot go further to the Kentucky Claims Commission. Any change comes with a written reason, audio recording is allowed, and a higher final figure means an extra bill.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Union County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Deeds and records at the County Clerk

The clerk's office at 100 West Main Street holds recorded land documents going back to 1811, mostly deeds, mortgages, assignments and releases. A deed is lodged where the land lies and must cite how the seller got title (KRS 382.110). KRS 382.135 adds the parties' mailing addresses, the full price, an in care of address for that year's bill and a sworn price certificate.

The clerk offers e-filing so a title company can send documents without mail or courier. Residents searching for personal reasons can use the online index free, five searches a day, and the same books can be viewed in the office at no cost. Commercial researchers pay $65 a month per county through the records vendor.

Selling with taxes owed or a house that needs work

An owner with a tenant, a probate delay or a house needing work can sell as is for cash instead of waiting for a retail buyer's inspection. Taxes owed do not block that sale. Get the sheriff's figure for the current year and the clerk's figure for anything older, then give both to the closing agent.

Check the clerk's records to confirm the deed matches the name on the sale contract. Ask the PVA whether your exemption is on file. And compare any offer by what you would keep after payoffs, not by price alone. A buyer who pays cash can often close on a date you pick.

Before you meet a buyer, put together a short folder: the latest tax bill, the deed, any exemption paperwork and a payoff letter if there is a mortgage. Bring a photo ID to the courthouse when you ask for written figures, and ask each office to date them. Penalties and interest change the totals, so a figure from close to closing day is the one that counts. If the house came through an estate, add the papers that show who may sign.

Frequently asked questions

Where do I pay a Union County property tax bill?

Bring it to the sheriff at 100 West Main Street, Morganfield, or mail it to PO Box 30. Questions go to (270) 389-1303 during weekday hours, 8:00 to 4:00.

Does the Union County PVA send my bill?

No. The PVA only values property and handles exemptions, and it leaves rates, tax calculation and collection to others. The sheriff handles billing and payment.

When is the Union County delinquent tax sale?

September, in the year after the tax year, is the usual month. The County Clerk posts the exact date on the county website about a month ahead, at (270) 389-1334 for questions.

Can I look up a Union County parcel online?

Yes. The county government site has a tax roll search and a tax calculator under the PVA pages, plus a rate page, so you can see the owner and assessed value.

How much is a house worth in Union County?

The midpoint for 2020 to 2024 is $104,500. Median rent is $790, and owners live in 70.2 percent of homes.

Webster County, KY Property Tax Guide: Offices, Appeals and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Kentucky

What the Webster County PVA decides

Webster County's Property Valuation Administrator, an elected official, assesses all real and personal property in the county at fair market value. The PVA's office does not decide your bill. A bill has two ingredients, the assessed value from the PVA and the rate, which comes from the fiscal court, city governments, the school board, and taxing districts such as the library board and health board.

Some property is valued in Frankfort, among it public service companies and bank shares, and vehicles go in that group too. The PVA may still change a vehicle's value for high mileage or a body shop's estimate.

The PVA's counter is on the courthouse's first floor, 25 US Highway 41-A South, Dixon, KY 42409. Phone 270-639-7016, Monday through Friday, 8 to 4. The Sheriff's Office, 270-639-5067, shares the courthouse address, and its website carries a Property Taxes page for bill details.

When is the Webster County bill due?

The usual statewide timetable of KRS 134.015 applies. If bills were mailed late, the Department of Revenue can run an alternative schedule, so follow the dates printed on your own bill. The Sheriff stays the place to pay until April 15.

Webster County payment stages for a real estate bill
Payment windowAmount owed
Through November 1Printed amount minus 2 percent
November 2 to year endPrinted amount
All of JanuaryPrinted amount, 5 percent added
February 1 to April 15Printed amount, 10 percent added

An open bill passes to the County Clerk the day after the Sheriff's window closes, carrying a recorded lien and extra fees. Dial 270-639-7006 to get a payoff from the Clerk.

How fast does a late Webster County bill grow?

Fast. Once the Clerk's office takes over a delinquent real estate bill, charges pile on in layers. At the handoff from the Sheriff, the bill already includes the 10 percent penalty and the Sheriff's add-on. Pay within five business days and only a modest extra cost applies. After the county attorney sends a first notice, the total jumps again, and interest of 1 percent runs each month. Commissions follow, and a newspaper advertisement in June adds more.

The sale falls between 90 and 135 days after the handoff. The purchaser inherits the lien and may add its own charges, so the amount you owe is highest if a third party buys the certificate. Paying the Sheriff before April 15 avoids every one of these steps.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Webster County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How to contest a Webster County value

Sit down with the PVA or a deputy first. The state will not hear an appeal from an owner who skipped that meeting. You file the written appeal with the County Clerk, no later than closing time on the first workday after inspection ends. The board wants documents: building and land details, insurance, construction costs, comparable listings.

  • Public display of the roll lasts 13 days and starts the first Monday of May.
  • The board convenes roughly a month after display ends.
  • Taxpayers may make their own audio recording of the hearing.

A late-printed bill uses the value you claimed, with a supplemental bill following if the board sets a higher one. Paid agents must qualify under state rules and carry written authority.

Who gets the homestead exemption?

You apply at the PVA, and you must live in the house. Age 65 or older qualifies, as does total disability under a federal or retirement plan. $49,100 comes off the assessed value for both 2025 and 2026. The state's 2025 rate of 10.6 cents per $100 is only the first layer, because county, city, school, and district rates are added.

Disability claims need payments for the entire assessment period and a new application each year, unless the owner has a service-connected disability or holds a permanent total ruling from Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems. After a sale, let the PVA know so the exemption leaves the old parcel.

Can I list a Webster County house with taxes behind?

Yes, though the debt does not vanish at closing. It belongs to the owner from the assessment date (KRS 134.015), and the lien outlives a sale for up to 11 years (KRS 134.420). Get written payoffs before accepting an offer: the Sheriff for this year, the Clerk for earlier ones.

The Clerk's site includes a delinquent tax lookup beside the land records. Should your certificate have been sold at the sale, the payoff goes to the buyer and includes that buyer's fees, so ask who holds it.

In a typical contract, the current year's bill is split in proportion to the days each party owns the house. Make sure the split is written down and appears on the closing statement.

A cash buyer will often accept a house with open taxes as-is, paying off the lien from your proceeds at closing. That path suits an inherited home, a house needing repairs, or one where a bill has already reached the Clerk, since it saves you from paying out of pocket before you sell.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Webster County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Steps to take before you list

Your first call goes to the PVA, 270-639-7016: find out the assessed figure and whether a homestead exemption is attached. Then stop at the Sheriff's Office, 270-639-5067, for this year's balance and confirm whether the bill is paid. If any earlier year went unpaid, the Clerk at 270-639-7006 can give you a payoff.

Write each figure down along with the date you were quoted. Hand the list to your closing agent so the settlement statement matches. If you plan to challenge a value, remember the appeal window is short: it opens the first Monday in May and ends the workday after the 13-day display. Miss it and the number stands for the year.

The buyer's title search will reveal any old delinquency. It is far easier to clear it before an offer than to renegotiate in the middle of a contract.

Webster County market snapshot

Webster County has 12,929 residents as of 2025, a 0.7 percent drop from 2020. Dixon holds the courthouse, and Providence is the largest of six cities that also include Clay, Sebree, Slaughters, and Wheatcroft. The county runs on Central time.

There are 5,772 housing units and 4,923 households. Owner-occupied homes make up 73.8 percent of the stock, valued at a median $112,900. Owners with a mortgage pay a median $1,241 a month, owners without one pay $405, and renters pay a median $783. Only five building permits were issued in 2025, so houses change hands mostly as resales. Providence and Sebree voted to allow alcohol sales in 2018, and Clay followed in 2022. The county sits in the Western Coal Field, and houses here are generally modest, so carrying costs and a clean tax record matter to buyers.

Frequently asked questions

What are the Webster County PVA's address and hours?

On the courthouse's first floor, 25 US Highway 41-A South in Dixon. Call 270-639-7016 on weekdays between 8 a.m. and 4 p.m.

Does the Webster County PVA decide my tax rate?

No. The fiscal court, city governments, school board, and districts such as the library and health boards set rates. The PVA only determines assessed value.

By when must a Webster County appeal reach the County Clerk?

Before closing time on the workday after the 13-day roll inspection ends, and only once you have met with the PVA.

How much does the exemption lower a Webster County assessment?

It removes $49,100 from the assessed value of your own home in 2025 and 2026, if you are 65 or older or totally disabled. The PVA handles the application.

Why does a Webster County bill cost more at the Clerk?

A 10 percent penalty and Sheriff's add-on are included at the handoff, then 1 percent monthly interest and commissions follow. The county attorney's notice adds more.

Three Wickliffe offices handle every bill

Barlow, Kevil, La Center and Wickliffe are the four cities, and Bandana and Lovelaceville are unincorporated communities. None has its own tax office. Every Ballard County parcel is billed and managed from the courthouse area in Wickliffe.

  • Sheriff, 437 Ohio Street, Wickliffe: bills and payments, (270) 335-3561 or (270) 335-5153.
  • Property Valuation Administrator, 132 North 4th Street, Wickliffe: assessments and exemptions, (270) 335-3400.
  • County Clerk, 132 North 4th Street, Wickliffe: appeals and, later, unpaid bills, (270) 335-5168.

Wickliffe has been the county seat since 1882. A courthouse fire on February 17, 1880 burned most early records, so a buyer or heir tracing an old parcel should ask the County Clerk which books survive from before 1880.

When a Ballard County bill becomes late

KRS 134.015 supplies one schedule for every Kentucky county, and Ballard follows it unless the state allows a delay. Pay in full by November 1 and 2 percent comes off the bill. From then through December 31 you pay the printed figure. January adds 5 percent. After January the penalty is 10 percent.

A bill unpaid at the end of the day on April 15 is passed to the County Clerk, who records a lien against the parcel. From that point interest builds at 1 percent for each month, and clerk and county attorney fees are added. Under a delayed schedule each stage lasts a month, so confirm the dates with the sheriff's office.

The tax calendar for a Ballard County parcel

Property tax year at a glance
Month or windowWhat occurs
January 1Value date for real estate
January 1 to March 1Real property listing window
First Monday in May, 13 daysPublic inspection of the tax roll
Day after inspection endsLast day to file an appeal with the clerk
25 to 35 days laterLocal board hears appeals for up to five days
December 31Bills due without penalty

You needn't list the property again when last year's roll described it fully and correctly and nothing major changed. A buyer's deed price can serve as the listed value for the next January 1.

Paying your bill, step by step

Start with the Sheriff's office on Ohio Street. Ask for the current-year bill and for any balance from earlier years in the same call, because older arrears are the item that surprises sellers. If you are going to pay before November 1, confirm that the full amount must be in the sheriff's hands by that date, not just mailed.

Escrow customers should check with the mortgage servicer before paying a second time. If the servicer paid, the sheriff's record will show it. If you own the house outright, the bill is yours to pay, and 2 percent off for early payment is the best price you will see all year.

Missed December 31? Pay as soon as you can. January adds 5 percent and each later stage costs more, so a few weeks of delay does real damage. Past April 15 the County Clerk takes over, and the number you need comes from that office.

How to appeal your assessment

An appeal opens with a conference at the PVA's office on North 4th Street. The clerk can't take a filing otherwise. After that you have until the workday following the end of roll inspection to file with the County Clerk. Write your own opinion of value on the form, because the bill relies on it if one is printed before a decision.

  • Evidence to bring: descriptions of the land and structures, insurance policies, construction costs, nearby sales listings.
  • Anyone paid to speak for you needs recognized credentials and your written authority.
  • You may audio-record the hearing.
  • A higher value set by the board produces a supplemental bill for the difference.

Keep copies of everything you hand in. If the board's value comes back higher than yours, you'll want your own paperwork to show how you got your figure, and the hearing is audio-recorded in case anyone needs to check what was said.

An owner who never files with the local board, or files and then skips the hearing, cannot take the case to a later stage.

Homestead exemption

Owners 65 and over, or classified as totally disabled, claim Kentucky's homestead exemption through the Ballard County PVA. For 2025 and 2026 it subtracts $49,100 from the assessed value, and the amount is revisited every other year. The state runs it, not the county.

An owner who never applied might be paying tax on value the state would exempt. A call to the PVA at (270) 335-3400 settles it. Residents who are 65 or older make up a sizable share of the county, so many households could qualify.

Ballard County housing and population

The county sits at the far western tip of Kentucky, where the Ohio River meets the Mississippi, and the population is slowly shrinking. The 2020 count was 7,728, and the 2025 estimate is lower at 7,594. Households numbered 3,228 in 2020 and 3,209 in 2025.

The middle owner-occupied home is valued at $145,800, and owners live in 76.0 percent of occupied homes. Middle gross rent is $817 and middle household income is $66,164. The county has 3,730 housing units. With a small buyer pool, a seller whose tax account is paid up and whose deed is in order has an easier time getting to a closing. Vacancy was 12.4 percent of units at the 2020 count, so buyers have choices, and a house with open tax questions will be passed over for one without.

What to settle before the closing date

Three phone calls cover most of it. Call the Sheriff for what is owed now and in prior years. Call the County Clerk to ask whether any lien is recorded against the parcel. Call the PVA to confirm that the exemption on file, if any, is correct and that it ends properly with the sale.

If the house was in a parent's name and the paperwork never changed, sort that out first, because the County Clerk records everything and a title company will want a clean chain. Tell the clerk's office if the oldest record you need predates the 1880 fire.

Selling a Ballard County house when taxes are owed

Kentucky treats the tax as the owner's personal debt from the assessment date, and a delinquency lien, once recorded, can stay on the land for as long as eleven years whoever owns it. A closing agent therefore tends to pay the year's bill from the seller's proceeds. Ask how that year is divided with the buyer.

  • Sheriff: what is owed this year and in past years.
  • Clerk: whether a lien is on record.
  • Deed: add the next bill's mailing address, which KRS 382.135 requires.

Owners who inherited a river-county house or moved away and now owe back taxes can request a written cash offer. Any lien balance is paid out of the price.

Frequently asked questions

Who do I pay in Ballard County?

Payments go to the Sheriff at 437 Ohio Street, Wickliffe. The numbers are (270) 335-3561 and (270) 335-5153.

How much do I save by paying early?

Two percent of the bill, provided the sheriff has the full amount by November 1 (KRS 134.015). After that date the printed amount stands through December 31.

What if December 31 passes?

The bill picks up 5 percent in January and 10 percent afterward. Once April 15 passes, the County Clerk holds it and interest of 1 percent a month runs.

Where is an assessment appeal filed?

File with the County Clerk, 132 North 4th Street, after your PVA conference. Filing closes the workday after inspection ends.

Is the homestead exemption a county program?

No, the state runs it. The Ballard County PVA, (270) 335-3400, takes applications from owners 65 or older or totally disabled, and the 2025 and 2026 amount is $49,100.
