When a bill goes unpaid

On April 15 the sheriff passes the bill to the clerk and a lien goes on record. Interest starts at 1 percent each month, with a 10 percent clerk charge and a 20 percent county attorney charge on top. The clerk may sell the certificate to an outside investor from mid-July onward.

The county attorney can set up installments before a sale. After a sale you answer to the investor, who may add large fees. The January 1 owner owes the tax personally, and the lien can ride with the parcel for 11 years.

Cabins and short-term rentals

A 4 percent transient tax applies to short-term rentals, and the county's Departments page links the registration form and the monthly return. With Cave Run Lake and the Red River Gorge nearby, plenty of cabins fit that description.

A buyer who plans to rent will want those filings in order. If you hosted guests, gather your returns and tell the buyer what you filed. The county tourism office can explain how a new owner registers.

Selling a Menifee County house with tax owing

It can be done. An open bill, or one already at the clerk, becomes a payoff number that the sheriff or clerk will quote. Once the bill is at the clerk the number climbs monthly, so ask for a fresh quote close to closing.

Homes here are often inherited, remote or in need of work. To compare a listing with a cash offer, subtract repairs, carrying costs and back tax from each. Get the payoff in writing before you accept anything. Lenders may ask about storm repairs on an older house, so keep permits and receipts together. Household income in the county is $45,096 at the middle, which affects what local buyers can pay, so price with that in mind.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What to bring and who to ask

For a sale, collect your deed, the latest bill and any exemption approval. Ask the PVA to confirm the parcel details, the sheriff for the current balance, and the clerk whether any lien is recorded. If the house passed to you by inheritance, have the papers that show who may sign. Once the sale closes, tell the PVA about the change in ownership so the exemption is removed from the old owner and the new bill goes out correctly.

Expect hillside parcels and small tracts to raise questions about boundaries and access. A recent survey, or at least a clear description in the deed, helps a buyer and a title company agree on what is being sold. Cabins near the lake or the gorge may also draw buyers who want rental income, so have your transient tax filings ready if the house was ever rented to guests. Cash buyers can often close without repairs, which helps when a roof or foundation would otherwise hold up a lender-financed sale.

Frequently asked questions

Who do I pay for Menifee County property tax?

Pay the Menifee County Sheriff at P.O. Box 142, Frenchburg, KY 40322, phone (606) 768-3875. Write the bill number on a mailed payment.

Which date ends the penalty-free window in Menifee County?

December 31. A bill paid by then costs its printed amount, and January adds 5 percent.

Where is an assessment appeal filed in Menifee County?

At the county clerk's office, after a conference with the PVA. The filing is due one workday after the May inspection period ends.

Does Menifee County give older owners a tax break?

Yes, through the Kentucky homestead exemption for owners 65 or older who live in the house. Apply at the PVA, 12 Main Street in Frenchburg.

Can the county take a house over a small unpaid bill?

After April 15 a lien is recorded, and collection may include selling the certificate to a private buyer. Speak with the county attorney early about installments.

Who does what on a Mercer County tax bill

Three offices on West Lexington Street in Harrodsburg handle Mercer County tax. The PVA appraises each parcel, the sheriff takes the payment, and the county clerk files liens and picks up any bill still open after April 15.

The sheriff's office collects more than $8,000,000 a year, so tax is a big share of its workload. Houses inside Harrodsburg also get a city bill, explained below.

Where to pay, appraise or record

  • Sheriff: bills and payments, at 207 W. Lexington St., with a mailing box at P.O. Box 126, Harrodsburg, KY 40330. Phone (859) 734-4221. Doors are open 8:00 to 4:30 on weekdays, and a box at the entrance takes payments left after hours.
  • PVA: appraisals and exemption forms. Same street address, P.O. Box 244, phone (859) 734-6330, same weekday schedule.
  • County Clerk: deeds, liens and delinquent bills. Courthouse address, P.O. Box 426, phone (859) 734-6310.

The PVA website has a public property search with limited detail, and a paid subscription opens the full database.

Why Harrodsburg homeowners get two tax bills

A house inside Harrodsburg pays two governments. The city sends its own bill, mailed at the end of September. The county sheriff bundles the county, state, library, extension, soil conservation, health and school taxes into a separate one.

Due dates and penalties

The sheriff follows KRS 134.015, with the county's own wording for the later penalty.

  • October 1 to November 1: 2 percent comes off.
  • November 2 to December 31: pay what is printed.
  • January: a 5 percent penalty.
  • After that: a 10 percent penalty, plus a further 10 percent sheriff fee on payments made between February 1 and April 15.

Whatever is still open moves to the county clerk when business closes on April 15. Anyone who gets no bill should phone the sheriff's office. Bills arrive on a white postcard with a yellow strip, which is easy to mistake for junk mail.

Mercer County housing and the market

Mercer sits in the Bluegrass of central Kentucky on roughly 249 square miles of land. Harrodsburg is the seat, Burgin is the second city, and Salvisa is a census-designated place. Visitors come for Old Fort Harrod State Park, the Shaker Village of Pleasant Hill and Herrington Lake.

The 2020 count was 22,641 people, up from 21,331 in 2010, and the mid-2025 estimate is 23,733. There are 10,824 housing units, and owners live in 75.9 percent of them. A typical owner-occupied home is worth $202,300 and typical rent is $831. Owners with a mortgage spend a median $1,373 a month on housing, against $497 for owners with none. With 132 building permits in 2025, some buyers will compare an older house with a new build.

How to dispute a Mercer County value

Ask for a PVA conference during the inspection window, a 13 day stretch that starts the first Monday of May. A conference that ends in disagreement leads to a filing at the county clerk's office, where you state your own figure.

A three person board takes up appeals about a month after the window ends and opens by examining recent sales of similar homes. If you hire someone to speak for you, KRS 133.120 limits the choice to lawyers, CPAs, brokers or appraisers and similar professionals, plus your own employees, and that person needs your written authorization.

Mercer County mixes town lots, farms and acreage on one roll, so choose sales of homes like yours. A farm house on acreage and a town lot do not compare well.

Homestead exemption

Age 65 or older, or a total disability classification, opens the door, and the exemption covers your own residence. If you haven't signed up, call the PVA at (859) 734-6330.

KRS 132.810 allows one exemption for each residential unit and treats a mobile home as a unit. Your assessment can't go up because of the value you write on the application. Someone who qualifies after paying is owed a refund on the exempt portion. Disabled owners under 65 reapply yearly, except those with a service-connected total disability and people found permanently disabled under Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems rules.

When Mercer County tax goes unpaid

After April 15 the clerk issues a certificate of delinquency and a lien attaches. Interest builds at 1 percent monthly, and the clerk (10 percent) and county attorney (20 percent) add their fees. The balance grows noticeably by the time of the attorney's first notice.

Outside buyers may purchase certificates beginning in mid-July. After a sale you pay that buyer, and added fees are possible. Before a sale, payment plans run through the county attorney.

The January 1 rule and your sale

January 1 fixes tax ownership. A buyer who closes later in the year still sees the bill issued to the former owner until the next calendar year, though the PVA's office tries to send the new owner a copy based on the recorded deed.

That shapes every closing. A buyer without a bill can ask the sheriff for one, and the contract should name who covers the year's tax. For an older bill at the clerk, ask for a payoff figure before picking a closing date. Cash buyers can often close quickly, which helps when a bill is already at the clerk and the interest is running.

Before you list, collect your deed, your latest bill and any exemption approval, and call the PVA to confirm the parcel details. A farm house on acreage may need a survey to settle what is being sold, while a town lot inside Harrodsburg also needs the city bill paid.

At closing, the title company will usually ask the sheriff and the clerk for figures, and the city for its own bill if the house is in Harrodsburg. Give them time, because the sheriff's office is open on weekdays only and the clerk keeps its own schedule. If the house changes hands after the bills go out in the fall, decide in the contract who reimburses whom for the part of the year each side owned it. Keep your receipts, since they prove the bill was paid and shorten any later questions. If you can't find a bill at all, phone the sheriff and ask for a duplicate before the discount window closes.

Frequently asked questions

Where is a Mercer County tax bill paid?

At the sheriff's office, 207 W. Lexington St. in Harrodsburg, or by mail to P.O. Box 126. Payments can also go in the box at the entrance after closing time.

Does the sheriff also collect Harrodsburg city tax?

No. City Hall bills its own levy, and the sheriff's bill covers county, state and school taxes plus the library, extension, soil and health districts.

When does the early payment discount end?

The 2 percent discount ends November 1. After that, the printed amount is due through December 31.

Is there a refund if I qualify for the homestead exemption after paying?

Yes. KRS 132.810 entitles a person who qualifies after paying to a refund on the exempt portion.

Whose name is on the bill if I closed after January 1?

The prior owner's, until the next calendar year. A new owner can call the sheriff at (859) 734-4221 for a copy.

Trimble County tax offices

Everything happens in Bedford, and all three offices have Highway 42 East addresses. The PVA values each parcel at fair cash value under KRS 132.450 and keeps the roll that every taxing district bills from.

Trimble County tax offices in Bedford
OfficeAddressPhoneHours
PVA, values property107 Hwy 42 E, PO Box 131(502) 255-35928:30 to 4:30, shut 12:00 to 12:30
Sheriff, takes payment30 Hwy 42 E(502) 255-71388:00 to 4:30
County Clerk, deeds and late bills30 Hwy 42 E, PO Box 262(502) 255-71748:30 to 4:30

All three keep weekday hours only. The sheriff's office also handles patrols, vehicle inspections and court security, so ring ahead when you need a payoff letter for a closing date.

Trimble County for a seller

Trimble is one of the smallest Kentucky counties by land, about 152 square miles, with the Ohio River as its western boundary facing Indiana. Bedford, the seat, sits at the junction of US 421 and US 42. Milton, at US 421 and KY 36 facing Madison, Indiana, is the oldest and largest town. Smaller places include Wises Landing, Providence, Monitor and Mount Pleasant. The Trimble County Generating Station, on 2,200 acres beside the river about 50 miles from Louisville, is the best known industrial site.

The population grew 33.4 percent in the 1990s to 8,125, peaked at 8,809 in 2010 and slipped to 8,474 by the 2020 count. It is now estimated at 8,701, which is 2.7 percent above the April 2020 base. Housing looks like this:

  • Homes lived in by their owners: 79.7 percent, with 3,931 housing units in all.
  • Typical home value: $172,000. Typical rent: $863 a month.
  • Monthly owner costs: $1,286 with a mortgage and $420 without one.
  • Households: 3,382 at 2.52 people each, with 93.6 percent of residents in the same house a year before.

Most owners stay put for years, so listings tend to come from long-time residents, heirs or landlords.

The state share of your bill

For 2025 the Commonwealth's rate is 10.6 cents per hundred dollars of assessed value, down a notch from 10.9 cents. County, school and district levies sit on top of that figure, and the sheriff can quote the combined rate for any parcel.

A homeowner with the $49,100 age or disability exemption is billed on the assessed value minus that amount, which lowers every levy applied to it. A 2 percent prompt payment discount trims the whole bill, not just the state's slice.

Due dates and penalties

One calendar governs the sheriff, written into KRS 134.015.

  • Through November 1: the bill is cut by 2 percent.
  • November 2 to December 31: the printed amount.
  • January: 5 percent is added.
  • February onward: 10 percent is added, along with the sheriff's own fee.

When April 15 closes, whatever is still open moves from the sheriff to the clerk. The clerk records a lien on the parcel, interest of one percent a month begins, and the clerk and county attorney earn commissions. Paying quickly after the handoff avoids part of the cost.

Two attorney letters follow, the second naming the sale date, and an advertisement runs a month or more before. No sale can be held until 90 days after the handoff. A lien can survive 11 years and follows the land, so a title agent will not close over it. Get the Trimble County Clerk's exact payoff and let closing funds cover it.

How to dispute your assessment

Start by phoning the PVA, because a meeting with that office is the gate to any appeal. Each year the roll is on public view for thirteen days, starting the first Monday of May. Anyone still unhappy then files at the clerk's office, no later than the day after viewing ends.

Local owners sit as the panel, 25 to 35 days after viewing. Only proof shown in front of the PVA or a deputy counts, so bring photos, repair estimates, insurance papers and nearby sales. The panel writes down any change it makes, and the hearing may be recorded. When the final figure ends up higher than the one you claimed, a supplemental bill covers the gap.

Homestead exemption

Owners who have reached 65 qualify, as do owners whom a federal agency or retirement system has classed as totally disabled. The deduction is $49,100 across 2025 and 2026. Hand the form to the PVA at 107 Hwy 42 E along with proof of age.

Anyone claiming on disability must reapply each year. The exceptions are owners whose disability came from military service and owners that Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems has ruled permanently and totally disabled. About 21.4 percent of Trimble residents are 65 or older, so a good share of owners may be able to use it.

Paperwork to line up before closing

Tax status and the deed are the two gating items. The clerk's office on Highway 42 records the deed. Kentucky wants mailing addresses for both parties, the full price, an in care of address for that year's tax bill and a sworn certificate that the price is true. It must also cite how the seller took title.

  • Get what is owed in writing from the sheriff.
  • Ask the clerk whether any delinquent bill has been recorded against the parcel.
  • Tell the PVA about the sale if an exemption was on file.
  • Write the buyer's own mailing address into the deed for next year's bill.

Back taxes, a vacant inherited house or a tenant in poor repair do not have to be fixed before selling. A cash buyer will take the house as is and pay the balance from the proceeds.

Selling with back taxes

The usual order is simple. Call the sheriff at (502) 255-7138 for this year's balance, then the clerk at (502) 255-7174 for anything that has been recorded as delinquent. Put both numbers in front of the closing agent. If the lien is older, expect it to be paid from your proceeds before you receive anything.

An owner who wants to skip showings and repairs can compare a cash offer against a listing by the amount left after payoffs, not by the price alone. Ask any buyer who will pay recording costs and how soon they can close.

Bring a photo ID and the parcel number to each office, and ask for each figure in writing with the date it was calculated. Interest runs monthly on a delinquent bill, so a number from close to closing day is the one a title agent will use. If you inherited the house, bring papers showing who has authority to sign the deed. Doing this a couple of weeks ahead leaves room for a second visit if an office needs something more.

Frequently asked questions

Which Trimble County office takes my tax payment?

The sheriff's office does, at 30 Hwy 42 E in Bedford, phone (502) 255-7138. The PVA down the road at number 107 only values property, and the clerk handles bills after they turn delinquent.

What are the hours at the Trimble County PVA?

Weekdays from 8:30 to 4:30, except a lunch closing from 12:00 to 12:30. The phone number is (502) 255-3592.

Is Bedford the largest town in Trimble County?

No, Milton is the largest town, while Bedford is the county seat. Milton stands on the Ohio River at US 421 and KY 36, across from Madison, Indiana.

How much is a typical Trimble County home worth?

The middle value for 2020 to 2024 is $172,000. Median rent is $863 a month, and owners live in 79.7 percent of homes.

Does a delinquent Trimble County tax bill disappear if I sell?

No. The lien rides with the parcel for as long as 11 years, so someone has to pay it by closing day. The County Clerk's office can give you the figure.
